title: Senior Radiochemist
description:
ABOUT US

Transmutex is a Swiss company founded in 2019. Transmutex is currently advancing the HI-BEAM (High Intensity Breakthrough Engineering for Advanced Medicine) project, an ambitious programme to develop an industrial-scale facility for the reliable production of medical-grade Actinium-225 (Ac-225), a critical radionuclide for emerging targeted alpha therapies. 

Our team spans nuclear physics, engineering, software, radiochemistry, pharmaceutical and industrial development. Working with research labs and industrial partners worldwide, we are building the production capacity needed for the next generation of cancer treatments.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As the HI-BEAM project progresses from conceptual design into experimental validation, Transmutex is expanding its radiochemistry capability to translate established laboratory methods—supported by collaboration with leading international research institutes—into automated, reproducible, and commercially viable production processes.

We are seeking a Senior radiochemist to actively contribute to the technical design of Transmutex’ s radiochemistry process, in strong collaboration with renowned research labs. You will report to the Head of Extraction unit and be part of a small international team

You will primarily be based in Vernier, GE, with regular travel to Villigen, AG and to partner research labs in North America.

MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES

Process development:

  • Design and optimize radiochemical separation and purification.
  • Collaborate across teams to develop radiochemical processes and methodology.
  • Perform radiochemical and chemical analyses, including alpha and gamma spectrometry.
  • Track radiochemistry developments and adopt relevant innovations and best practices.

Industrialization and operations:

  • Develop the radiochemical process flowsheet, including unit operations, process parameters, material balances, cycle times and waste streams.
  • cale up and transfer laboratory processes to a robust and GMP-compliant production line.
  • Define process, equipment, utility, instrumentation and facility-interface requirements.
  • Support equipment selection, sizing, qualification, commissioning and process validation.
  • Develop operating procedures, batch records, control strategies and consumables requirements.
  • Prepare laboratory and production operations aligned with capacity and customer needs.
  • Train and mentor colleagues.

Compliance, quality, and safety:

  • Work with QA and Safety to ensure regulatory compliance and meet applicable standards
  • Implement and monitor safety protocols and regulatory requirements.

QUALIFICATIONS AND PROFESSIONAL ACHIEVEMENTS

The candidates we are looking for must have:

  • PhD or Master’s degree in Radiochemistry, Nuclear Chemistry or related field
  • A minimum of 10 years of experience in radiochemistry.
  • Proven experience in radiochemical separation and purification with strong knowledge of actinide chemistry.
  • In-depth understanding of radiochemistry processes, equipment and tools.
  • Mastery of characterization, alpha or gamma spectrometry, ICP-MS, ICP-OES, liquid scintillation counting, or comparable analytical techniques.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of safety, radioprotection and GMP regulations and requirements. 
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with ability to collaborate effectively with multiple internal and external stakeholders across disciplines. 
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities to address complex technical challenges.
  • Proven experience in translating lab-scale processes to GMP production line would be an asset
  • Fluent in English. Excellent knowledge of French or German would be an asset

TERMS AND CONDITIONS

  • Start date:          early 2027, and no later than April 2027

  • Contract:            Full-time, permanent employment contract
  • Package:             We offer competitive remuneration and social security, accident/disability insurance and pension plans; one day per week work from home, as well as five weeks’ paid vacation.

RECRUITMENT PROCESS:

One to two technical interviews with the hiring manager, HR and other Transmutex team members; interview with Management for shortlisted candidates. At least one interview will be organized on-site in Geneva.

Je ondersteunt bij de dagelijkse HR-processen, krijgt verantwoordelijkheid die past bij jouw ontwikkeling en werkt nauw samen met de HR-adviseur en HR-manager.

Wie ben jij

Je volgt een hbo-opleiding in de richting van Human Resource Management en zoekt een meewerkstage waarin je veel praktijkervaring kunt opdoen.

Daarnaast:

  • werk je nauwkeurig en zorgvuldig;

  • ga je goed om met vertrouwelijke informatie;

  • vind je het leuk om contact te hebben met medewerkers en sollicitanten;

  • ben je nieuwsgierig en leergierig;

  • neem je initiatief en durf je vragen te stellen.

Wat ga je doen

Je ondersteunt bij de administratieve HR-processen rondom instroom, doorstroom en uitstroom. Denk aan het verwerken van personeelswijzigingen, het opstellen van arbeidsovereenkomsten, brieven en werkgeversverklaringen.

Ook werk je mee aan onze werving en selectie. Je beheert sollicitaties, houdt overzicht op lopende vacatures en ondersteunt in de communicatie met kandidaten en collega's.

Daarnaast krijg je de mogelijkheid om:

  • een onboarding voor te bereiden en zelf te verzorgen;

  • mee te kijken met het verzuimproces;

  • deel te nemen aan het wekelijkse HR-werkoverleg;

  • aan te sluiten bij het overleg over de optimalisatie van HR-processen in AFAS;

  • mee te denken over vragen van medewerkers en leidinggevenden.

Ook is er ruimte voor een eigen verbeterproject. Het onderwerp bepalen we samen, zodat het past bij jouw interesse én bij een actueel HR-vraagstuk binnen onze organisatie.

Wat bieden wij

Je krijgt een veelzijdige stage waarin je diverse kanten van HR leert kennen. Omdat ons HR-team klein is, krijg je veel mee van wat er speelt en is er ruimte om steeds meer zelfstandig op te pakken.

Wij bieden je:

  • begeleiding door ervaren HR-collega's;

  • ervaring met verschillende HR-processen en AFAS;

  • ruimte voor een eigen verbeterproject;

  • een werkplek op ons hoofdkantoor in Heerhugowaard;

  • een stagevergoeding van € 450,- bruto per maand.

Wie wij zijn

Het mooie van Univé? Dat zijn de mensen, de resultaten, de geschiedenis, de cultuur, het ontstaan, de betrokkenheid. Dat is samenwerken. Een coöperatie zijn zonder winstoogmerk. Supporter van Sport zijn. Een 9 voor klantvriendelijkheid krijgen en een Great Place to Work zijn. Wij richten ons op het voorkomen van risico’s, het beperken van gevolgen en we verzekeren alleen als het echt nodig is. Coöperatie Univé bestaat uit diverse onderdelen, waaronder Univé Schade, Univé Rechtshulp, verschillende ondersteunende afdelingen en acht verschillende Regionale Univé’s, zodat we op landelijk én lokaal niveau altijd dichtbij onze klanten zijn. Bij Univé ontwikkelen we samen continu nieuwe producten, diensten én onszelf. Alles voor onze klanten. Dat is het mooie van Univé. Kom jij ons versterken?

Univé Noord-Holland is één van de acht Regionale Univé’s. Ons werkgebied strekt zich uit van Den Helder tot het noordelijke deel van het Groene Hart én Zwolle. Onze klanten kunnen bij ons terecht voor verzekeringen, hypotheken en andere diensten die zekerheid bieden. Voor elke klant is er altijd iemand van Univé in de buurt, fysiek in één van onze twaalf advieswinkels in de regio, telefonisch of online via de Mijn Univé-App. Mooi toch? Onze circa 170 particuliere en zakelijke adviseurs krijgen ondersteuning vanuit ons hoofdkantoor in Heerhugowaard van ongeveer 80 collega’s als het gaat om financiën, marketing, communicatie, HRM, ICT, schadeafwikkeling en compliance.

title: Senior Business Informatie-analist - Omnichannel Salesfunnels
description:
Zorg jij dat complexe verandering niet blijft hangen in analyse en afstemming?

Wie ben jij

Als Senior Business Informatie Analist binnen de waardestroom Direct Verzekeren en Advies (DVA) breng je de ketens bij elkaar. Je activeert collega's om verder te kijken dan hun eigen team, proces of systeem en organiseert de beweging van vraagstuk naar besluit en resultaat.

Je combineert stevige businessanalyse met een goede IT-basis. Daarbij kijk je niet alleen naar wat er gevraagd wordt, maar juist naar het achterliggende probleem, de samenhang in de keten en de oplossing die Univé ook op langere termijn verder helpt.

Wat ga je doen

Binnen DVA werken business en IT samen aan de processen waarmee particuliere klanten zich oriënteren, advies krijgen en verzekeringen afsluiten. Dat gebeurt via verschillende kanalen en raakt meerdere processen, teams en IT-oplossingen.

Die omgeving is inhoudelijk en technisch complex. Veranderingen stoppen zelden bij één applicatie of één team. Juist daar kom jij in beeld.

Als Senior Business Informatie Analist:

  • analyseer je complexe verander- en informatievraagstukken en breng je processen, informatie, systemen en afhankelijkheden in samenhang;

  • achterhaal je samen met business en IT het werkelijke probleem achter een vraag en vertaal je dat naar heldere oplossingsrichtingen, requirements en keuzes;

  • bewaak je de integraliteit van veranderingen en kijk je nadrukkelijk naar effecten op andere processen, systemen, teams en domeinen;

  • breng je stakeholders en IT-disciplines bij elkaar wanneer een resultaat meerdere teams of onderdelen raakt;

  • coördineer je over teams heen wat nodig is om voortgang en resultaat te realiseren, zonder daarbij de verantwoordelijkheid van anderen over te nemen;

  • signaleer je blokkades en tegengestelde belangen vroegtijdig en help je betrokkenen om tot besluiten en een werkbare weg vooruit te komen;

  • daag je collega's uit om niet alleen vanuit de eigen oplossing of discipline te denken, maar vanuit het resultaat voor de hele keten en uiteindelijk onze leden;

  • adviseer je gevraagd én ongevraagd over verbeteringen in processen, informatievoorziening en IT-oplossingen;

  • draag je bij aan de ontwikkeling van andere Business Informatie Analisten en andere inhoudelijke professionals door kennis te delen, te coachen en samen de kwaliteit van analyse en samenwerking te verhogen;

  • onderzoek je actief hoe technologische ontwikkelingen, waaronder AI, kunnen bijdragen aan betere oplossingen en aan een slimmere manier van werken.

Je beweegt daarbij continu in het spanningsveld tussen snelheid en kwaliteit. Soms is versnellen nodig, soms juist vertragen om een keuze goed te doorgronden. Van jou verwachten we dat je die afweging zichtbaar maakt en helpt om samen tot een bewuste keuze te komen.

Succes in deze rol betekent voor ons dat complexe onderwerpen niet blijven hangen. Jij organiseert duidelijkheid, brengt de keten bij elkaar, spreekt mensen aan en helpt ervoor te zorgen dat besluiten daadwerkelijk tot uitvoering komen.

Wat bieden wij

De functie Senior Business Informatie Analist is ingeschaald in schaal 10. Afhankelijk van je kennis en ervaring ligt de salarisrange tussen €65.807 en €94.551 bruto per jaar, op basis van een 38-urige werkweek, inclusief vakantiegeld en een dertiende maand en exclusief variabele beloning.

Daarnaast bieden we onder andere:

  • een variabele Collectieve Prestatie Beloning van maximaal 9% van het jaarsalaris;

  • een arbeidsvoorwaardenkeuzesysteem: tijd voor geld of geld voor tijd;

  • 26 vakantiedagen bij een 38-urige werkweek;

  • een goede studiekostenregeling en veel ruimte voor professionele ontwikkeling;

  • een goede pensioenvoorziening;

  • vergoeding voor woon-werkverkeer en thuiswerken;

  • korting op je schade- en zorgverzekeringen bij Univé;

  • hybride werken.

Wie wij zijn

Univé IT wil bijdragen aan het waarmaken van de strategie van Univé door technologie zo in te zetten dat de organisatie efficiënter, innovatiever en wendbaarder wordt.

Daarbij draait het niet alleen om technologie. We willen als IT zichtbaar beweging creëren, eigenaarschap nemen en vanuit ons vakgebied actief bijdragen aan de doelen van de waardestromen.

IT Distributie werkt daarom dicht op de waardestromen van Univé. We ontwikkelen en verbeteren klantreizen en de IT-oplossingen die daarvoor nodig zijn. We kijken kritisch naar wat we zelf moeten kunnen, waar we samenwerken met technologiepartners en hoe nieuwe technologie – waaronder AI – ons en onze leden verder kan helpen.

Als Senior Business Informatie Analist heb je hierin een belangrijke positie. Je bent niet alleen degene die een vraagstuk analyseert, maar ook een senior professional die helpt om mensen, expertise en besluitvorming in beweging te krijgen.

Enthousiast?

Herken jij jezelf in deze rol en krijg je energie van complexe veranderopgaven waarin business, IT en meerdere teams samen moeten komen? Dan horen we graag van je.

In de kern ondersteunt het Centric CIO Office de Centric-organisatie bij het realiseren van operational excellence en het krijgen van grip op haar processen. Het CIO Office bestaat momenteel uit een Enterprise Architect en een Business Architect. Met de toevoeging van de Data Architect zijn de kerndiensten van het team gedekt. Je rapporteert aan de CIO en werkt nauw samen met de managers van de afdelingen Internal IT en Business Applications die ook binnen de verantwoordelijkheid van de CIO vallen.

 

Wat jij doet

Je geeft richting aan de definitie en continue verbetering van beleid voor de levenscyclus van data en het gebruik van AI, in samenwerking met verschillende stakeholders over de internationale Centric locaties. Bevindingen moeten worden opgenomen in de bredere Enterprise Architecture, maar er moet ook aandacht zijn voor het in de praktijk brengen van initiatieven. Je adviseert interne stakeholders en data-eigenaren en vertaalt opkomende bedrijfsbehoeften naar actueel beleid. Met jouw ontwerp van onze data-architectuur stuur je de organisatie richting effectieve en efficiënte besluitvorming rondom data voor interne en commerciële oplossingen. 

Wat doe je nog meer?

  • Het ontwerpen en onderhouden van enterprise data-architectuur (datamodellen, pipelines, platforms en integraties) 

  • Het definiëren en handhaven van datastandaarden, governance en kwaliteitskaders 

  • Het ondersteunen van data-eigenaren in de business, zodat hun data veilig, toegankelijk en compliant is 

  • De evolutie naar een moderne data architectuur leiden, inclusief een ondersteunend platform (zoals data lakehouse, real-time data) 

  • Het begeleiden en goedkeuren van AI-usecases en oplossingsontwerpen binnen de organisatie 

  • Het definiëren van best practices voor datapipelines, modelimplementatie en lifecycle management 

  • Het definiëren en implementeren van richtlijnen voor ethisch, verantwoord en veilig gebruik van AI-systemen 

  • Het stimuleren van experimenten en proof of concept initiatieven binnen de afdelingen Internal IT en Business Applications 

  • Het beïnvloeden zonder formele bevoegdheid in een complexe stakeholderomgeving 

  • Het communiceren van complexe technische concepten aan niet-technische en internationale stakeholders 

  • Het bijhouden van opkomende trends op het gebied van data-architectuur en AI 

  • Het bevorderen van een datagedreven en AI-ondersteunde cultuur binnen de organisatie

title: Engineering Manager Platform (m/f/d)
description:
Our mission

We are on a mission to save our planet - one second hand product at a time.

Join us at our Berlin headquarters as Engineering Manager Platform (m/f/d)!

Around 80 engineers in 10 product teams build and run their products on our cloud platform. You will take charge of the team that owns it and turn it into something they use on their own instead of waiting in a queue. In this role, you’ll report to the Head of Department.

Your mission

  • Lead a team of four platform engineers as their people and technical manager: hiring, 1:1s, feedback and growth plans
  • Own our Google Cloud infrastructure and its security, with decisions that shape how the whole IT organisation works
  • Run the platform as a reliable product for the software engineering teams: they are your customers, you are the key interface to them and success is measured by adoption
  • Build a self-service platform that gives teams what they need without raising a ticket
  • Drive AI and agent-based automation of infrastructure work, starting with first-pass reviews of Terraform changes against one standard, with engineers making the final call
  • Consolidate monitoring and alerting into one unified observability stack
  • Stay hands-on - you are an engineer who leads, not a manager who stopped engineering

Our Tech Stack

  • Google Cloud: GKE, Compute Engine, Cloud SQL, Cloud Storage, IAM
  • Infrastructure and delivery: Terraform, ArgoCD, self-hosted GitLab, Vault
  • AI: Claude Code, ChatGPT and Gemini
  • Observability: Grafana, Sentry

Your profile

  • Several years of experience with a major public cloud (GCP, AWS or Azure)
  • Kubernetes and Terraform in production environments
  • CI/CD pipelines and workflows, e.g. GitLab CI, Jenkins or GitHub Actions
  • Solid cloud security knowledge and a broad understanding of networking and Linux
  • Experience leading people or technical topics and the wish to grow as a manager
  • You organise your own work, communicate openly, share what you know and ask for feedback
  • You prioritise, execute and move things forward without waiting to be asked
  • Fluent English; German is not required

You can look forward to

  • Flexible working hours: We follow a hybrid work model with 20 in-office days per quarter to foster important personal interaction while enabling a modern, flexible way of working. The remaining days can be worked from home, and you also have the option to spend up to 6 weeks per year working from countries within EU. You’ll also benefit from flexible working hours to fit your individual needs.
  • Individual work environment: Design your ergonomic workspace just the way you like it – with height-adjustable desks and the laptop of your choice (MacBook or ThinkPad). If things get a bit noisy in the office, your Bose noise-cancelling headphones ensure uninterrupted focus. If needed, we can also provide you with an ergonomic chair or additional monitors for your home office.
  • Sustainability: We love second-hand and incorporate our sustainable business idea into the office routine with simple methods like using eco-friendly supplies, double-sided printing, energy-saving modes on devices, waste separation, etc. In doing so, we take responsibility and integrate sustainability into all our activities.
  • Open work environment: We work together in a bright, open-plan office where even the few existing doors are always open. Our teams are motivated and open to new ideas. Bring your creativity to the table and make things happen! If you need a moment of peace, you can retreat to a cozy corner of the medimops library in the break room, or recharge with a game of foosball, table tennis, or PlayStation.
  • Reduced ticket for the public transport: Save real money with the Germany or Job Ticket for the Berlin S-Bahn.
  • Company discounts: As a momoxian, you can look forward to a monthly voucher for our momox Fashion online shop, as well as medimops. Additionally, you benefit from numerous company discounts from our partners.
  • Training: momox is only as good as you. That's why you will find room and budget for your individual professional development with language classes, internal training, conferences, (online) courses and more.
  • Team events: Having fun at work and celebrating our successes together are core to our values. That’s why we regularly come together at various events to connect, get to know each other better, and strengthen our team spirit.

title: Senior Backend Engineer, Platform
description:
Join Apaleo and shape the future of hospitality tech

Apaleo is the world's most open, API-first property management platform, powering the next generation of hospitality operations. Our modular, AI-powered infrastructure lets hoteliers customise their tech stack, automate routine work and deliver seamless, personalised guest experiences, powered by best-in-class apps and autonomous AI agents that adapt to every stay.

If you're driven by the idea of making hospitality smarter, more human and powered by cutting-edge technology, we'd love to hear from you.

About the role

You'll join our Platform team as an individual contributor, working directly with our Platform Lead, who sets Platform's technical direction. Platform owns infrastructure, developer experience and security foundations for the whole engineering organisation. It's a small team, so you'll cover a wide surface area, with no dedicated DevOps or QA function to hand work to.

This is a high-ownership seat. You'll take on substantial, ambiguous, cross-cutting initiatives, agree the direction with the Platform Lead, then drive them from first analysis through to completion with real autonomy over how you get there.

We don't run a groomed backlog or sprint planning. We assign a significant topic to someone who owns it end to end. If you thrive with structure handed to you, this isn't the role. If you love spotting the problem worth solving and driving it yourself, you'll fit right in.

 

What you'll be up to 

  • Designing and building scalable, reliable and maintainable backend systems.
  • Spotting and scoping problems and initiatives yourself, not just picking up assigned tickets: weighing impact, priority and timing.
  • Contributing to architectural decisions and design discussions, and bringing other teams along.
  • Driving substantial, cross-cutting initiatives end to end, coordinating with stakeholders across engineering.
  • Building and maintaining internal tools and infrastructure (AWS, Terraform) that help teams deliver faster and more reliably.
  • Owning observability, logging and operational excellence to keep the platform highly available.
  • Sharing knowledge through code reviews, design reviews and pairing, and helping raise technical standards.
  • Spotting where AI and automation can improve how we build and run software.

 

Some of the challenges waiting for you 

You'll take ownership of one of these as your first initiative, with no other distractions.

  • Solving horizontal write-scaling for our database.
  • Modernising our CI/CD pipeline for faster, more reliable delivery.
  • Migrating our infrastructure-as-code fully from CloudFormation to Terraform.
  • Extracting and reworking common services to get us ready for our next scale level.

What you'll bring to the team 

  • 5+ years of backend development experience, with a track record of owning significant technical work from ambiguity through to completion.
  • Substantial hands-on ownership of infrastructure, reliability or performance, ideally on a platform or infrastructure team rather than a pure product team.
  • Strong engineering fundamentals that transfer across languages and cloud platforms. We care more about how you think than which stack you've used.
  • Experience designing and scaling distributed systems in cloud-native environments (AWS preferred; strong Azure fundamentals and genuine enthusiasm for the switch work just as well).
  • Comfort with containerised services and infrastructure-as-code (Docker, Terraform; CloudFormation exposure is relevant given our current stack).
  • Confidence writing your own unit and integration tests, as we don't have a dedicated QA function.
  • A project you can talk about in depth: the problem, what you did and the impact it had.
  • Fluent English.

Nice to have 

  • Direct experience with C# (.NET), PostgreSQL, AWS and ECS or Kubernetes: a great fit, though not a hard requirement if your fundamentals are strong.
  • Experience setting up infrastructure-as-code from scratch and working with it day to day, ideally with Terraform, including migrating or consolidating from other approaches (like CloudFormation).
  • Experience with Kafka or other event-driven and streaming systems (Azure Service Bus, RabbitMQ or SQS are good transferable equivalents).
  • Experience owning observability and logging for highly available systems.
  • Hands-on use of AI-assisted development tools (GitHub Copilot, Cursor AI, ChatGPT, Amazon CodeWhisperer) and a genuine interest in AI-driven engineering improvement.
  • Experience mentoring other engineers, and introducing new technology, like AI tooling, to other teams.

 

Culture & Growth

What We Offer 

  • An International Team: Work alongside colleagues from over 20 nationalities. 
  • Growth and Development: 360° feedback reviews, an evolving career framework and an annual learning budget of €1,000+. 
  • Autonomy and Ownership: Great ideas can come from anywhere. We trust you to make decisions and contribute directly. 
  • Real Impact: Join a fast-growing scale-up transforming hospitality. From day one, your work drives real impact. 
  • Fair Pay: Competitive salaries guided by benchmarking data, with recognition for performance and contribution. 
  • Flexible Work: Work from home, the office or a hybrid mix. We focus on results, not clocking hours. 
  • Time Off and Wellbeing: 30 days of vacation and an EGYM Wellpass membership. 
  • Free Public Transport: A fully covered Deutschland Ticket for travel across Germany. 
  • Team Connection: Regular team dinners, company meetups and offsite events. 

How you make an impact joining Apaleo: Joining Apaleo is more than taking on a role. It's about driving real change in the hospitality industry. Your contributions will directly shape our innovative platform, influence company-wide decisions and help redefine the future of hospitality tech. At Apaleo, your voice matters, your ideas are valued and your impact is tangible. Be part of a team where your work fuels progress, collaboration sparks innovation and growth is a shared journey. 

We are proud to be an Equal Opportunity and Affirmative Action Employer, committed to fostering a diverse, inclusive and welcoming workplace. We encourage applications from individuals of all backgrounds, regardless of race, colour, religion, gender identity or expression, sex, national origin, age, marital status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. Your personal data will be handled with the utmost care and in compliance with GDPR and relevant data protection regulations. We celebrate differences and believe that diversity enriches our team and drives innovation.

title: Claims Controller - Schadencontrolling & Impact Analytics (m/w/d)
description:
Über Enzo

Enzo ist ein innovativer Technologiedienstleister mit Sitz in Heidelberg, der eines der größten strukturellen Kostenprobleme der Gebäudeversicherung adressiert: Leitungswasserschäden.

Mit unserer patentierten IoT- und KI-basierten Lösung one.drop erkennen wir Wasserverluste frühzeitig und helfen Versicherern und ihren Kunden, Schäden zu verhindern oder ihr Ausmaß zu begrenzen.

Unsere Mission ist klar: Prävention als wirtschaftlich messbaren und skalierbaren Bestandteil der Gebäudeversicherung etablieren - mit ökonomischem und ökologischem Impact.

Gemeinsam mit führenden Versicherungsunternehmen setzen wir diese Mission um. Dafür müssen wir präzise verstehen, wie sich die Schadenentwicklung in den betreuten Beständen verändert und welchen Beitrag Enzo dazu leistet.

Genau dafür suchen wir dich.

Aufgaben

Deine Rolle

Als Claims Controller übernimmst du die Verantwortung für einen fundierten, ganzheitlichen Blick auf die Schadenentwicklung unserer Versicherungspartner.

Du verstehst, wie Versicherer Schadenbestände auswerten, Kennzahlen definieren und Ergebnisse beurteilen. Du sprichst ihre Sprache und kannst mit Schadencontrolling, Schadenmanagement und Aktuariat auf Augenhöhe zusammenarbeiten.

Aus unterschiedlichen Datenquellen entwickelst du eine konsistente Sicht auf Schadenhäufigkeit, durchschnittlichen Schadenaufwand und Gesamtschadenkosten. Du machst Veränderungen sichtbar, ordnest sie fachlich ein und schaffst belastbare Grundlagen, um die wirtschaftliche Wirkung unserer Prävention zu bewerten.

Dabei gehst du über die Erstellung von Reports hinaus: Du erkennst Auffälligkeiten, hinterfragst Interpretationen und leitest konkrete Erkenntnisse für unsere Versicherungspartner und unser eigenes Team ab.

Dein Verantwortungsbereich

Schadenentwicklung verstehen und transparent machen

  • Aufbau eines übergreifenden Schadencontrollings für die von Enzo betreuten Versicherungsbestände

  • Analyse von Schadenhäufigkeit, durchschnittlichem Schadenaufwand, Gesamtschadenkosten und – bei entsprechender Datengrundlage – Schadenquoten

  • Differenzierung nach Schadenursachen, Bestandsmerkmalen, Zeiträumen und relevanten Kundengruppen

  • Frühzeitiges Erkennen und fachliches Einordnen von Trends, Abweichungen und Auffälligkeiten

Vergleichbarkeit und Datenqualität sicherstellen

  • Abstimmung von Datenanforderungen, Kennzahlendefinitionen und Auswertungslogiken mit unseren Versicherungspartnern

  • Zusammenführung und Plausibilisierung unterschiedlicher Bestands- und Schadendaten

  • Berücksichtigung von Bestandsstruktur, Exposition, Beobachtungsdauer, Schadenreife und Reservierungsstand

  • Aufbau nachvollziehbarer Standards, die partnerübergreifende Analysen ermöglichen und Unterschiede transparent machen

Präventionswirkung belastbar bewerten

  • Entwicklung geeigneter Vorher-nachher-Auswertungen und Vergleiche zwischen Beständen mit und ohne Sensorik

  • Bewertung, inwieweit beobachtete Unterschiede durch Prävention oder andere Einflussfaktoren erklärt werden können

  • Klare Unterscheidung zwischen beobachteten Veränderungen, modellierten Einsparungen und belastbar nachgewiesenen Effekten

  • Zusammenarbeit mit Customer Success und unserem Daten-Team bei der Weiterentwicklung unserer Wirkungs- und ROI-Modelle

Erkenntnisse in Entscheidungen übersetzen

  • Erstellung verständlicher Reports und Analysen für Fachbereiche, Management und Vorstände

  • Fachlicher Austausch mit Schadencontrolling, Schadenmanagement und Aktuariat unserer Partner

  • Ableitung konkreter Handlungsempfehlungen für Bestandsauswahl, Präventionsmaßnahmen und operative Verbesserungen

  • Aufbau wiederverwendbarer Auswertungen und zunehmend automatisierter Reporting-Prozesse

Qualifikation

Dein Profil

Erfahrung im Schadencontrolling

  • Mehrjährige Erfahrung im Schadencontrolling, Versicherungscontrolling, in der Schadenanalyse oder einer vergleichbaren analytischen Funktion bei einem Versicherer

  • Gutes Verständnis der Schadenprozesse und der betriebswirtschaftlichen Steuerung im Schaden-/Unfallgeschäft

  • Erfahrung in der Wohngebäudeversicherung ist besonders wertvoll

Fachliche und analytische Sicherheit

  • Du kennst die Kennzahlen, Datenstrukturen und Auswertungslogiken, mit denen Versicherer ihre Schadenentwicklung steuern

  • Du kannst Zahlungsstände, Reserven und Schadenaufwand fachlich einordnen und weißt, wie sich Auswertungen nach Schaden-, Melde- oder Geschäftsjahr unterscheiden

  • Du erkennst, wann Daten einen belastbaren Schluss zulassen und wann weitere Informationen oder eine andere Vergleichslogik erforderlich sind

  • Du arbeitest präzise und machst Annahmen, Unsicherheiten und Grenzen einer Analyse transparent

Sicherer Umgang mit Daten und Tools

  • Sehr gute Excel-Kenntnisse und Erfahrung mit BI- und Reporting-Werkzeugen, beispielsweise Power BI, Tableau oder vergleichbaren Lösungen

  • Idealerweise SQL-Kenntnisse und Erfahrung mit größeren Datenbeständen

  • Interesse daran, manuelle Auswertungen in verlässliche, wiederholbare Prozesse zu überführen

Kommunikation und Ownership

  • Du kannst komplexe Analysen verständlich erklären und gegenüber erfahrenen Ansprechpartnern auf Versichererseite vertreten

  • Du hinterfragst Ergebnisse konstruktiv und bleibst fachlich klar, auch wenn eine Analyse Erwartungen nicht bestätigt

  • Du übernimmst Verantwortung von der Datenanforderung bis zur belastbaren Schlussfolgerung

  • Sehr gutes Deutsch und gutes Englisch

Benefits

Warum Enzo?

  • Deine Analysen machen Wirkung sichtbar
    Du schaffst die Grundlage, auf der Versicherer über den Einsatz und die Skalierung von Prävention entscheiden.

  • Aufbau statt bestehender Routinen
    Du entwickelst unser Schadencontrolling und prägst dessen Methoden, Standards und Werkzeuge.

  • Versicherungswissen trifft Technologie
    Du verbindest deine Erfahrung aus der Versicherungswirtschaft mit IoT, KI und frühzeitiger Schadenprävention.

  • Direkter Einfluss auf das Geschäft
    Deine Erkenntnisse fließen in Produktentwicklung, Kundenarbeit und strategische Entscheidungen ein.

  • Enge Zusammenarbeit mit dem Gründerteam
    Kurze Entscheidungswege, viel Gestaltungsspielraum und Verantwortung für ein zentrales Thema unserer Entwicklung.

  • Builder-Kultur
    Wir schätzen Klarheit, Ownership und die Fähigkeit, Erkenntnisse in konkrete Verbesserungen zu übersetzen.

Du möchtest dein Versicherungswissen einsetzen, um Schäden früher zu verhindern und die Wirkung von Prävention belastbar nachzuweisen? Dann freuen wir uns auf deine Bewerbung.

title: Social Media & Content Creation (m/w/d)
description:
Über uns

Gute Bars leben von guten Geschichten. Von unvergesslichen Abenden, spontanen Begegnungen, guter Musik und Menschen, die gerne wiederkommen.

Wir sind die stadtbörse GmbH und betreiben Gastronomiekonzepte in Bonn. Unsere Bars sind Treffpunkte für Studierende, Freundeskreise, Nachtschwärmer und Stammgäste. Jeder Standort hat seinen eigenen Charakter, aber eines haben alle gemeinsam: Wir lieben lebendige Gastronomie und möchten Orte schaffen, an denen Menschen gerne ihre Zeit verbringen.

Und genau dieses Gefühl wollen wir auch online vermitteln.

Dafür suchen wir jemanden, der Social Media nicht einfach nur bespielt, sondern Lust hat, unsere Marken kreativ mitzugestalten.

Deine Aufgaben

Bei uns bekommst du keine fertigen Posts auf den Tisch gelegt, die du nur noch veröffentlichen musst. Du kannst eigene Ideen entwickeln, ausprobieren und umsetzen.

  • Content Creation: Du produzierst Fotos, Reels, Stories und andere kreative Inhalte für unsere Social Media Kanäle.

  • Social Media Management: Du betreust insbesondere unsere Instagram- und TikTok-Accounts und entwickelst sie kontinuierlich weiter.

  • Kreative Konzepte: Du entwickelst neue Content-Formate, Kampagnen und Ideen, die zu unseren Bars und ihrer jeweiligen Zielgruppe passen.

  • Content vor Ort: Du bist regelmäßig in unseren Bars unterwegs, fängst besondere Momente ein und machst unsere Atmosphäre digital erlebbar.

  • Community Management: Du interagierst mit unserer Community und hilfst dabei, unsere Reichweite und Bekanntheit auszubauen.

  • Events & Aktionen: Du begleitest Veranstaltungen, Specials und Marketingaktionen von der ersten Ankündigung bis zum Rückblick.

  • Performance & Trends: Du beobachtest aktuelle Trends, analysierst die Entwicklung unserer Kanäle und findest heraus, welche Inhalte besonders gut funktionieren.

Das bringst du mit

Wir suchen keine Person, die einfach nur viel Zeit auf Instagram verbringt. Wir suchen jemanden, der versteht, warum manche Inhalte funktionieren und andere nicht.

  • Du hast ein gutes Gespür für Ästhetik, Bildsprache und aktuelle Social Media Trends.

  • Instagram, TikTok und Reels sind für dich keine Fremdwörter.

  • Du kannst mit deinem Smartphone guten Content produzieren und hast idealerweise erste Erfahrung mit Tools wie Canva, CapCut oder Adobe.

  • Du arbeitest eigenständig, zuverlässig und bringst gerne eigene Ideen ein.

  • Du hast Lust auf Gastronomie, Events und das Bonner Nachtleben.

  • Du bist zeitlich flexibel genug, um gelegentlich auch abends oder am Wochenende Content vor Ort zu produzieren.

Besonders wichtig ist uns dein kreatives Gespür. Ob du bereits professionelle Social Media Accounts betreut hast oder bisher vor allem eigene Projekte umgesetzt hast, ist für uns zweitrangig. Entscheidend ist, dass du gute Ideen hast und sie auch umsetzen kannst.

Das bieten wir dir

  • Kreative Freiheit: Du kannst eigene Ideen einbringen, neue Formate testen und unseren Social Media Auftritt aktiv mitgestalten.

  • Echte Verantwortung: Du betreust eigene Projekte und siehst unmittelbar, was deine Arbeit bewirkt.

  • Flexible Arbeitszeiten: Wir stimmen deine Arbeitszeiten auf dein Studium ab.

  • Hybrides Arbeiten: Vieles kannst du flexibel erledigen. Für Contentproduktionen bist du regelmäßig vor Ort.

  • Kurze Entscheidungswege: Du arbeitest direkt mit der Geschäftsführung zusammen, ohne komplizierte Freigabeprozesse.

  • Abwechslungsreiche Projekte: Unterschiedliche Bars, Veranstaltungen und Zielgruppen sorgen für immer neue kreative Möglichkeiten.

  • Moderne Arbeitsmittel: Wir stellen dir die notwendigen Tools und Arbeitsmittel zur Verfügung.

  • Ein junges, unkompliziertes Team: Bei uns zählen gute Ideen, Eigeninitiative und ein angenehmes Miteinander.

  • Kostenlose Getränke und Mitarbeiterrabatte in unseren Betrieben.

Assistant General Counsel – Product and Regulatory Legal (EU)
description:
Building the Future of Open Finance

Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.


Before you apply, we encourage you to explore our culture page to understand what drives us and how we work.

The team

Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.

Join our Product and Regulatory Legal team, embedded with Kraken's Product, Design and Engineering teams to ship novel products and experiences that accelerate the global adoption of crypto. We are a tight, experienced group of lawyers from a diverse range of tradfi, fintech and crypto backgrounds who move fast, stay curious and take pride in the commercial accountability of our advice, partnering directly with Product, senior leadership and Compliance to chart clear, defensible paths to launch and to keep our licensed entities running smoothly.

This is a senior product-facing legal role for the European Union. You will be the lawyer the business trusts on questions that cut across several regimes at once: for example, a single product such as a tokenised equity, a card, or an institutional custody and prime brokerage service can touch the Markets in Financial Instruments Directive ("MiFID II"), the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation ("MiCA"), the Payment Services Directive ("PSD2"), the Electronic Money Directive ("EMD2") and banking rules at the same time. You will bring clarity on which regime applies, what it requires, and how to launch within it.

 

The opportunity

Reporting to the Head of Product Legal, you will act as a senior legal adviser to European leadership on new products, licensing structure and regulatory strategy.

  • Own cross-functional product counselling for European Union launches from discovery to design, launch and iteration, giving Product, Engineering, Compliance and leadership decision-ready advice with clear options and risk trade-offs

  • Advise on the regulatory perimeter and classification of new offerings across MiFID II and the Markets in Financial Instruments Regulation ("MiFIR"), MiCA, the European Market Infrastructure Regulation ("EMIR"), payment services and electronic money rules, and banking regulation, including where an instrument or service falls between regimes (for example tokenised securities, crypto-asset derivatives, margin and financing, and stablecoin-linked products)

  • Advise on payments and electronic money offerings, including the Krak card and account propositions, safeguarding, open banking and account-access obligations, and the developing Payment Services Directive 3 and Payment Services Regulation framework

  • Advise on banking-related questions that arise in the European Union, including bank partnerships and sponsor-bank arrangements, deposit-taking and lending perimeter questions, the Capital Requirements Regulation and Directive, and the interaction of these rules with our custody, prime brokerage and financing products

  • Monitor and interpret European Union legislative and supervisory developments, take part in consultations and industry association work where appropriate, and translate their significance for the business proactively

  • Draft and negotiate client-facing terms and conditions, taking clear, business-aligned positions

  • Act as gatekeeper for European Union outside counsel engagements: scope the work, estimate and manage cost, and sign off before matters go externally

  • Mentor and develop more junior lawyers in the team, set quality standards for plain-English, risk-based advice, and act as a senior sounding board for colleagues across the Regulatory Legal team

  • Use AI-assisted tools (for example Enterprise GPTs) to speed up regulatory analysis, first drafts and matter tracking, and to build self-service tools that let stakeholders answer commoditised legal and regulatory questions themselves

  • Advise on anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing requirements affecting products, including the Transfer of Funds Regulation ("Travel Rule") and the new European Union anti-money laundering package, and on market abuse, conduct, outsourcing and operational resilience obligations, including the Digital Operational Resilience Act ("DORA")

  • Lead or oversee licensing, authorisation and variation workstreams in the European Union, including scoping requirements, mapping pathways, supervising outside counsel, preparing application materials and managing regulator interactions

 
 

What you bring

  • Qualified lawyer admitted in Ireland, England and Wales, or another European Union Member State

  • 15 or more years' post-qualification experience ("PQE") in financial services regulatory law, gained at a regulated financial services institution (for example a bank, payment institution, broker-dealer, exchange, central counterparty or crypto services provider) or at a leading law firm supporting such clients, ideally with in-house or direct product counselling experience

  • Deep, current knowledge of several of the following, with real depth in at least two: MiFID II and MiFIR (investment services, market structure, derivatives and conduct), MiCA (crypto-asset services, custody, trading platforms and stablecoins), European Union payment services and electronic money regulation, and European Union banking regulation

  • Demonstrated ability to analyse novel products against overlapping regimes and give a clear view on classification and perimeter, including in areas where the rules are unsettled or supervisors have not yet spoken

  • Direct experience managing senior regulator relationships, including notifications, information requests, supervisory correspondence and examinations

  • Working knowledge of anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing, outsourcing and operational resilience obligations, including DORA

  • Proven ability to instruct, supervise and manage the cost of outside counsel across multiple jurisdictions

  • Outstanding analytical, drafting and organisational skills, with crisp, plain-English writing

  • Ability to distill complex legal and regulatory issues into clear, actionable guidance for non-lawyer stakeholders and for senior leadership

  • A pragmatic, commercially accountable approach to legal and regulatory risk that gives stakeholders a useful range of options and a clear recommendation

  • Experience mentoring or managing lawyers, and the judgement to know when to escalate

  • Comfort operating with a high degree of autonomy in a fast-moving, remote environment

  • Familiarity with using AI tools such as Enterprise GPTs to increase the efficiency of legal services

 
 

Nice to haves

  • Experience advising on tokenised securities and the European Union Distributed Ledger Technology Pilot Regime

  • Experience with EMIR, including the clearing obligation, margin for non-centrally cleared derivatives and transaction reporting

  • Experience with prime brokerage, securities financing, margin lending or institutional custody

  • Experience advising on the United Kingdom cryptoasset regime or other non-European Union frameworks that intersect with European Union operations

  • Experience supporting regulatory aspects of corporate transactions, such as change-of-control notifications and entity migrations

  • Experience with European Union data protection and consumer protection rules as they apply to financial products

  • Fluency in a second European language

  • An authentic interest in crypto and digital assets, and familiarity with Payward's and competitors' products

 
 
 

Unless a specific application deadline is stated in the job posting, applications are accepted on an ongoing basis.

We consider qualified applicants with criminal histories for employment on our team, assessing candidates in a manner consistent with the requirements of the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.

Our commitment

Payward is powered by people from around the world and we celebrate the diverse talents, backgrounds, contributions, and unique perspectives that everyone brings to the table. We hire based on merit, seeking out people with the right abilities, knowledge, and skills for the job. We encourage you to apply for roles where you don't fully meet the listed requirements, especially if you're passionate or knowledgeable about crypto.

title: Clinical AI Engineer
description:
We’re Heidi.

We're building the future of healthcare by giving every clinician the earth's finest AI Care Partner. Our platform has absorbed the administrative chaos of 175 million patient visits and supported 67 million clinical hours. Today, we support 2.8 million patient sessions a week across 190+ countries, in 110 languages and over 200 specialties.

Healthcare systems are failing us; clinicians spend more time on documentation than on patients, and the human connection that makes medicine worth practicing is eroding. Our mission is simple: double the world’s capacity for care and strengthen the human connection at its heart.

We found product-market fit with a freemium medical scribe that clinicians love. Now, we're expanding. Every task a clinician hands to Heidi is a patient who feels more attended to, a health system unclogged, and a clinician who gets to be a clinician again.

We’ve grown annual recurring revenue from $1 million to $50 million in two years.

To go further, we’ve secured US$340 million: a $100 million Series C led by Blackbird, with Phoenix Court, Point72 Private Investments and Headline, alongside a $240 million growth investment led by General Catalyst’s Customer Value Fund.

If you want to join us in doing work worth shipping, jump in.

The role

We’re looking for a doctor who has moved into AI and can code, to join Clinical AI R&D as a Clinical AI Engineer. You’ll sit inside a product pod and own the evidence for its product: define the evaluation before anyone builds, run it to a standard a journal reviewer would accept, keep watching the product once it ships, publish what the evidence shows, and change the product when the evidence says to.



The pod’s engineers can change the product but can’t judge whether a discharge summary missed something a consultant would catch. Clinicians can make that call but can’t open a pull request. You do both, and you treat the gap between a model’s output and good clinical practice as the thing you’re here to measure and close.



The loop doesn’t end at launch. You stay with the product for its life in market.

 

What you’ll do

  • Design the evaluation. Define evaluations for greenfield products to an academic standard: endpoints, comparators, ground truth, sample size, analysis plan. Set the bar before the result arrives.

  • Build the measurement. Build, optimize and validate the LLM judges and rubrics that score the product at scale. Report their agreement with clinician ground truth, not their convenience, and retire the ones that drift.

  • Run it and write it up. Execute the evaluation, do the statistics, and write it up once in a form that serves the pod, the regulatory file and an academic submission.

  • Run post-market surveillance. Monitor output quality in production and respond to regulatory feedback with data. Our clinical safety team triages complaints and incidents; you’re their counterpart in the pod, working out what their findings mean for the product and what should change.

  • Fix what the evidence finds. Prompt and rubric changes, evaluation harness changes, code changes in the pod’s codebase, shipped through the pod’s normal review and release process.

  • Publish. Contribute to peer-reviewed literature on the translational benefit of the product.

  • Be the clinician in the room. Catch the output that reads well and is wrong. Hold the line on clinical nuance when a shortcut would ship faster.

 

What you'll need

  • A medical degree and clinical practice with independent clinical judgment. This role runs on medical nuance, and this requirement doesn’t flex.

  • Academic depth. Study design, inferential statistics, agreement and reliability measures, sample size, handling of multiple comparisons. Thesis or publication-level work, not a methods module.

  • Experience evaluating medical software or clinical AI, including building or validating LLM-as-judge pipelines.

  • Enough engineering to work in a production codebase. Read it, understand what a change will do, make the change in Python or TypeScript, and get it through review. Prompt engineering and AI-assisted coding are daily tools here, and they’re the floor, not the ceiling.

  • Independence. You can run a project for weeks with light direction, and you say early when it’s stuck.

  • Clear writing. Evaluation reports, surveillance summaries and manuscripts are the primary output of this role.

Nice to have

  • Post-market surveillance or vigilance work under a medical device framework (TGA, MHRA, FDA or EU MDR). Appetite to learn counts for more than existing depth.

  • Peer-reviewed publications on clinical AI or LLM evaluation.

  • Machine learning background beyond prompting, such as fine-tuning or classical model evaluation.

  • Specialty depth in an area Heidi is moving into.

  • An academic or clinical-site network able to host a study.

How we show up

  • Build for the next decade, not next quarter. Our targets are outrageous on purpose. The world's health doesn't have the luxury of incrementalism.

  • Lead, don't wait. We treat tomorrow's problems today. Sometimes we build what's needed before it's wanted, and we're fine with that.

  • Follow the evidence. Trust the patient. We pursue truth relentlessly. But when the subjective and objective disagree, we treat the patient, not the numbers. Ego is a comorbidity we can't afford.

  • Own the outcome. Everyone here carries the company. Raise problems with solutions, solve them end-to-end, and never be a bystander.

  • Ship, measure, go again. A button today, a workflow tomorrow. More iterations beat better planning. We're precise at pace, not reckless.

  • Live in clinicians' reality. Not the ideal workflow, the twenty-patients-before-lunch actual one. We build for exhausted humans, and we'd better be decent ones while we do it.

 

Why Heidi?

You’ll join a team measured on real-world impact, not press cycles. We live and breathe the challenges of modern health systems, and are laser-focused on exacting the change we’d like to see. We’re medicos, engineers, builders and designers who’ve felt (on every side of the equation) what non-care feels like, the moral and practical toll as a provider or receiver.

Building what we’re building isn’t always easy. Standard tech playbooks routinely fail in healthcare, and the friction of the medical system will test your perseverance. But we didn’t choose easy, we chose a purpose-driven mission that actually matters. We hold ourselves to a higher standard because healthcare demands it. If you join Heidi, you recognize that the deeper question isn’t whether AI can solve the global healthcare crisis, but whose hands will shape it.

True A-players progress extremely fast here. The nature of the scale-up game is demanding, but we value sustainable performance and mental health. You're trusted to perform, and you set your schedule. We operate on outcomes > inputs, not process theatre. We all take the bins out, metaphorically and literally.

Our Benefits

  • Equity from day one. When Heidi wins, you win. You'll share directly in the success you help create.

  • Your health, covered. Comprehensive private medical and dental cover through Bupa, plus 24/7 mental health, coaching and wellbeing support through Sonder and a £100/month Healthy Heidi’s stipend.

  • Global parental leave. 26 weeks paid for primary carers and 18 weeks for secondary carers, subject to eligibility.

  • Fertility support. £7,000 one-off payment, eligibility applies.

  • Learning & development. £700 per year for courses, books, memberships, conferences and more.

  • Home office budget of £500 one-off to set up a workspace you actually want to work in.

  • Recharge days after major milestones and busy periods so you can reset and come back strong.

  • Work from anywhere for up to 4 weeks per year, wherever the world takes you.

  • Clinical leave. 10 days per year for eligible clinical roles to maintain accreditation and requirements.

  • Flexibility that works. A hybrid environment, with 3 days in the office.

Heidi’s commitment to Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

Heidi is dedicated to creating an equitable, inclusive, and supportive work environment that brings people together from diverse backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. Our strength is in our differences. We're proud to be an equal opportunity employer and are proud to welcome all applicants as we're committed to promoting a culture of opportunity for all.

title: Senior HW Engineer – PCB Layout
description:
The Opportunity

Lumai's optical engine only works if the electronics around it hold up. Our boards carry large FPGAs and custom ASICs, multi-gigabit links and fine-pitch packages, and they have to be laid out to tolerances that leave no room for guesswork. This role takes the designs coming out of our hardware and SI/PI teams and turns them into manufacturable, high-layer-count boards.

The Role

You will own board layout from schematic handoff to fabrication release. That covers stackups and HDI structures, controlled-impedance routing, differential pairs, length and phase matching, BGA breakout for large fine-pitch devices, and the full manufacturing package: Gerber/ODB++, drill files, assembly drawings and fabrication notes. You will also own the footprint and symbol libraries, the design rules and the CAD standards the rest of the team works to.

What is genuinely hard about it is that the constraints are real and they conflict. Signal integrity, power integrity, thermal and mechanical requirements all land on the same square centimetres, and the fabricator's process limits decide what is actually buildable. You will be the person who turns simulation output into layout rules and who can defend a stackup to a fabricator.

By month six, you will have taken at least one board through to fabrication release, set the libraries and design rules the team works from, and be the first point of contact for our fabricators and assembly houses.

What You'll Do

  • Lay out dense, high-layer-count PCBs from schematic through to fabrication release, using constraint-driven flows.

  • Implement controlled-impedance routing, differential pair and length/phase matching, and HDI structures including microvias, via-in-pad and back-drilling.

  • Plan BGA breakout and component placement for large FPGAs, custom ASICs and fine-pitch packages, balancing SI, PI, thermal and mechanical requirements.

  • Translate SI/PI and hardware constraints into layout rules, and iterate quickly with engineers on simulation feedback.

  • Run DFM, DFA and DFT reviews, and act as the main technical contact with PCB fabricators and assembly houses.

  • Generate complete manufacturing outputs (Gerber/ODB++, drill files, assembly drawings, fabrication notes) and manage design revisions.

  • Own and maintain the footprint and symbol libraries, CAD standards and design templates, compliant with IPC standards.

What We're Looking For

Must-have

  • Extensive professional experience laying out complex, high-speed, high-layer-count boards, with a portfolio of designs that went into production.

  • Expert proficiency in Cadence Allegro, including Constraint Manager. Equivalent Altium experience will also be considered.

  • Hands-on experience with HDI technologies: microvias, via-in-pad, stacked and staggered vias, and back-drilling.

  • Proven BGA breakout and placement for large, fine-pitch devices such as FPGAs and ASICs.

  • Thorough working knowledge of IPC standards (IPC-2221, IPC-7351, IPC-6012) and of DFM/DFA/DFT principles.

Strong preference for

  • Boards carrying 56G+ SerDes, PCIe Gen5/6 or DDR5 interfaces.

  • Working closely with SI/PI simulation engineers.

  • Rigid-flex, RF or mixed-signal layouts.

  • ECAD/MCAD collaboration on thermal and mechanical integration.

  • Experience setting up CAD standards, libraries and design templates in a growing team.

About Lumai

Lumai is the optical compute company building the next generation of AI infrastructure. Spun out of optics research at the University of Oxford in 2021, we compute with light instead of electrons. Our 3D optical technology carries out the matrix multiplications at the heart of AI inside beams of light travelling through free space, which lets it go beyond the limits of both silicon GPUs and integrated photonics.

In April 2026 we launched Iris Nova, the world's first optical computing system to run billion-parameter large language models in real time, using up to 90% less energy than conventional GPU-based systems. Iris Nova, the first server in the family, is now available for evaluation by hyperscalers, neoclouds, enterprises and research institutions. Aura and Tetra will follow.

Our work won the Falling Walls Award for Science Breakthrough of the Year 2025 and 'Best Overall Technology' at the OCP Future Technologies Symposium. We are headquartered in Oxford.

Why Lumai

You'll work on a new kind of computer. Optical computing for AI has been promised for decades. We have a working system running real models, and the hard part left is taking it to volume.

Your work ships. We are moving from first product to volume production, so what you build this year goes into the servers our customers run.

You'll work across disciplines. Optical engineers, machine learning researchers, and hardware and software engineers solve problems together. You will learn things that don't appear on your job description.

The work matters beyond Lumai. AI's appetite for energy is one of the defining constraints of the next decade. Our mission is sustainable intelligence at global scale: AI that is faster, cheaper to run and far less power-hungry.

You'll join early. You'll have a real say in how we build the product, the team and the way we work.

Equal Opportunity

Lumai is an equal opportunity employer. We make hiring decisions based on skills, experience and potential, and we welcome applications from people of all backgrounds. If you need an adjustment at any stage of the hiring process, let us know and we will do our best to support you.

title: Payment Operations Lead
description:
Payment Operations Lead

Global expansion is broken. Without a local company, conversion rates fall, costs rise, and compliance gets messy. Outpost fixes it.

Selling internationally is a maze of tax, payments, and operational friction. Most brands avoid it, or expand slowly and expensively.

Outpost is your modular back office for global commerce.

Pick only what you need - tax, payments, treasury, or operations - and unlock new markets without the overhead. Sometimes we become liable for a merchant's taxes. Sometimes we become the legal reseller in each market and carry the payments, tax and compliance risk. Other times, we give you the tools to do it yourself.

We go live wherever a merchant needs to sell next, for digital and physical goods. That means we own the full stack - payments, tax, compliance, treasury, and merchant experience.

Sell anything, anywhere. Without compromise.

🧠 The Role

We're looking for a Payment Operations hire to own the part of Outpost where the money actually moves.

When we become the legal reseller in a market, we take the payment. Every merchant we onboard gets its own merchant ID and its own merchant category code, never pooled into one shared code, which is exactly why our approval rates beat the alternatives. Keeping that true across every market, every processor and every merchant is the job.

This is a quantitative role in an operational seat. You'll live in the transaction data: why authorisation rates differ by market, issuer, card type and hour of day, what a routing change is actually worth, where a 40 basis point cost difference is hiding, which decline codes are recoverable and which are noise. Then you'll act on it, with processors, with engineering, and with merchants.

You won't be siloed. Payments at Outpost touches pricing, treasury, tax and the product roadmap, and you'll be pulled into all of it. But your edge is the numbers, and we want someone whose first instinct on any problem is to pull the data and model it.

You'll work directly with the founding team and with engineering, who will build what you spec.

🧗 What You'll Get

Yes, the work is intense. But in return you'll get scope and exposure most people wait 10 to 20 years to access.

You'll own economics that decide whether the company is profitable, negotiate with processors and banks as a principal rather than a customer, and get to see the full machinery of cross-border payments from the inside. We won't handhold, but we'll coach you hard.

🧩 What You'll Do

Build the system

  • Run payment operations agentically. Build agentic system that monitor approval rates, triage declines, assemble dispute evidence, chase reconciliation breaks and draft the processor follow-up, so humans only touch the exceptions. You'll design the workflows, set the guardrails, and audit what the agents produce

  • Write the playbooks: new processor onboarding, new market launch, incident response, dispute handling

  • Onboard new processors, banking partners and local acquiring as we launch new markets

Own payments performance

  • Own approval rates by market, processor, issuer, card type and merchant, and know why each one moves

  • Build and run routing logic. Decide what goes where, prove the uplift, and iterate

  • Run decline recovery: retry logic, network tokens, account updater, 3DS strategy and exemption handling

  • Run chargeback operations and fraud strategy. Set thresholds, represent disputes, keep merchants inside scheme limits

  • Own the payment incident path. When authorisations drop in one market at, you're the one who spots it and fixes it

Own the economics

  • Build full visibility into cost per transaction: scheme fees, interchange, processor margin, FX, and where each one leaks

  • Own processor relationships day to day. Performance reviews, pricing negotiations, new partner evaluation

  • Model the trade-off between approval rate and cost by market, and make the call

  • Feed real payment economics into how we price merchants

Own the money movement

  • Settlement, reconciliation and payouts. Every penny accounted for, every break chased down

  • Reserve logic and settlement timing by merchant segment and risk profile

  • Work with treasury on funding, FX exposure and cash timing across our local companies

💥 Example Projects

  • Take a market from a 66% approval rate to 90% or better, and prove exactly which changes did it

  • Build the routing framework that optimises approval rate against cost, market by market

  • Renegotiate processor pricing using our own volume and performance data

  • Build the cost-per-transaction model across every processor and market, and find the basis points nobody is watching

  • Debug delays in settlement and fix them across engineering, operations and the processor

  • Design reserve and settlement logic for a new merchant segment and implement it

  • Cut chargeback rate through better fraud tooling and merchant policy

  • Evaluate and onboard a new processor for local acquiring in Latin America or Asia

  • Build the payments monitoring layer so anomalies find us, not the other way round

🧱 What We're Looking For

Ideal background:

  • A STEM or quantitative degree is strongly preferred - mathematics, physics, engineering, computer science, statistics, econometrics or similar.

  • 3 to 7+ years in payment operations, payment analytics, or a data or analytics role that moved into payments, at a processor, acquirer, or high-volume fintech (Adyen, Stripe, Checkout.com, Nuvei, Worldpay, Revolut, Wise, Dojo, Airwallex or similar)

  • Strong analytical skills — advanced Excel or Sheets, experience with BI tools, and the ability to build models and run analyses independently without waiting for a data team.

  • Bonus: experience at platforms that act as the legal reseller (Global-e, Digital River, Paddle), local acquiring outside Europe and the US, interchange and scheme fee economics, or a background in data science or quantitative consulting before payments

Signals we care about:

  • Ridiculous bias for action. You solve, you don't observe

  • Analytically strong and commercially sharp. You quantify the opportunity before you argue for it

  • Systems thinker who still does the work. You fix the transaction, then remove the reason it broke

  • Strong EQ. Processors, banks and merchants all need managing, often at the same time

  • Exceptionally hard working. You see work as a core part of your purpose

  • Fluent in ambiguity and chaos. Startups are not neat, this will be hard

  • Curious and resourceful. You can figure anything out

  • Clear, quantified achievements on your CV, not vague descriptions

What this role is not:

  • Not a payments strategy role without operational depth. You'll be in the dashboards daily

  • Not a pure analytics role. The analysis is the start, the change is the job

  • Not a narrow specialist seat. Payments here touches pricing, treasury, tax and product

  • Not for someone who needs defined processes and hierarchy to be effective

🚀 Why This Role Is Different

Most companies treat payments as a cost centre someone else manages. Here it is the product and the margin at the same time.

We take legal responsibility for our merchants' payments. That means a point of approval rate is real revenue for them and real evidence for us, and a basis point of cost is real profit. Very few people get to own that surface this early, with this much data and this little bureaucracy in the way.

We expect whoever is in this role to grow rapidly, and we'll back you every step of the way.

🦾 Outpost Team

Our team were leaders at Revolut, Airwallex, Adyen and Wayflyer, and we're backed by top-tier investors who have built or backed some of the world's leading fintechs.

🧾 What We Offer

  • Equity and salary in a well-funded startup

  • Ability to own your work and move fast

  • World-class training from operators who've scaled globally

  • A global mission with real impact

  • Low politics, high output

  • Chance to grow into a senior leadership role

  • A culture of builders, not talkers

🧭 Working Style

We work together in person in London 5 days a week. We believe the hardest problems are solved in the room.

Learn more

  1. Outpost Culture

Rattachement hiérarchique

• Encadre un à deux collaborateur(s) en charge du suivi quotidien de la métrologie sur l'ensemble des agences au

niveau national.

 

Mission principale

Le Responsable Métrologie garantit la conformité métrologique des équipements utilisés pour le transport des échantillons biologiques. Il est responsable de l'étude, du choix, de l'installation et du suivi des matériels permettant d'assurer le maintien de la chaîne de température réglementaire dans les véhicules frigorifiques. Il travaille en étroite collaboration avec le Responsable Parc Automobile, les Responsables Exploitation et les fournisseurs afin d'assurer la fiabilité des équipements et la qualité du transport.

 

PRINCIPALES RESPONSABILITES

Métrologie et maîtrise de la température

• Définir et mettre en œuvre la politique métrologique de l'entreprise.

• Garantir le respect des exigences réglementaires relatives au transport des échantillons biologiques.

• Assurer le suivi des équipements de mesure de température (capteurs, enregistreurs, sondes, etc.).

• Organiser les opérations de vérification, d'étalonnage et de qualification des équipements.

• Analyser les dérives et mettre en œuvre les actions correctives.

• Connaître et faire appliquer les référentiels applicables : ADR (matières biologiques catégorie B – UN3373), norme NF EN 12830 (enregistreurs de température) et NF X15-140 (étalonnage) / accréditation COFRAC.

 

Étude et déploiement des matériels

• Étudier les solutions techniques adaptées aux besoins de l'entreprise.

• Définir les spécifications techniques des équipements de transport sous température dirigée.

• Piloter l'installation des équipements frigorifiques et des systèmes de surveillance embarqués.

• Participer à la validation des nouveaux véhicules et matériels.

• Assurer la maîtrise et le suivi quotidien des plateformes de télésurveillance métrologique : deux solutions sont actuellement utilisées, l'une auprès d'un fournisseur couvrant la majorité du parc, l'autre auprès d'un second fournisseur actuellement en phase de test.

• Superviser l'outil interne propriétaire de l'entreprise, connecté aux équipements et générant des alertes en temps réel en cas de dérive de température.

• Remonter au service IT les besoins d'évolution et contribuer au développement et à l'amélioration continue de ces outils.

 

Coordination avec le parc automobile et l'exploitation

• Travailler avec le Responsable Parc pour planifier les installations, maintenances et immobilisations des véhicules.

• Coordonner avec l'Exploitation afin de limiter l'impact des interventions sur l'activité.

• Veiller à la disponibilité opérationnelle des véhicules conformes aux exigences de température.

• Assurer la sensibilisation et la formation des conducteurs aux bonnes pratiques de maintien de la chaîne du froid (chargement, fermeture, temps d'ouverture des portes, contrôles visuels).

• Tenir à jour un tableau de bord des non-conformités température et en assurer le suivi avec la facturation des pénalités associées.

• Assurer le reporting Qualité de Service auprès des Responsables Exploitation et du Commerce, afin d'assurer le suivi avec le client et de le rassurer sur les actions menées.

 

Gestion des fournisseurs

• Identifier et sélectionner les fournisseurs de matériels et de prestations métrologiques.

• Participer aux consultations, appels d'offres et négociations.

• Suivre les contrats de maintenance et les performances des prestataires.

• Assurer une veille technologique sur les équipements de transport sous température dirigée.

 

Qualité et amélioration continue

• Participer aux audits internes et externes.

• Élaborer les procédures et instructions de travail.

• Assurer le suivi des indicateurs de performance.

• Conduire les analyses de causes en cas de non-conformité.

• Proposer des actions d'amélioration continue.

• Représenter la métrologie lors des audits qualité menés directement par les clients laboratoires et préparer les éléments de preuve associés (certificats d'étalonnage, historiques de température).

 

ACTIVITES DECISIONNELLES

Le Responsable Métrologie est amené à :

• proposer les investissements en matériels de mesure et équipements frigorifiques ;

• valider les choix techniques des installations ;

• décider des actions à engager en cas de dérive de température ou de non-conformité ;

• arbitrer les solutions techniques en lien avec les contraintes opérationnelles ;

• sélectionner les fournisseurs dans le cadre de sa délégation.

• Toutes ces décisions devront être validées avec la Direction des Opérations.

 

RELATIONS FONCTIONNELLES

En interne

• Direction des Opérations

• Responsable Parc Automobile

• Responsable Exploitation

• Service Qualité

• Conducteurs

• Commerce (reporting Qualité de Service et suivi client lié aux non-conformités température).

En externe

• Fournisseurs d'équipements frigorifiques

• Prestataires de métrologie

• Clients laboratoires, dans le cadre des audits qualité et des demandes de justificatifs métrologiques.

 


PROFIL RECHERCHE

Formation

• Bac +3 minimum dans un domaine technique, qualité ou équivalent.

Expérience

• 2 à 3 ans d'expérience dans une fonction technique, qualité ou analytique similaire.

• Une expérience dans le transport de produits de santé, la logistique pharmaceutique, les laboratoires ou le transport sous température dirigée est appréciée mais non indispensable, ce poste étant nouvellement créé en interne.

Compétences techniques

• Capacité à étudier des cas techniques et à aider à la prise de décision.

• Connaissances de base en métrologie, étalonnage et gestion de la chaîne du froid.

• Connaissance de la réglementation applicable au transport d'échantillons biologiques (ADR – UN3373, NF X15-

140 / COFRAC).

• Analyse de données de température.

• Maîtrise des outils bureautiques et des logiciels de suivi métrologique.

Qualités personnelles

• Sens de l'organisation.

• Rigueur et méthode.

• Esprit d'analyse.

• Capacité de prise de décision.

• Aisance relationnelle.

• Force de proposition.

• Capacité à coordonner plusieurs interlocuteurs.

• Réactivité face aux situations d'urgence.

Objectifs du poste

• Garantir le maintien permanent de la chaîne de température des échantillons biologiques.

• Assurer la conformité réglementaire des équipements et des véhicules.

• Optimiser les investissements en matériels de métrologie et de transport frigorifique.

• Réduire les incidents liés aux écarts de température.

• Développer une collaboration efficace entre la métrologie, le parc automobile et l'exploitation afin de sécuriser les opérations de transport.

• Réduire les non-conformités température ayant un impact contractuel ou financier (pénalités, litiges de facturation), suivies via le tableau de bord dédié

  • Engineering partnership: understand architectural trade-offs, review technical approaches and unblock decisions. Write specs engineers actually want to read: clear, technical and opinionated.

  • Early-stage startup background.

At Vivid, we're on a mission to change how businesses and individuals manage their money across Europe.
