title: Senior Projectmanager
description:
Jouw Missie bij CCS

Geen dag is hetzelfde in deze rol. Samen met je collega’s zorg je ervoor dat wij succesvol onze softwareoplossingen bij klanten implementeren en dat onze klanten een excellente dienstverlening krijgen! Voor deze complexe systeemimplementaties en integratieprojecten zoeken we een zeer ervaren projectmanager. Je leert de verzekeringsbranche kennen en klanten helpen. Dat doe je niet alleen: je werkt samen met enthousiaste collega’s in een projectteam.

Voordelen voor de sollicitant

Als projectmanager krijg je veel verantwoordelijkheid, help je klanten en samen met je projectteam zet je mooie resultaten neer. Je kunt deels thuiswerken, deels op ons kantoor in Woerden en bij verschillende klanten in Nederland. Tijdelijk werken vanuit het buitenland kan ook dankzij onze workation-regeling (maximaal 30 dagen aaneengesloten per jaar).

Bij ons draait het om klantgericht werken én werkplezier. Daarom is er volop ruimte voor ontspanning en plezier. Denk aan een levend tafelvoetbaltoernooi, pubquiz en een bier- & wijnproeverij. Ons actieve Fun-team zorgt elke maand weer voor iets leuks.

En als je reislust nog niet is gestild met 25 vakantiedagen en een workation, dan kun je zelfs tot 20 extra verlofdagen bijkopen. Genoeg redenen om verder te lezen en te ontdekken of deze functie iets voor jou is, toch?


Een voorbeeld van je werkdag

Opstarten: Aan het begin van je werkdag heb je een dagstart met zowel collega’s als projectteamleden van de klant. Hierin bespreken jullie de voortgang, resultaten en eventuele hulpvragen.

Na de dagstart: Allereerst neem je nog wat tijd met een van de consultants naar aanleiding van de dagstart. Je coacht en begeleidt de consultant en helpt deze met een hulpvraag. Vervolgens ga je aan de slag met het opstellen van de voortgangsrapportage. Hiermee zorg je voor proactieve en transparante rapportage over het project aan de klant. De stuurgroep met de klant is volgende week, vandaag spreek je samen met de delivery manager deze stuurgroep voor. Wat zijn de belangrijkste punten voor de klant en voor CCS en hoe vliegen we die aan.

Na de lunch: Je checkt nog een paar tickets qua voortgang op het planboard, waarbij je de samenhang met de planning checkt. Vervolgens ga je naar de werksessie met het CCS projectmanagement guild. Hier werken jullie aan tickets om de CCS Prince2Agile projectmethodiek verder te verbeteren. Hierna heb je nog een afspraak met je collega van sales voor afstemming over een mogelijk vervolgproject bij de klant.

Wie jij bent

De ideale kandidaat beschikt over daadkracht, doorzettingsvermogen, enthousiasme en drive om projecten succesvol te leiden en verbeteringen door te voeren om te komen tot nog efficiëntere en klantgerichte projecten. Jij herkent jezelf in de volgende punten:

· Je wordt blij van projectmanagement en blijft kalm bij verschuivende prioriteiten;

· Je hebt bewezen ervaring met het succesvol uitvoeren van productsoftware-implementaties in een complexe, maar klantgerichte omgeving, binnen budget, planning en scope;

· Je hebt ruime ervaring met diverse projectmanagement en delivery methodieken, bij voorkeur een Prince2-, Ipma of PMI of Agile / scrum certificaat;

· Je vindt, net als wij, klanttevredenheid het uitgangspunt. Daarbij ben je in staat om de klantverwachtingen helder te analyseren, te managen en actief bij te sturen waar nodig;

· Je beheerst de Nederlandse en Engelse taal uitstekend in woord en geschrift;

· Jouw persoonlijkheid kenmerkt zich door: gestructureerd, motiverend, communicatief sterk, duidelijk, open, tikje eigenwijs, enthousiast, relativerend, creatief en pragmatisch;

· Je haalt energie uit het opstellen en bewaken van planningen, analyseren van gegevens en opstellen van duidelijke, gestructureerde rapportages en presentaties;

· Je hebt minimaal een afgeronde bachelor, bij voorkeur richting bedrijfskunde, bedrijfseconomie en/of informatica.

Wat bieden wij jou?

Naast de genoemde leuke functie binnen een groeiend en innovatief bedrijf bieden wij:

· Salaris: We bieden je een salaris tussen € 5.590 en € 7.958 per maand (o.b.v. 40 uur per week), afhankelijk van je ervaring en kennis;

· Middelen: Leaseauto, laptop, telefoon;

· Werkdagen: Je bent minimaal 4 dagen per week beschikbaar, al heeft 5 dagen onze voorkeur;

· Vergoeding voor thuiswerken: Je kunt gedeeltelijk thuiswerken en krijgt een onkostenvergoeding van € 2,40 per thuiswerkdag. Ook krijg je een budget van € 750,- om thuis een ergonomische werkplek in te richten;

· Workation: Je kunt tot 30 dagen aaneengesloten per jaar vanuit het buitenland werken;

· Leuke teamactiviteiten: Leer je collega’s beter kennen door deel te nemen aan maandelijkse evenementen georganiseerd door ons energieke Fun-team, zoals een pubquiz, Zomer BBQ, wine & beer tastings en movie night;

· Vakantiedagen: Je krijgt 25 vakantiedagen en de mogelijkheid om maximaal 20 extra dagen bij te kopen;

· Groei en ontwikkeling: De mogelijkheid om je vaardigheden en verantwoordelijkheden te ontwikkelen binnen de functie, middels opleidingen en Linkedin learning, of door te stromen naar een van de andere functies binnen CCS;

· Vakantiegeld: Jaarlijks 8,33%;

· Voordelen: Je krijgt een aantrekkelijke pensioenregeling met een lage eigen bijdrage en kunt gebruikmaken van collectieve verzekeringen met korting. Ook is er een bedrijfsfitnessregeling voor een gezonde levensstijl en een fietsregeling voor duurzaam vervoer.

Waarom CCS?

Omdat wij geloven dat werk meer is dan een baan. Het is een plek waar je jezelf kunt zijn, impact kunt maken en kunt groeien. Het is een omgeving waar je wordt geïnspireerd om het beste uit jezelf te halen en samen te werken aan een duurzame toekomst. Kom bij ons en ontdek wat er mogelijk is als je een carrière bouwt vol passie, plezier en betekenis. Jij bent de ontbrekende schakel in ons team. Word onderdeel van ons verhaal. 🚀

Role summary

How much numerical precision does an LLM need, and where in the model architecture does it matter most? When does quantization improve runtime, and what does it cost in model quality?

We're looking for a motivated working student to help turn these questions into experiments and experiments into maintainable code. You'll explore optimization methods and build reusable evaluation tooling.   • Build reproducible tooling: Automate evaluations, track configurations and results, and make experiments accessible to engineers and AI agents.
  • Measure runtime performance: Characterize latency, throughput, and memory usage to understand bottlenecks under different deployment scenarios.

A first project could involve exploring the quality–performance Pareto frontier of a Qwen or LlaMa model. You'll experiment with 16-bit, 8-bit, and 4-bit quantization configurations to find the best runtime-quality tradeoff.

  • Clear communication and the ability to present experimental findings and technical tradeoffs to the team.

Strong pluses: experience with quantization, LLM evaluation, performance profiling, or inference optimization.

Put your university knowledge into practice with leading open-source LLMs, deepen your understanding of quantization and inference optimization, and build skills in experimental design, software engineering, and AI coding tools. title: Senior Solutions Architect | Germany | Remote
Senior Frontend Engineer
description:
About Heidi Systems

Heidi Systems builds the energy OS for real estate. We help property managers and owners get their heating, water and electricity meters online, see consumption in real time and run the yearly utility billing without paper, Excel and site visits.

Submetering in Germany is still mostly analog. Meters get read by hand, data sits in PDFs, and tenants see their consumption once a year. We change that end to end: we install the meters and gateways in the building, collect the data and build the web platform property managers work in.

We're a small team in Berlin. Product and engineering work directly with the founders, and what you ship lands with real customers fast.

The role

We're looking for a best-in-class frontend engineer. Someone whose code other engineers learn from.

You'll be our senior frontend engineer and own the web platform end to end: architecture, code quality and the day-to-day experience of the property managers using it.

The platform is a SvelteKit and TypeScript app. It shows consumption data per building and unit, flags anomalies, manages tenants and owners, and produces the documents for the yearly billing. A lot of it is data-heavy UI, and it has to be right, because the numbers end up on invoices.

You'll work closely with our backend engineers and the founders, and you'll help onboard and mentor junior developers and interns as the team grows.

What you'll do

  • Own the frontend architecture of our SvelteKit app: routing, load functions, SSR, state and how we talk to the backend via oRPC

  • Ship features end to end, from a rough idea with the founders to production, often before the design is final

  • Build the data-heavy parts of the product: consumption dashboards, notification rules, tenant and owner management, billing documents

  • Set up and maintain our component library on Tailwind and DaisyUI so the UI stays consistent as we add features

  • Raise the bar on quality: strict TypeScript, Vitest coverage, code reviews, a sane PR flow

  • Shape the API contract together with backend (types, Zod schemas, error handling) so frontend and backend stay in sync

  • Mentor juniors and interns through reviews and pairing

What you bring

  • 5+ years of professional frontend experience, ideally at startups or other fast-moving product teams

  • 2+ years building production apps with Svelte and SvelteKit, with a deep understanding of its reactivity model, stores, lifecycle, routing, load functions and SSR

  • Strong TypeScript: strict mode, generics, utility types, and the judgment to know when types help and when they get in the way

  • Hands-on with Tailwind CSS (DaisyUI is a plus)

  • Experience with RPC-style APIs (oRPC, tRPC or similar) and typed contracts between frontend and backend

  • Testing as a habit: Vitest, JSDom or comparable tooling

  • Comfortable in a Unix environment (Linux or macOS), with Git, branches and PRs

  • You've made architecture decisions on a real product and can explain the trade-offs

  • You work well with little oversight and ship in small, frequent steps

  • Fluent English, written and spoken

  • You're in Berlin or willing to move, and you're in our office 2 to 3 days a week

How we work

  • Hybrid in Berlin. You're in the office 2 to 3 days a week. That's fixed. The rest of the week you work from wherever you like.

  • Short paths. You talk to the founders directly, most decisions take one call.

  • Real ownership. The frontend is yours to shape, and you'll set many of the standards the team builds on.

  • Real impact. Your work runs in buildings across Germany and makes energy use visible where people live.

  • Room to grow with the company as the engineering team gets bigger.

Your next steps

If you match most of these requirements and are ready to help digitize the building sector, we encourage you to apply. You will join a growing team where your work directly shapes the future of energy management in real estate.

description:
Mapbox is the leading real-time location platform for a new generation of location-aware businesses. Mapbox is the only platform that equips organizations with the full set of tools to power the navigation of people, packages, and vehicles everywhere. More than 4 million registered developers have chosen Mapbox because of the platform’s flexibility, security and privacy compliance. Organizations use Mapbox applications, data, SDKs and APIs to create customized and immersive experiences that delight their customers. 

What you'll do

This role is scoped by skill rather than by product. The problems below span multiple departments and show up across our Search and Places data work, our Location and Navigation Intelligence work, and the Platform work that makes Mapbox usable by agents. You'll be hired into one specific team or product area, but you'll work across teams where your expertise meets the highest-priority AI problems. You should expect to move between teams and tech stacks as the work demands.

At this level you own the technical design and delivery of a multi-component AI system, and you are accountable for the quality of what ships in your area.

In this role, you will:

  • Define how the products you own should work, build a measurement framework for it, and build evaluation systems for non-deterministic behavior. Formulate hypotheses around the products we build and seek the signal needed to validate them. Define what a correct result is for a given input and state, determine whether to assemble datasets from real usage or hand-written cases, and gate changes on regression results.

  • Run continuous evaluation of the products we build, whether APIs, SDKs, data representations, or reference applications, from the position of the end user, whether developer, agent, or consumer. Assess the gaps such as misuse of parameters or integration anti-patterns, recommend the fixes, and make sure they land.

  • Own the MVP against an agreed north star technical design, and balance technical perfection against shipping useful increments.

  • Build data pipelines and the tooling around them: ingestion, conflation, entity resolution, quality checks, and the batch and streaming jobs that keep a large dataset current.

  • Track and pull external datasets, models, and benchmarks from published research and open-source releases. Evaluate what fits the problem and constraints , and decide when to adopt what exists versus build your own.

  • Design feedback loops so that using a product generates data that improves it. Instrument systems so failures arrive with enough context to reproduce, then turn the recurring ones into evaluation cases.

  • Design the boundary between a model and the tools it calls. Build or improve the model harness, decide what the model handles, what it delegates, and how to keep it working from the state it actually fetched.

  • Work to a latency and cost target per request: streaming, partial results, caching, model routing, prompt structure.

  • Build the internal harnesses and tools (CLI, MCP, and others) your team needs to iterate quickly, and share the parts that generalize with other teams.

  • Raise the bar on your team through code and design review, and bring other engineers up on eval practice.

  • Some of the technical questions in this area are still open. You will help answer them.

  • Participate in an on-call rotation to ensure our systems remain available to customers 24/7. Team members alternate as the on-call primary responder, which may require immediate response outside normal working hours, including weekends.

  • Bachelors degree in STEM discipline and 5+ years of software engineering experience, with production ownership of services, pipelines, or SDKs.

  • Experience diagnosing latency in a distributed request path.

  • Comfort with ambiguity, and the judgment to ship something narrow that works while the general solution is still unclear.

  • Clear written communication. Mapbox is distributed across time zones and we make most decisions in documents and Slack.

  • Public API or SDK design experience, particularly for developers you never talk to.

  • Experience building against MCP or similar tool transports.

  • Experience operating a product through its first external integrations, where the customer finds the gaps before you do.

Your Role

Zip is looking for a Senior Director of EMEA Commercial Sales to lead and scale our Commercial business across Europe.

This is a second-line leadership role. You will initially lead two frontline Commercial Sales Managers and, through them, a growing team of Account Executives. As Zip expands across Europe, you will build the leadership structure, sales capacity, and go-to-market approach required to capture that opportunity.

Your leverage comes through your managers, but this is not a role for someone who operates from a distance. You will stay close to the business: understanding the pipeline, inspecting deals, helping your managers improve their teams, and personally getting involved in the opportunities where your experience can change the outcome.

You will own the performance of EMEA Commercial end to end: the number, pipeline, forecast, talent, geographic expansion, and operating rhythm of the segment.

Commercial is already an important part of Zip's EMEA business. The opportunity now is to turn it into a scaled, predictable growth engine across the region.

  • Own EMEA Commercial performance. Deliver quarterly and annual new-business revenue targets through the frontline managers and Account Executives who report into your organization.

  • Build and develop exceptional frontline managers. Coach your leaders on pipeline management, forecasting, deal inspection, rep development, and performance management. Hold them accountable for running their businesses with the same rigor you bring to yours.

  • Scale Commercial across Europe. Determine where and when to add coverage as Zip expands into new countries and markets, and build the teams and leadership required to win locally without creating unnecessary complexity.

  • Represent the Commercial business internally. Provide clear, credible reporting on performance, pipeline, forecast, market dynamics, competitive trends, and the investments required to continue scaling.

gravity9 is recruiting Java engineers and architects for a portfolio of engagements across UK central government. These are large-scale, data-intensive modernisation programmes: replacing legacy systems that carry statutory weight, decomposing monoliths that serve millions of users, and building secure data platforms where access control and auditability are first-class architectural concerns rather than late additions.

We are hiring across two overlapping profiles — Senior Java Developer and Application / Migration Architect — and expect most people to move between programmes as engagements start and complete. Several of these are hands-on architect roles: you will own design decisions and also write production code

The kind of work

The following are representative of current and upcoming engagements. Individual roles will draw on some of this, not all of it — we are more interested in engineers who can work confidently at the intersection of Java and data than in a checklist match against any one programme.

Secure data catalogue and access-control platform

A greenfield metadata catalogue acting as a federated index over data held across independent domains, so that authorised parties can locate and retrieve data the catalogue itself never holds. The work includes designing an attribute-based access control model over attributes such as clearance, nationality, organisational unit and compartment; enforcing those policies inside the database query path rather than filtering results afterwards; application-layer encryption with externally managed keys; hybrid lexical and semantic search with access filtering applied before candidate retrieval rather than after it; and a tamper-evident audit trail that can reconstruct why a given record was returned, redacted or withheld.

Real-time decision-support data architecture

Replacing point-to-point integration across a multi-vendor estate with a microservices architecture and a common data layer, so that operational data flows in near real time instead of over days. The work includes target-state architecture and decision records, change-data-capture ingest pipelines from upstream data services, ontology and mapping-layer design across suppliers with competing data models, separation of system, reference and insight data classes including time-series, and deployment topologies spanning cloud-hosted services down to constrained edge hardware.

Legacy-to-document-model migration at national scale

Migrating hundreds of millions of records and tens of terabytes of XML out of a legacy relational platform into a sharded document store, in support of a COBOL-to-Java microservices rewrite. The work includes a configuration-driven XML-to-JSON transformation framework backed by a versioned schema registry — twenty years of history, multiple record types and continual schema and semantic drift; CDC and streaming pipelines, or a checkpointed parallel bulk-extract alternative; a field-level mapping validation and reconciliation framework robust enough to stand up to audit; a replay and failure-diagnostics harness with dead-letter routing and idempotent re-runs; and repeated dress rehearsals toward a single cutover window with no dual running.

Monolith decomposition and data-ownership migration

Breaking a distributed monolith of well over a hundred Java services sharing a handful of database clusters into domain-owned services — moving from borrowed data to owned data without reintroducing hidden coupling. The work includes bounded-context analysis to establish which domain genuinely owns which collections, in-place data remodelling ahead of any physical move, a data-access facade with feature-flagged per-request routing between old and new stores, dual-write / backfill / reconcile / read-switch cutover lifecycles with a defined rollback at every step, cluster-to-cluster streaming and live migration tooling, and automated parallel-run and diff-on-read testing.

What you will be doing

Emphasis varies by role and programme, but MongoDB is the common thread. Every one of these engagements involves modelling for it, migrating onto it, or building on top of it, and genuine depth here is what most differentiates candidates.

•      Design and implement MongoDB document models, aggregation pipelines, indexing and sharding strategies, and integrate them cleanly into Java service layers rather than through a leaky abstraction

•      Write the tests: unit, integration, golden-record fixtures, parallel-run reconciliation, and load and stress harnesses that prove performance under realistic volumes

•      Model relational, XML or other legacy schemas onto MongoDB document models, handling schema and semantic drift through versioned, configuration-driven mappings rather than forked code

•      Design and prove cutover mechanisms — dual-write, backfill, reconcile, read-switch, rollback — for systems where a failed migration is not an acceptable outcome

•      Build validation and reconciliation tooling that satisfies audit: completeness, field-level fidelity, and query-level equivalence between old and new

Security, access control and assurance

•      Design and implement attribute- or role-based access control models, including enforcement at the data layer and policy administration

•      Work with application-layer and field-level encryption — MongoDB client-side field level and queryable encryption, and externally managed key material

•      Support knowledge transfer and upskilling of client teams — on these programmes enablement is a deliverable, not an afterthought

•      Use AI-assisted engineering tooling as part of normal delivery, within the constraints client security policy sets


Essential

•      Data-intensive systems — demonstrable experience of pipelines, migrations or integrations at meaningful scale, and sound reasoning about throughput, ordering, idempotency and failure recovery

•      API design — clean, well-documented REST interfaces suitable for integration by multiple consuming systems

•      Testing — genuine automated testing discipline, plus practical experience of load and stress testing against realistic volumes

•      Infrastructure and deployment — Terraform or equivalent infrastructure as code, containerised deployment on Kubernetes, and AWS or a comparable cloud

•      Communication — able to write clear design documentation and hold your own in a client design authority or architecture review

•      UK resident, and either holding current UK SC clearance or clearly eligible to obtain it

For architect-level roles we additionally expect:

Working context

title: Communications Lead
description:
Who we are

Yubo is the Social Discovery app to make new friends and hang out online. By eliminating likes and follows, we empower our users to create genuine connections and show up as their true selves.

We've pioneered a new way for Gen Z to socialize online, and with millions of active users, our goal is to redefine how we connect today and tomorrow.

Our team is international, multicultural and deeply committed to its mission. As the leading platform to socialize online, we have a special responsibility to build a safe digital space for our community. Safety is embedded in our DNA, and our proactive approach focuses on user protection, support, and education.

Join us in this exciting journey and help us shape the future of social interactions!

About this role

Yubo doesn't have a PR team yet, and that's exactly why this role exists: to build one from scratch and help Yubo become culturally relevant, resilient to reputational bumps, and a real driver of growth.

It's a rare chance to shape a PR function from day one inside a fast-moving global tech company. You'll design how it works, lead our agency partner, and craft the stories, moments and relationships that make people pay attention to Yubo. The role covers everyday consumer stories, corporate communications, and handling sensitive issues or crises when they arise. To start, you'll focus on the US, UK and France, with room to grow from there.

You'll report to the Director of Brand & Communications and work closely with teams across the business, especially Brand, Product, Data, Trust & Safety and Legal. You'll own the relationship with our PR agency, making sure they feel like a true extension of the team, and you'll help set up the habits and processes that make PR part of how Yubo works day to day.

This is a freelance role on a 6-month contract, with a target start in Q4 2026.

Your responsibilites

Set up how PR works at Yubo

  • Build PR operations and onboard Yubo's PR agency, setting clear ways to spot stories, check facts, and turn insight into coverage.

  • Dig into Yubo's data to find trends and stories worth telling.

  • Build a simple way to report on PR performance, linking coverage and sentiment to awareness and growth.

  • Review and embed Yubo's Crisis Comms Playbook.

Plan and run the PR agenda

  • Build Yubo's 2027 PR calendar and strategy, balancing campaigns, cultural moments, and day-to-day press activity.

  • Lead proactive and reactive media relations so Yubo speaks with a clear, consistent voice.

  • Spot and activate cultural moments through PR, research, events, creator partnerships and other earned activity.

  • Team up with Product and Data to build proof points and stories that show what Yubo means to people.

Look after Yubo's reputation

  • Advise senior leaders on reputational opportunities and risks.

  • Support corporate communications and reactive issues management when needed.

  • Work with Trust & Safety and Legal so Yubo talks about sensitive topics responsibly.

  • Help rally the right people internally when a crisis hits.

Who you are

You're a proactive PR lead with sharp cultural instincts and a track record of creating stories that genuinely earn attention, not just promote launches.

You'll bring:

  • Solid PR experience, with real results to show from leading a function or campaign.

  • A good read on Gen-Z culture and how 18 to 24 year-olds socialise and engage online.

  • Experience turning insight and data into media stories, including digging into data yourself to find the angle.

  • A track record of using different levers to earn attention: influencers, experts, events, activations, research, stunts.

  • Experience managing and getting the best out of an external PR agency.

  • Good judgement under pressure, with experience in issues or crisis communications.

  • Strong writing and speaking skills, comfortable with both consumer storytelling and sensitive corporate messaging.

  • The ability to influence cross-functional teams and senior stakeholders.

  • A self-starter mindset, with examples of building something from the ground up.

Nice to have, but don't let that stop you:

  • Experience in high-growth tech, consumer apps, youth culture, media, entertainment or lifestyle.

  • Experience in the US market, including relationships with US media and journalists.

Within a month, you will

  • Get familiar with Yubo's product, mission and community, and where our communications and reputation stand today.

  • Meet key people across Brand, Product, Data, Trust & Safety and Legal.

  • Start onboarding our PR agency and reviewing the Crisis Comms Playbook.

Within 3 months, you will

  • Have set up solid working habits with the PR agency and cross-functional teams.

  • Be well into building the 2027 PR strategy, calendar and measurement framework.

  • Have embedded the Crisis Comms Playbook and be actively building relationships with consumer, culture, lifestyle, tech and business media.

Within 6 months, you will

  • Have delivered Yubo's finished 2027 PR strategy and calendar.

  • Have landed our first standout data- and culture-led stories in top-tier media, backed by a working way to measure PR performance.

  • Have wrapped up the agency onboarding and defined the role of creators, experts, events and activations in Yubo's communications, leaving a solid foundation for what's next.

The recruitment process

  • A first introductory call with Nicolas, Talent Acquisition

  • A case study with Alex, our Brand Director.

Our approach to privacy & safety

As part of your role, you may handle tools and features involving personal data. We expect all employees to demonstrate strong awareness of privacy and safety issues, and to actively support our Privacy & Safety by Design efforts.

Join Yubo and help shape the future of Social Discovery while enjoying a culture that values flexibility, well-being, and impact.

 

Here’s how we live our mission every day:

You own the impact: Step up, adapt, and make it matter

Unconventionally Smart: Hack with intent, borrow smart, build better

Be Bold & Resilient: Raise your head, break barriers, keep moving forward

One team, one mission: No egos, no passengers, just shared wins

 

Trust & Flexibility: Our hybrid model calls for only two office days a month; the rest is up to the rhythm that works best for you.

 

Enjoy Top-notch Benefits

Culture is central at Yubo, hence the numerous benefits:

Cool Workplace: enjoy our amazing Parisian office and our many hybrid work options

Team Activities: participate in get-togethers, events, and team-building activities

Family-Friendly: we support parents with childcare options and family-friendly policies

Wellness Programs: benefit from comprehensive health insurance, wellness programs, sports classes, and mental well-being initiatives

title: Infrastructure Engineer (ML Systems) - Paris
description:
You’ll own the GPU compute that powers our model training, evaluation and serving systems.

This role sits in our Infrastructure team, which works at the lowest layers of our stack, from Kubernetes down to the GPU hardware. You’ll run the clusters, GPUs and schedulers that our research, product and platform teams depend on, and manage the capacity we buy from our cloud providers.

What success looks like

Success is measured by how well we use our GPUs: keeping production reliable and improving the performance of our training and serving stack.

What you’ll be doing

  • Running Kubernetes clusters for GPU training and inference

  • Improving how GPU work is scheduled and placed

  • Detecting, draining and repairing unhealthy GPU nodes

  • Managing capacity with our cloud providers

  • Debugging failures in GPUs, Linux, storage and networking

The first year

By month 3, you’ll be handling a share of cluster incidents on your own and will have shipped one change to scheduling or node health, such as automatically detecting and draining unhealthy GPU nodes. By month 6, you’ll own one part of the compute layer outright: scheduling and placement, node health and repair, or capacity and new regions. By month 12, you’ll be responsible for a globally distributed GPU system that shifts capacity between training and inference as needs change.

Who you’ll work with

Your hiring manager is our VP of Engineering. Day to day, you’ll work with the Platform Infrastructure team, the research and product teams who use our compute, and our cloud providers and other vendors.

What we think it takes

You’re likely a good fit if you:

  • Have built and run GPU workloads on Kubernetes

  • Could design a GPU cluster for training and online RL from scratch

  • Debug confidently at the OS layer and below (Linux, GPU drivers, networking and storage)

  • Write strong Python

It’s a plus if you’ve worked as an SRE or infrastructure engineer, or have used:

  • Slurm

  • Kubernetes scheduling and autoscaling tools such as Kueue or Karpenter

  • Multi-cloud orchestration tools such as SkyPilot

  • AWS services such as EKS or SageMaker HyperPod

  • High-performance interconnects and collective communication libraries such as EFA, InfiniBand, NCCL or Open MPI

  • Terraform

You don’t need ML research experience. If you match most of this but not every point, please apply.

How we hire

Four stages, about three hours in total: a 30-minute call with our Talent team, a 60-minute coding interview, a 60-minute system design interview and a closing 30-minute conversation with our VP of Engineering. The coding and system design interviews are modelled on real-world problems you’d face in this role.

Practicalities

The role is hybrid, with three days a week in our Paris or London office and occasional travel between the two. We offer a competitive package.

title: Product Designer - Paris

As a Product Designer, you'll work on the H Platform, where our users create and run agentic AI workflows powered by our models. Nobody has written the playbook for designing these experiences yet. Our next stage is making the platform truly useful for its users and levelling it up, in design as much as in technology, and you'll build the product experiences that deliver real value in organisations.

At H Company, we believe AI should take action in the real world, and our mission is to make agentic AI genuinely useful for large organisations. We're pioneers in computer use: our own vision-language models power agents that see, click and type their way through the software businesses already run, with no integrations or rebuilds, and we own the whole stack, from research and models to the products built on top of them.

What you'll be doing

  • Talking to our users constantly to understand their needs and figure out what will make the platform truly useful for them.

  • Turning those insights into research and explorations, looking at problems from different angles before settling on a direction.

  • Picking the right tool for each task: a Figma design, a prototype, or a small PR when a quick change is the fastest way to ship.

  • Testing what you build with users, measuring its impact (A/B testing, user interviews, users daily use data...) and iterating quickly based on what you learn.

  • Shaping the roadmap together with the whole team, engineers and PMs alike.

Who you'll work with

The role sits in our Product team, which is responsible for product direction, strategy and design. You'll join the product designer who owns design and UX today, and work closely with product, engineering and forward deployed engineers.

What we think it takes

Above all, we want someone who cares deeply about users, has great product taste and can explain it, moves fast while keeping quality high, leaves their ego at the door and welcomes feedback.

Likely a good fit if you

  • Have 5+ years of experience as a Product Designer at tech companies.

  • Have excellent UX, UI and interaction design skills, and can make complex, technical flows, like building and running AI agent workflows, feel simple and intuitive.

  • Have a portfolio that shows your latest work.

  • Have hands-on experience running user tests and A/B tests.

  • Know when a proven solution is good enough and when a problem deserves something new.

  • Have designed complex data or ML/AI-driven products: you know how to make complex systems understandable and how to design for AI behaviour that isn't always predictable, building trust and keeping users in control.

  • Are comfortable in technical discussions: you can dig into constraints and trade-offs with engineers and ramp up quickly on technical topics to discuss them with our researchers and more technical engineers.

  • Are fluent in Figma.

  • Can work within a design system and contribute to it.

Stronger still if you

title: Research Lead, Predictive Oncology
description:
About Orakl Oncology

At Orakl Oncology, we combine patient-derived tumor models, experimental drug screening and computational modelling to improve oncology drug development. Our research brings together functional treatment-response measurements, molecular profiles and clinical information where available, creating opportunities to investigate how experimental responses translate into patient outcomes. Our platforms are designed to help anticipate clinical trial outcomes, evaluate therapies and identify new therapeutic opportunities.

Our mission is simple yet ambitious: to bring more effective treatments to patients who need them and to make drug development smarter, faster, and more personalised. We collaborate with top hospitals, research institutes, and pharmaceutical companies worldwide. Backed by leading investors, we are a fast-growing, mission-driven startup at the intersection of science and technology.

About the Role

We are looking for a Research Lead - Predictive Oncology, to build and lead a research programme to improve the translational capabilities of Orakl Oncology’s platform, and to provide the scientific backbone of O-Predict, Orakl’s predictive solutions.

You will own O-Predict's long-term scientific roadmap, choose the questions we pursue, and lead the work needed to answer them. The opportunity combines access to Orakl's experimental and molecular data, clinical information where available, and the ability to shape future data generation with our experimental and clinical collaborators.

This is a hands-on scientific leadership role. You will develop and test methods, mentor contributors, and build a coherent body of research with a recognisable scientific contribution. Publications, presentations and external collaborations will be integral outputs of that programme.

You will work closely with the CTO and our Data Science, Computational Biology, experimental, product and engineering colleagues. Your research will establish which predictions are reliable, identify their limitations, and inform how O-Predict can support drug-development decisions.

The role is suited to a researcher ready to take ownership of an independent programme within a collaborative company, including an emerging research leader with a strong record of original work.

What You'll Do

Own O-Predict's long-term research roadmap: define and maintain a 2-year scientific agenda, translated into a prioritised 12-month execution plan. Identify the key uncertainties, research hypotheses, data requirements, dependencies and resources; set milestones and explicit criteria for continuing, redirecting or stopping projects. Review priorities with the CTO as evidence and company needs evolve.

Lead R&D execution: take research programmes from question formulation through method development, validation and interpretation. Coordinate agreed contributions across Data Science, Computational Biology and experimental teams, establish project ownership, run scientific reviews, resolve blockers and mentor researchers. Remain hands-on in the analyses and modelling decisions that determine scientific quality.

Shape future data generation: identify the experiments, measurements and cohorts that would resolve important scientific uncertainties. Co-design these studies with experimental and clinical colleagues, prioritise them within the agreed research allocation, and use the results to test and revise your hypotheses.

Advance O-Predict's predictive capabilities: investigate how drug screening, patient-derived models, molecular and clinical data can improve treatment-response and trial-outcome predictions. Assess extensions to new cohorts, indications and therapeutic settings, specifying the evidence needed before extending claims.

Own the validation strategy: define relevant endpoints, external baselines and evaluation protocols. Lead independent and prospective validation plans with clinical and experimental collaborators, and document both performance and failure modes.

Connect research to product development: work with product and engineering colleagues to translate promising findings into reproducible methods and clearly documented scientific requirements. Define the evidence needed for transfer into O-Predict and assess feasibility, expected value and limitations.

Lead publications and scientific materials: build a publication and conference plan around the research roadmap. Lead manuscripts from analysis and figures through submission and reviewer responses, with contributions distributed across the research team. Produce abstracts, posters, talks and methods notes; provide scientific direction and review for partner evidence decks.

Build substantive scientific collaborations: work directly with clinical investigators and quantitative researchers to formulate questions, co-design studies, access complementary expertise and pursue independent validation opportunities. Represent O-Predict at relevant oncology and computational conferences, present your team's research, and turn scientific discussions into joint projects and publications.

Run publication governance: coordinate authorship and co-author review with hospital and pharmaceutical partners, track contractual publication and acknowledgement obligations, and align disclosure with confidentiality, patient-data permissions and intellectual-property considerations.

Minimum Qualifications

  • PhD, PharmD, MD, or MSc with an equivalent research record in a quantitative or biomedical discipline relevant to predictive oncology.

  • Demonstrated ownership of a research programme: you have formulated a scientific agenda, prioritised competing questions and led projects from initial hypothesis to validated findings.

  • Experience leading and mentoring scientific contributors, including coordinating work across disciplines and critically reviewing others' methods and conclusions.

  • A strong publication record in translational oncology, computational biology, biostatistics and/or ML for health, with clear intellectual and analytical contributions.

  • Hands-on proficiency in Python and SQL: you can work with internal data and libraries, develop and evaluate methods, and produce reproducible analyses and figures.

  • Strong grounding in statistical inference, predictive modelling and study design; able to challenge biological assumptions and machine-learning evaluations.

  • Excellent scientific writing and oral communication in English, including manuscripts, scientific presentations and substantive discussions with external researchers.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience leading R&D in a biotech, health technology or translational research setting, with responsibility for milestones and resource planning.

  • Experience translating research methods into a predictive product or decision-support workflow.

  • Familiarity with patient-derived models, drug sensitivity assays, clinical trial design and oncology endpoints.

  • Experience with independent or prospective validation, multimodal data integration, survival modelling, or pharmacological modelling.

  • Experience establishing academic or clinical collaborations and publishing with pharmaceutical partners.

  • Familiarity with appropriate reporting standards and reproducibility practices, including protocol registration and code and data availability statements.

  • Experience presenting research at oncology or computational conferences and maintaining an active scientific network.

Who You Are

  • A scientific owner: you turn an ambitious objective into a focused research agenda and make explicit choices about what deserves the team's time.

  • A hands-on leader: you develop others while staying close enough to the data and code to challenge results and solve difficult problems.

  • Rigorous and intellectually honest: you seek evidence that could disprove your hypotheses, distinguish exploratory findings from validated claims, and report limitations clearly.

  • Curious across disciplines: you connect experimental biology, clinical questions and quantitative methods.

  • An effective collaborator: you build productive relationships, navigate scientific disagreement and turn external discussions into research progress.

Why Join Orakl

  • Own a research programme with a clear scientific identity. Shape O-Predict's direction and build a body of work around the translation of experimental treatment responses into clinical predictions.

  • Study a distinctive combination of data. Bring together patient-derived tumor models, functional drug screening and molecular profiles, incorporating clinical information where available. Explore questions that require these modalities to be studied together.

  • Help decide what gets measured next. Work with experimental and clinical colleagues to design new studies that test your ideas and address the limitations of existing data.

  • Work across disciplines every day. Develop methods alongside the scientists generating the measurements, the engineers supporting their use, and collaborators who understand the clinical questions.

  • Build your scientific reputation. Lead original research, manuscripts and conference contributions, and develop sustained collaborations around your programme.

  • Connect discoveries to consequential decisions. Develop and validate methods intended to inform therapy evaluation and clinical development, with a clear account of what the evidence does and does not support.

  • Grow as a research leader. Mentor researchers and help shape the capabilities and future team needed to deliver the programme.

Interview Process

  1. HR Call: Align on motivation, role scope and expectations.

  2. Scientific Deep Dive: Discuss a research programme you led: the questions you chose, your own technical contributions, validation decisions, team leadership and published outcomes. We will share a confidential scientific briefing on O-Predict's current evidence, available data and open questions so you can assess the opportunity.

  3. Research Strategy and Analysis Discussion: Using a bounded, representative evidence package, discuss research priorities and a validation plan, critique an analysis, and outline how you would communicate the findings. Meet the experimental and computational colleagues you would work with and discuss the studies you would want to pursue.

  4. Reference Call: Speak with one or two close collaborators who can assess scientific judgement, research ownership and leadership.

  5. Founder Interview: Discuss O-Predict's scientific direction, decision-making responsibilities, research resources, publication arrangements and mutual ambitions.

Why join now

title: Director of rewards, data & analytics
description:
Hi, we’re Back Market.

We’re here to help make tech reliable, affordable, and better than new. We're a global marketplace for refurbished devices, helping lower our collective environmental impact by providing trustworthy, affordable tech with 92% less carbon emissions than new.

Yep, you read that right. Turns out refurbished tech is way better for the planet than new. In fact, With every device purchased on Back Market, our positive impact on the planet grows. From our Customer Care representatives to our software engineer, every individual at Back Market cuts the planet — and consumers — a break. Our mission is simple: to do more with what we already have.

Are you ready to join us?

As Director, Rewards & Data, you make pay, equity, benefits, workforce costs and People data work as one decision system

You join the People Leadership Team and lead a team of three experts (Compensation; People Data & HR Cockpit; Cost Control & Workforce Planning), plus our Benefits and Immigration providers.

Your mandate has two sides:

  • Total Rewards — design and run a reward system (compensation, stock options and BSPCE, benefits, international mobility) that is competitive, fair, transparent and financially sustainable.

  • People data and workforce economics — give leadership a reliable, shared view of headcount, people costs and workforce trends, and turn it into recommendations before decisions are made.

What you'll do

Build and lead the hub

  • Set the hub's vision, roadmap and ways of working; lead and grow your three experts and manage specialist providers with clear accountability.

  • Define who decides what with People Partners, Finance, Legal, Payroll and People Operations & Tech, and shape our People strategy as a member of the People Leadership Team.

Own Total Rewards and compensation

  • Own our reward philosophy and global compensation framework: job architecture, salary ranges, benchmarking and pay positioning.

  • Lead the annual compensation review with Finance, and advise executives and People Partners on offers, promotions, retention and organisational changes.

  • Monitor internal equity and market competitiveness, and get Back Market ready for the EU Pay Transparency Directive.

Steer our equity programmes (stock options and BSPCE)

  • Own equity principles, governance and the role of equity in total compensation, with Finance and Legal.

  • Guarantee a reliable, documented and auditable lifecycle from grant to exit, and help employees understand and value their equity.

Turn People data into decisions

  • Own the HR Cockpit priorities and the definition of our key People metrics, built on Workday and aligned with company data standards.

  • Co-steer workforce planning and the people cost trajectory with Finance (headcount, compensation, equity, benefits, contingent workers), with scenarios for organisational decisions.

Shape benefits and international mobility

  • Set the principles for global and local benefits and immigration, and manage providers on compliance, quality, cost and employee experience as we grow internationally.

Keep it trustworthy

  • Make sure reward decisions and sensitive data are handled with clear governance, approvals, auditability and data protection, and flag reward-related risks early.

What you'll bring

  • Significant experience leading a Total Rewards or Comp & Ben function in an international, multi-site company. Scale-up, tech or marketplace experience is a strong plus.

description:

Je bent verantwoordelijk voor het functioneel beheer, de technische inrichting, continuïteit en doorontwikkeling van Relatics. Je test en implementeert de wijzigingen en bewaakt dat de inrichting stabiel, uniform en toekomstbestendig blijft.

Je werkzaamheden bestaan onder andere uit:

  • Je ontwikkelt en configureert Relatics-modules voor onder andere eisenmanagement, contractmanagement en risicomanagement, inclusief de bijbehorende structuren, objecten, relaties en standaardbibliotheken;

  • Je richt schermen, tabellen, queries en views in en verbetert deze op basis van project- en gebruikersbehoeften. Daarbij bewaak je de uniformiteit, datakwaliteit en traceerbaarheid;

Hier zit je op je plek

Je standplaats is ons moderne kantoor De Verbinding in Utrecht, waar je deel uitmaakt van de afdeling Informatiemanagement (IM): een groeiend team van informatiemanagers, applicatiespecialisten, BI-specialisten en product owners. In jouw rol werk je nauw samen met je collega’s binnen IM, de werkmaatschappijen, stafafdelingen en Groep IT. Dat doe je zowel in kleinere optimalisaties als in grotere projecten. Zo helpen we Dura Vermeer om een voorloper te blijven op het gebied van digitalisering in de infrasector.

Denk aan het uitnutten van contracten, stroomlijnen van interne- en klantprocessen, het structureel realiseren van afgesproken prestaties en samen met klanten de samenwerking doorontwikkelen;

  • Commerciële strategie vertalen naar executie: Je vertaalt de langetermijnvisie van Orion naar concrete commerciële kansen en innovaties. Samen met je collega’s identificeer je marktontwikkelingen en zorg je dat onze dienstverlening hierop aansluit;

  • Coachend leiderschap & mentorschap: Je geeft leiding aan een (medior) business development manager. Je voorziet hen van coaching, deelt jouw ervaring, helpt bij het doorgronden van complexe klantvragen en begeleidt hen proactief in hun professionele ontwikkeling.

  • WO werk- en denkniveau: Het bezit van een universitaire master is een harde eis voor deze functie;

  • 8+ jaar relevante werkervaring: Je hebt een bewezen trackrecord in het sluiten van complexe, meerjarige servicecontracten. Je hebt dan ook minimaal acht jaar relevante werkervaring in business development, complexe sales of een andere commerciële en klantgerichte rol. Ervaring met consulting en/of verandermanagement is een pré;

Je praat daarbij net zo makkelijk met onze CEO en klanten over de commerciële strategie, als met de monteurs in de werkplaats over de dagelijkse operatie. Je luistert goed en bouwt snel vertrouwen op, maar durft ook kritische vragen te stellen en scherp te onderhandelen;

  • Aantoonbare ervaring met het bouwen en verbeteren van (sales)processen: Je hebt in eerdere rollen bewezen dat je processen vanaf nul kunt opzetten en professionaliseren. Hier word je enthousiast van:

Je werkt nauw samen met verschillende stakeholders, zoals de CEO, maar ook met klanten, de werkplaatsen en het softwareontwikkeling- en data-team. Die afwisseling maakt het werk niet alleen dynamisch en intellectueel uitdagend, het zorgt er ook voor dat je de impact van jouw werkzaamheden direct terugziet op de werkvloer en bij de klant;

Pionieren in een sector die volop verandert brengt uitdagingen met zich mee, maar geeft jou vooral de kans om mee te bouwen aan tastbare, toekomstbestendige oplossingen;

  • Scale-up dynamiek binnen een Pon-bedrijf: We zijn marktleider, maar hebben de flexibele en informele cultuur van een scale-up behouden. Tegelijkertijd profiteren we van de slagkracht, stabiliteit en het netwerk van Pon. Het sales team verandert en haar scope groei, wat volop kans biedt om hier zelf vorm aan te geven.

  • In totaal 34 vrije dagen: 20 wettelijke verlofdagen, 8 bovenwettelijke verlofdagen en 6 ADV-dagen; 

  • Flexibele werktijden en de mogelijkheid om hybride te werken; op kantoor, vanuit huis en natuurlijk bij de klant;

  • Een (elektrische) auto van de zaak;

  • Mogelijkheid om je verder te ontwikkelen, inclusief persoonlijk trainingsbudget, intensieve begeleiding en 1:1 coaching.

Wat we verder nog bieden: 

  • Een leuke werkplek met lekker vers fruit, heerlijke koffie en een gratis gym;

  • Uiteraard een mobiele telefoon (Samsung of Apple) en laptop (Windows of MacBook);

  • Een goed pensioen, met een zeer ruime pensioenbijdrage vanuit Pon;

  • Een collectieve zorgverzekering bij Zilveren Kruis en ONVZ met een bijdrage van € 300,- bruto per jaar vanuit ons;

  • Aantrekkelijke kortingen (€ 500,- per jaar) op Pon-producten zoals een Gazelle fiets of een Pon Privé Lease;

Wij zijn de strategische partner en marktleider in integraal fleet management voor complexe, bedrijfskritische voertuigen. Denk aan de bussen van Keolis en Qbuzz, of het materieel op Schiphol. Dagelijks vertrouwen duizenden reizigers en bedrijven op de voertuigen die wij beheren; de maatschappelijke impact van ons werk is dan ook enorm. title: Native Android Engineer
description:
Healthcare professionals have to spend too much time on administrative tasks when they should be spending that time delivering great care. Attendi allows healthcare professionals to report with their voice. This saves them precious time and removes the screen between client and caregiver, allowing more personal and effective care to be given.

As our Android engineer, you will play a central role in building and scaling Attendi’s native Android app: a voice-powered notepad for healthcare professionals to capture and structure medical data at the point of care.

Healthcare professionals prefer to stay close to their patients, not behind a laptop. As mobile usage in care settings grows, a native Android app becomes essential. That’s why we’re bringing Attendi’s voice-powered functionalities straight to their pocket.

We envision this app as the healthcare sector’s voice-enabled notepad: a flexible, intuitive tool for capturing and structuring medical data quickly and accurately—whether caregivers are at the bedside, in the hallway, or between visits. A thoughtful mobile strategy, seamless UX, and high-performance native Android implementation will be key to realising this vision.

Our mission

Attendi has built a strong user base with its API-first speech-to-text solutions and client SDKs, which are used and loved by healthcare professionals through our integrations with electronic health record (EHR) vendors. Currently, our users primarily interact with our products from within existing EHR systems. But why stop there? We want to give healthcare professionals the ability to benefit from our functionalities whenever and wherever they like.

Your Role

As our Android engineer, you will:

  • Develop and maintain Attendi’s native Android application.

  • Develop and maintain Attendi’s open-source Android microphone SDK (attendi-android).

  • Build high-quality voice recording, transcription, and medical documentation flows for real healthcare workflows.

  • Collaborate with backend engineers, frontend engineers, UX designers, product, and other mobile engineers to ensure smooth development and a cohesive user experience.

  • Take ownership of Android architecture, development quality, testing, CI/CD, Play Store releases, phased rollouts, crash reporting, monitoring, and user feedback.

  • Help shape Android-specific UX decisions using Material Design and platform conventions.

  • Contribute to our open-source efforts where applicable.


You might be a good fit if you:

  • Have at least 5 years of experience.

  • Have strong experience developing native Android applications with Kotlin.

  • Have production experience with Jetpack Compose.

  • Understand Android lifecycle, permissions, foreground services, background execution limits, and platform-specific UX patterns.

  • Have experience with Kotlin coroutines and reactive programming with Flow.

  • Are able to take meaningful ownership of Android features end-to-end.

  • Have a strong user and product-focused mindset, whether that user is an end user of the Attendi App or another developer using our SDKs.

  • Have experience with and a well-formed opinion on testing strategies for Android applications, such as when to use unit tests, integration tests, UI tests, screenshot tests, or other testing strategies.

  • Take pride in building robust, scalable, and maintainable software.

  • Communicate clearly about trade-offs, risks, progress, and technical decisions.

Strong candidates may also

  • Have released at least one Android application to the Google Play Store.

  • Have been involved in the full release lifecycle of an Android app.

  • Have experience with MVVM and Clean Architecture.

  • Have experience designing public APIs or SDKs, including semantic versioning and sample apps.

  • Have experience with audio recording, speech-to-text, offline/network-resilient flows, or privacy-sensitive applications.

  • Have worked in healthcare, regulated, security-sensitive, or high-reliability environments.

  • Have experience with Gradle, modularization, CI quality gates, crash reporting, and monitoring.

  • Have collaborated with iOS engineers or worked on cross-platform product consistency. This is a plus, not a requirement.

What success looks like in three to six months

You will have:

  • Successfully implemented, merged, and released at least two or three medium to large sized features for Attendi’s native Android application.

  • Implemented at least one feature mostly independently, from product input to release.

  • Built a strong understanding of our Android app, Android SDK, voice recording flows, and product domain.

  • Contributed to improving Android architecture, quality, observability, or release processes.

  • Collaborated effectively with product, design, backend, frontend, and mobile stakeholders.

What we offer

  • Salary between €6000 and €8000 per month.

  • Travel and lunch allowance.

  • Home office budget.

  • Lease bike.

  • Training budget of €1,500 per year.

  • Company MacBook.

  • ClassPass membership.

  • Time to learn the Android / iOS platform if not proficient in one of these

  • Working on impactful solutions for problems in healthcare: our solutions directly result in time savings for healthcare professionals, time they can use to deliver better and more personal care.

  • Transparent and responsible personal development: we encourage personal growth by making development plans together and giving the opportunity to follow courses that you feel contribute to your development.

  • Possibility to work from home: while we like to work together at our Amsterdam-based office, we think having the freedom to work at home when it suits you is important. Most of us spend two to three days per week at the office and the rest working from home.

  • A great place to work – feel free to reach out to our team to ask what it’s like!

  • Regular drinks and team outings.

  • Interview with 2 colleagues: 1 for culture-fit and 1 for technical-fit assessment

  • Technical assessment with two technical-fit assessors

Diese Rolle ist für jemanden, der in Systemen, Nutzen für die Anwender und operativer Klarheit denkt, nicht nur in Jira-Status.

Wir entwickeln schnell mit modernen KI-Werkzeugen (Cursor, Claude, Copilot usw.). Als unser Product Owner musst du selbst keinen Produktivcode schreiben, aber du musst verstehen, wie KI-native Entwicklung Lieferzyklen, Aufwandsschätzung und Scoping verändert.

Die KI-Werkzeuge können Code schreiben, aber sie wissen nicht, was unsere Kunden wirklich brauchen, wie Abläufe über Unternehmen hinweg zusammenhängen oder welche Kompromisse für unsere Architektur sinnvoll sind. Genau für dieses Urteilsvermögen suchen wir dich. Die Messlatte ist nicht „Kannst du eine User-Story-Vorlage ausfüllen?“. Die Messlatte ist: Kannst du eine unübersichtliche betriebliche Realität in glasklare Produktanforderungen übersetzen, konsequent priorisieren und Entwickler wie KI-Assistenten effizient dahin lenken, das Richtige zu bauen?

  • Du entwickelst unsere Produktprozesse mit unserem Wachstum weiter, hältst Feedbackschleifen kurz und die Developer Experience reibungslos.

  • Methodik: agil, Lean Product Development, kurze Iterationen, wenig Bürokratie

title: Geschäftsführer (m/w/d) für Gebäude-Energieberatung & Sanierungskoordination
description:
Haben Sie schon länger über eine berufliche Veränderung nachgedacht? Möchten Sie ein Unternehmen als Geschäftsführer in unserem Franchise leiten und dabei eine Aufgabe übernehmen, die wirtschaftlich attraktiv ist und echten Sinn stiftet? Dann könnte diese Chance für Sie passen – insbesondere, wenn Sie aus einer dieser Regionen kommen:

  • Erfurt
  • Weimar
  • Gotha
  • Arnstadt
  • Sömmerda

Gebäude-Energieberatung

Die Nachfrage nach Gebäude-Energieberatung steigt stark: Kunden wollen ihre Öl- und Gaskosten senken und Immobilien zukunftssicher sanieren. Gleichzeitig fehlen vielerorts Gebäude-Energieberater – das schafft hervorragende Chancen für Quereinsteiger.

Ideal für Quereinsteiger

Sie benötigen keine umfangreichen fachlichen Voraussetzungen, um einen gebietsgeschützten Standort aufzubauen. ENERDOMO unterstützt Sie von Anfang an – auch nach der Neueröffnung.

Qualifizierung in 27 Tagen

In der hybriden ENERDOMO Akademie (Königstein/Frankfurt & Online) erhalten Quereinsteiger ein strukturiertes Einarbeitungs- und Qualifizierungsprogramm. Projektleiter, Ingenieure, Maschinenbauer, Handwerksmeister und Immobilienmakler finden bei uns einen schnellen Einstieg in alle Themen rund um die energetische Sanierung.

ENERDOMO Sanierungssprint

Ein- und Zweifamilienhäuser werden in 22 Werktagen energetisch saniert. Ein Taktplan steuert die Gewerke, die parallel arbeiten. Die Sanierungssprintkoordination übernimmt Baubegleitung, Bauzeitenplanung sowie die Koordinierung der Gewerke.

Zukunftsmarkt mit Sinn

„Grüne Jobs“ sind dabei mehr als ein Trend. Umwelt- und Energieberufe gehören zu den wichtigsten Zukunftsmärkten. ENERDOMO gibt Know-how an Existenzgründer und Quereinsteiger weiter, die Verantwortung übernehmen und etwas Eigenes aufbauen wollen.

Aufgaben

Wir helfen Immobilienbesitzern (privat und gewerblich), Fördermittel für energetische Sanierungen zu beantragen. Dazu erstellen wir einen Sanierungsfahrplan (iSFP) und unterstützen bei den baulichen Maßnahmen.

Statt die Arbeit von Architekten, Dachdeckern oder Heizungsbauern zu ersetzen, kooperieren wir eng mit ihnen.

Als Geschäftsführer und ENERDOMO-Partner übernehmen Sie dabei folgende Aufgaben:

  • Aufbau Ihrer eigenen, lokalen Präsenz von ENERDOMO, inklusive eines Netzwerkes aus Handwerkern und eventuellen Mitarbeitern
  • Beraten von Kunden zu allen Fragen rund um die Gebäude-Sanierung und verfügbaren Fördermittel
  • Beantragen von Fördermitteln mit oder für den Kunden
  • Vor-Ort Begehung von Gebäuden zur Aufnahme von Gebäude-Daten
  • Erstellung von individuellen Sanierungsfahrplänen (iSFP) in Hottgenroth
  • Erstellungen von Zusatzleistungen wie z.B. Energieausweisen oder Heizlastberechnungen
  • Schreiben von Angeboten und Rechnungen in Lexware Office

Qualifikation

Ein erfolgreicher Geschäftsführer im Bereich der Energieberatung sollte folgende Qualifikationen mitbringen:

  • Interesse am Energiesektor: Kenntnisse über Immobilien, Produkte und Dienstleistungen sowie die Fähigkeit, sich in dieses Thema einzuarbeiten.
  • Führungserfahrung: Erfahrung in der Leitung von Teams und der Entwicklung von Geschäftsbeziehungen.
  • Unternehmerisches Denken: Fähigkeit, neue Ideen und Geschäftsmöglichkeiten umzusetzen und Verantwortung für den erfolgreichen Betrieb des Standorts zu übernehmen.
  • Finanzielle Kenntnisse: Kenntnisse in Budgetplanung, -analyse und -berichterstattung zur Sicherstellung des erfolgreichen Betriebs.
  • Marketing- und Vertriebskenntnisse: Fähigkeit, erfolgreiche Marketing- und Vertriebsstrategien zu entwickeln und umzusetzen, um neue Kunden zu gewinnen und den Umsatz zu steigern.
  • Kommunikations- und Präsentationsfähigkeiten: Fähigkeit, effektiv mit Kunden, Mitarbeitern und Geschäftspartnern zu kommunizieren und zu präsentieren.

Sie benötigen:

  • Technisches Verständnis
  • Nachweisbare Erfahrung mit technischen Anlagen

Zusätzlich vorteilhaft: Ein Abschluss in einem technischen Studiengang oder einer berufsbildenden höheren Schule. Dies ist jedoch keine Voraussetzung bei ENERDOMO. Wir unterstützen Sie bei der Befähigungsprüfung zum Energieberater.

Quereinsteiger: Selbst wenn Sie kein Handwerksmeister, Ingenieur oder Architekt sind, können Sie mit unserer Hilfe die „Qualifikationsprüfung Energieberatung“ erfolgreich ablegen.

Benefits

  • Gestalten Sie Ihr eigenes Unternehmen innerhalb eines erprobten Geschäftsmodells
  • Profitieren Sie vom ENERDOMO-Netzwerk: Erhalten Sie die Unterstützung bestehender ENERDOMO-Partner bei fachlichen Fragen und wachsen Sie gemeinsam mit uns in einem aufstrebenden Markt.
  • Unterstützung im Marketing durch die Systemzentrale: Konzentrieren Sie sich ganz auf den Vertrieb und Ihre Kunden
  • Unterstützung beim Aufbringen der Startgebühr und der Finanzierung der Selbstständigkeit mithilfe fachkundiger Inhouse-Beratung durch einen unserer Experten wie zum Beispiel Dr. Arthur Schäfer

CO₂ runter, Umsätze hoch! Mit ENERDOMO gestalten wir aktiv die energetische Zukunft der Immobilienberatung. Mit einer starken Marke. Aber noch wichtiger: mit starken Partnern.

Deshalb rücken wir am liebsten Menschen wie Patrik Brings ins Rampenlicht. Denn letztlich geht es nicht um Logos, sondern um echte Persönlichkeiten – mit Profil, klarer Haltung und einer echten Story. Warum setzen wir so auf Personal Branding?Weil Menschen am liebsten mit Menschen zusammenarbeiten.

Weil Persönlichkeit die besten Kunden anzieht – und gleichzeitig die passenden Mitarbeiter. Weil jeder Partner einzigartig ist und genau das sichtbar werden soll.

Patrik hat sich entschieden, Gesicht zu zeigen – heute steht er nicht nur für ENERDOMO, sondern ist die Adresse Nr. 1 in Koblenz, wenn es um energetische Sanierung geht.

Brings sagt: „Die Entscheidung für ENERDOMO war eine der besten meines Lebens. Jetzt unterstütze ich Menschen dabei, ihre Immobilien zukunftssicher zu gestalten. Diese Aufgabe ist wirtschaftlich äußerst attraktiv und gibt meinem Leben einen echten Sinn."

title: Forward Deployed Engineer (f/m/d)
description:
About Valova

We are building the AI operations platform for European hospitals, so every clinician can focus on patients.

Behind every patient sits a chain of admin work: documentation, coding, billing, audits, scheduling. It runs through disconnected systems and endless manual hand-offs, while most German hospitals already operate at a loss.

We start where the impact is measurable from day one: case to cash. Valova codes every case, defends it in audits and makes sure the money lands. From there we take on every workflow that runs a hospital, until one agentic system handles the routine and people decide the exceptions. First Germany, then Europe.

Doctors, engineers and operators, on-site in Munich and Berlin. Join us!

Why this role matters

Valova only works as well as it fits into the hospital. Our product creates the most value when it’s deeply connected to a hospital’s systems and built around how coders and medical controlling actually work. Today, connecting to a hospital information system can take months. That’s time hospitals keep losing revenue and coders keep working by hand.

That’s where you come in. As Forward Deployed Engineer, you own technical go-lives from start to finish: from the first sandbox to production, from the interface to the workflow on the ward. You’re the bridge between hospital IT, the people who use Valova and our engineering team.

Your impact is easy to see: in hospitals that go live faster, in integrations that run reliably, and in a product that gets better with every deployment because you bring back what you learn.

This is a hands-on engineering role with real code in production and direct influence on our roadmap. It’s not a support desk, not a pre-sales role and not project management where others do the building. And it’s not a desk job: you’ll regularly be on site in hospitals

How the role sits in the team

You report directly to Christian, our CTO, and work day to day with our engineering team on connectors, deployments and internal tooling. With Malte and our product team, you turn what you see in hospitals into clear requirements. In hospital projects, you work hand in hand with our customer success and sales team and on the hospital side with IT leads, KIS vendors, coders and medical controlling.

What you will do

  • Bring hospitals live: You take hospitals from sandbox to production, deploy Valova on hospital VMs and connect it to KIS systems such as SAP i.s.h.med, Orbis or Dedalus.

  • Build the connections: You build and maintain interfaces (HL7, FHIR, archive and document exports) together with hospital IT and their partners.

  • Set up Valova for each customer: You configure document types, case filtering, department rules and coding workflows.

  • Learn from the ward: You work on site with coders and medical controlling and turn their friction into clear product requirements.

  • Make deployments repeatable: You write the code that makes the next go-live faster: connectors, scripts, monitoring and internal tooling.

  • Earn the hospital’s trust: You answer technical questions in security and data protection reviews (BSI C5, GDPR).

What we are looking for:

  • Engineering experience: At least two years in software engineering, and you’re comfortable with Linux, Docker and basic networking.

  • Integration know-how: You’ve worked on system integrations. Experience with HL7/FHIR or SAP environments is a big plus.

  • Customer focus: You enjoy working with customers and explain technical topics clearly to IT leads and coders alike.

  • High ownership: You move things forward, even when three parties are involved.

  • Travel: You’re happy to spend around 30 percent of your time at hospitals across Germany.

  • Languages: You speak fluent German and English, since our customers work in German.

  • Location: You work from our office in Munich or Berlin.

Missing one or two points, but convinced you’re the right person for this role? Apply anyway. We’re looking forward to meeting you!

What you get

  • Work that means something, every day. Your agents are the core of our product and directly help improve the German healthcare system.

  • Ownership from week one. You take over real projects with a clear outcome and your name on it, not a list of tasks someone else defined.

  • Direct access to the founders. You work day to day with our founders Sophia, a physician and ex-McKinsey consultant, and Christian, who has founded two health tech startups and spent a decade building clinical systems. No layers, no waiting weeks for approvals.

  • Trust and freedom. We trust you to solve problems your way, and the team has your back 100%.

  • Learning at startup speed. You will see more in one year here than in three years elsewhere, across models, infrastructure, product and customers, with a team that has a proven track record of deploying AI in healthcare.

  • One team, in the heart of the city. We work together on-site at WeWork Odeonsplatz in Munich and WeWork in central Berlin. Fully serviced offices with coffee, meeting rooms and phone booths mean zero admin, and the city-center location means short commutes, easy access to customers and investors, and lunch spots around every corner.

  • Team events that bring Munich and Berlin together, because the people you build with should also be the people you celebrate with.

What success looks like

  • After 3 months, you know Valova’s stack inside out and have taken a hospital through its first technical setup together with our team.

  • After 6 months, you’ve taken at least two hospitals live, and a new KIS connection takes weeks instead of months.

  • After 12 months, our deployments are largely repeatable: connectors, scripts and monitoring you built make every go-live faster.

  • Throughout, what you learn in hospitals shapes our roadmap, and hospital IT teams see you as their trusted contact at Valova.

How it works

Just upload your CV with your application. We’ll get in touch with you for the next steps:

  1. Intro call (30 min): We get to know each other, talk about your background and answer your first questions.

  2. Technical interview with Christian (CTO) (60 min): We dive into your engineering experience and the integrations you’ve built.

  3. Case: You work through a realistic hospital integration scenario and present it to the team.

  4. References: We speak with two or three people you’ve worked with, such as former managers or colleagues.

  5. Meet the team: You spend a day with us on-site in Munich or Berlin, meet our founders Sophia and Christian and see how we work day to day.

  6. Offer: If it’s a match for both sides, you’ll hear from us quickly.

We look forward to your application, regardless of gender, background, religion, disability, age or sexual identity.

  • Founders’ office: Strategic projects end to end, from planning cycles to board preparation.

You were among the best there, and you can show it. We will ask for the proof.
