description:
Location : Lyon, France

ABOUT ARCHIMED

With offices in Europe, the US and Asia, ARCHIMED is a leading investment firm focused exclusively on healthcare. Our mix of operational, medical, scientific and financial expertise positions us as both a strategic and financial partner to healthcare businesses. Priority areas include Biopharma Products, Consumer Health, Healthcare IT, In Vitro Diagnostics, Life Science Tools and Biologic Services, MedTech and Pharma Services. ARCHIMED helps partners internationalize, acquire, innovate and expand their products and services.

ARCHIMED manages $11 billion across its funds, including the largest healthcare-only private equity fund raised by a European-based GP. MED I, MED II and MED Platform I are all top-decile performers for their vintage according to Preqin data. Since inception, ARCHIMED has been a committed impact investor, both directly and through its EURÊKA Foundation.

THE TEAM

  • An global team with complementary backgrounds across investment, medical, scientific, strategic and operational disciplines.
  • Alumni of INSEAD, Wharton, Berkeley, Georgetown, Bocconi, HEC Paris, École des Ponts ParisTech, ESSEC, Imperial College and Dartmouth, among others.
  • Professional backgrounds spanning Private Equity (3i, Siparex, USS Ltd, Barings, Capiton, Partners Group, KKR), Consulting (A.T. Kearney, Bain, McKinsey), M&A (Lazard, EY, KPMG, PwC, Goldman Sachs, Jefferies) and Industry (Biotronik, Cerba, Stryker, Phillips, Pfizer, Baxter, LivaNova, J&J, Galderma, Sanofi).

THE DIAGNOSTICS TEAM

The Director will serve as a senior investment professional with direct responsibility for sourcing, evaluating and executing investments across the Diagnostics portfolio. The Director will lead deal activity across an assigned geography, technology platform or investment theme, and will carry accountability for investment outcomes, value creation and portfolio company support.

This is a senior operating role combining strategic direction setting with hands-on deal execution, positioning the Director as a trusted senior advisor to Partners and portfolio management teams.

  • Investment Sourcing & Strategy
    • Drive sourcing and pipeline development across assigned Diagnostics sectors or geographies, identifying and cultivating relationships with sellers, intermediaries and LP co-investors.
    • Lead the formation and evolution of investment theses within assigned focus areas, including category mapping, competitive positioning and market trend analysis.
    • Serve as primary investment decision maker and deal sponsor, with direct accountability for investment committee presentations and recommendation.
    • Lead the negotiation of transaction terms, pricing and deal structure in partnership with Partners and external advisors.
  • Due Diligence & Execution
    • Oversee comprehensive commercial, financial and operational due diligence, working with external advisors to validate assumptions and identify key risks and levers.
    • Lead the development of post-acquisition value creation roadmaps, including 100-day plans and multi-year operating strategies.
    • Manage the investment committee approval process and coordinate all transaction closing mechanics with legal and finance teams.
  • Portfolio Leadership & Value Creation
    • Serve as the primary investment relationship owner for assigned portfolio companies, working directly with management teams on strategy, M&A, capital deployment and operational priorities.
    • Lead add-on acquisition identification, evaluation and execution, including syndication with co-investors.
    • Drive performance monitoring and problem-solving, escalating key decisions to Partners and intervention areas to senior management.
    • Sponsor and mentor portfolio company boards, ensuring robust governance and strategic clarity.
  • Team & Platform Development
    • Mentor and develop Senior Analysts and Associate-level team members, contributing to talent development and succession planning within the Diagnostics function.
    • Contribute to ARCHIMED's Diagnostics thought leadership and external positioning through conference participation, investor communication and industry engagement.
    • Identify and build capabilities across the Diagnostics platform to support scaling and evolution of the investment program.

Requirements

  • 8 to 12 years of investment or operating experience, with a strong track record in private equity investing, transaction execution or operational leadership within diagnostics sector.
  • Demonstrated success originating, evaluating and closing significant investments (€50 million+ enterprise value preferred), with evidence of value creation across the portfolio.
  • Deep expertise in the Diagnostics landscape, including brand strategy, omnichannel distribution, and regulatory dynamics .
  • Exceptional executive presence and communication skills. Able to command credibility with sophisticated management teams, institutional LPs and external partners.
  • Strong financial acumen and fluency with investment modeling, valuation and deal structuring. Advanced Excel and PowerPoint skills required.
  • Proven operational judgment and the ability to translate market insights into concrete investment theses and deal opportunities.
  • Track record of building and leading high-performing teams. Comfort with mentoring junior professionals and shaping investment culture.
  • Strategic, entrepreneurial and partnership-minded. Takes ownership of outcomes, moves with pace and brings a builder's orientation to platform development.
  • Advanced degree preferred. MBA or equivalent experience strongly valued.
  • Embodies and reinforces ARCHIMED's cultural values of inclusion, meritocracy, partnership, accountability, client focus and trust.

title: Senior Data Platform Engineer
description:
We are looking for a Senior Data Platform Engineer to join the Data Platform at Smartly!

Smartly is building the standard path for governed data sharing across product services, analytics, and AI/ML. The Data Platform team owns the contracts, control mechanisms, publication paths, catalog metadata, lifecycle rules, lineage, permissions, and runtime building blocks that make reusable data safe and practical at scale.

This is a role for someone who wants to shape a platform early, while working on concrete production problems from the start. Smartly already has the production systems, Kafka backbone, PostgreSQL databases, analytical consumers, and AI/ML use cases that need a better data foundation. The challenge is to turn that reality into a standard path that engineers actually want to use.

Our first milestone is focused: centrally managed publishing tables in service-owned PostgreSQL databases, captured through Debezium CDC into Kafka, and registered in DataHub with ownership, lifecycle, lineage, and impact-analysis metadata. Longer-term, the platform expands toward self-service data products, governed materialisations, durable shared state, and reusable data across Smartly's operational and analytical systems.

This is not a role where you only maintain an existing reporting pipeline. You will help design and build the platform path that other engineering teams use when they publish and consume shared data.

What you will do

  • Design and build platform services, tools, and workflows for contract-driven data publishing and consumption.
  • Build the first production path for platform-managed PostgreSQL publishing tables, Debezium CDC, Kafka topics, and catalog registration.
  • Create GitOps-style workflows where contracts, schemas, ownership, lifecycle, compatibility, policy metadata, and runtime desired state are reviewed, validated, and reconciled as code.
  • Build tooling that gives product engineers fast feedback before they publish or change data products.
  • Help define how Smartly models data products, publishing contracts, schema evolution, field stability, deletion semantics, access policy, lineage, and cost attribution.
  • Operate and improve the CDC runtime model, including Kubernetes workloads, source-specific isolation, offsets, schema history, heartbeats, signal channels, lag visibility, replay, resnapshotting, and recovery.
  • Integrate platform metadata into DataHub so engineers can discover data products, understand ownership, trace lineage, and reason about the impact of changes.
  • Work with product, infrastructure, data engineering, analytics, and AI/ML teams to make the standard path easier and safer than bespoke point-to-point integrations.

What we are looking for

  • Strong experience building and operating production software systems, preferably in platform, infrastructure, backend, or data-intensive environments.
  • Deep understanding of distributed systems trade-offs: reliability, idempotency, replay, eventual consistency, ownership boundaries, compatibility, and operational failure modes.
  • Practical experience with PostgreSQL or other relational databases, including schema design, migrations, transactions, replication, or operational performance.
  • Experience with Kafka, event streaming, CDC, Debezium, or adjacent data-movement technologies. Direct Debezium experience is valuable, but strong fundamentals matter more.
  • Experience building software that other engineers use: CLIs, internal platforms, control planes, automation, CI validation, developer tooling, or self-service workflows.
  • Familiarity with Kubernetes and cloud or infrastructure platforms, including runtime isolation, deployment, observability, and operational ownership.
  • Ability to turn ambiguous architectural direction into practical increments, make trade-offs explicit, and deliver useful production systems without waiting for perfect certainty.
  • Clear written and spoken communication in English. This role involves aligning multiple engineering teams around standards, contracts, and ownership boundaries.

Useful experience, but not required

  • DataHub or other data catalog, lineage, or governance systems.
  • Open table formats such as Apache Iceberg, object-store-backed data lakes, S3, BigQuery, ClickHouse, or analytical storage systems.
  • GitHub Actions, policy-as-code, infrastructure-as-code, controllers, operators, or reconciliation-based systems.
  • Data contracts, schema registries, Protobuf, Avro, JSON Schema, compatibility checking, field-level metadata, or contract testing.
  • Experience supporting analytics, AI/ML, feature-store-style access patterns, or cross-domain product-service integrations.
  • Experience with JVM languages and Python, TypeScript, Go, or Ruby.

What we offer you

At Smartly, we offer a place where you can do meaningful technical work while growing with a global team.

  • Inclusive global culture built on trust, transparency, open feedback, and respect for different perspectives.
  • Global impact through technology used by major brands to plan, create, optimize, and understand digital advertising at scale.
  • Wellbeing support, paid holidays, family leave, and sustainable ways of working.
  • Equity options, performance-based rewards, competitive compensation, and career development opportunities.
  • A flexible hybrid workplace that balances office collaboration with focused remote work. At Smartly we work 3 days a week from the office.

About Smartly

Smartly is an advertising technology company helping brands create, manage, optimize, and understand digital advertising across major media platforms. Our engineering organization builds the systems that connect media, creative, and intelligence capabilities into a product used by customers globally.

We value clear communication, ownership, curiosity, and collaboration across teams. We want Smartly to be a place where people can do strong work, grow, and feel respected.

Not sure you tick every box? Please apply anyway. We care about strong engineering fundamentals, ownership, curiosity, and the ability to build reliable systems with others. Direct experience with every technology listed here is less important than the judgment to learn, reason from first principles, and ship useful platform capabilities.

About Smartly

Smartly is the AI-powered advertising technology company transforming ad experiences for brands and their consumers. Our comprehensive advertising platform seamlessly integrates the capabilities of media, creative, and intelligence to power more than 800 billion impressions and generate more than 300 billion creatives annually, delivering tangible business outcomes for brands and advertisers.

Smartly is the only company in the industry recognized as a Leader in The Forrester Wave: Creative Advertising Technologies with PwC validating the results it delivers for brands. We manage creative and media for 700+ brands worldwide and $6B in ad spend across the largest media platforms, including Facebook, Google, Instagram, Pinterest, Snap, and TikTok. Our end-to-end technology, unmatched access to media platforms and exceptional customer service help Fortune 500 brands to reach and engage consumers and learn what performs best.Smartly is a multinational and diverse team of 750+ Smartlies from 60+ nationalities, working in 13 countries. description:
Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.

We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

Here’s what this particular role covers.

🛠️ About our AI Platform Teams

Our AI Platform teams build the infrastructure that powers Wayve’s embodied AI. We store and serve hundreds of petabytes of driving data, growing towards exabyte scale, to support model training, simulation and data pipelines across regions and clouds.

As our first dedicated Staff Software Engineer for Storage Platform, you’ll set the technical direction for how we manage, protect and serve this data. Working closely with Infrastructure, Security, Privacy, Data Engineering and ML teams, you’ll help make training more efficient while reducing one of Wayve’s largest infrastructure costs.

 

🧠 Your day-to-day

  • Lead a hands-on, multi-quarter storage programme, from defining the problems and architecture to delivering platforms that teams adopt.

  • Build production services, controllers and infrastructure using Python, Go or a similar language, alongside Kubernetes and Terraform.

  • Partner with ML and data teams to understand access patterns, remove storage bottlenecks and reduce the time GPUs spend waiting for data.

  • Work with Security and Privacy to strengthen access controls, auditing and safe deletion of vehicle-collected data.

  • Write design documents and RFCs, align teams around shared standards, and mentor engineers as the platform and team grow.

 

🧩 What you’ll be working on

  • Data ownership and governance: Give datasets clear owners, purposes and retention classes, with tagging and team-level cost attribution.

  • Safe lifecycle management: Build retention, deletion and re-tiering capabilities for Azure Blob, backed by dry runs, audit trails and recovery paths.

  • Read performance and caching: Improve throughput and latency by tackling small-object reads, throttling, unnecessary data access and cross-region hops.

  • Secure data movement: Design Kubernetes-native NVMe caching and secure replication across regions and clouds.

  • Measurable platform outcomes: Establish standards, dashboards and SLOs for availability, performance, cache effectiveness, storage tiers and cost.

🙌 You should apply if

  • You’ve operated at Staff Engineer scope, leading complex infrastructure programmes across multiple teams from problem definition through adoption.

  • You’ve owned petabyte-scale object storage end to end—including data layout, lifecycle management, performance and cost—with measurable outcomes against a cost target.

  • You’ve built scalable systems for data ownership, tagging, cataloguing, retention or deletion.

  • You bring strong security and access-management experience, including IAM/RBAC, encryption, secure replication and auditing.

  • You’re a hands-on software engineer with strong Python, Go or comparable skills, plus production Kubernetes, Terraform and CI experience. You build durable platforms and services, not just one-off scripts.

  • You can influence technical decisions without formal authority, mentor others and are excited to start in a founding, hands-on role with the opportunity to grow a team.

  • You can work on a hybrid basis from our London office.

Experience with AWS or GCP is welcome—you don’t need to have worked exclusively with Azure.

 

🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! If you’re passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement.

 

More about Wayve:

🚀 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines.

Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility.

 

How we work 💻- Locations & Flexible Working:

Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated office spaces with focused time working remotely. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together, alongside the flexibility to do their best work in a way that fits their lives.

 

🔍 The Interview Process:

Our process is clear and respectful of your time:

  • Initial call / recruiter screen (30 mins) - A conversation with our Talent Partner about your experience, interest in the role and practical details.

  • Competency Interviews (60 mins) - A programming interview to assess your hands-on software engineering skills.

  • Deep-dive technical interviews - A system design interview and a domain-specific interview with the Hiring Manager, exploring your storage experience, technical leadership and approach to the role.

  • Final interview (30 mins) - Mission & values alignment

We’ll always explain the format and work around your availability.

 

What’s in it for you (Location dependant):

💰 Salaries benchmarked against the market annually
📈 Meaningful equity, sharing in the ownership and long term success of Wayve
✈️ Relocation support and visa sponsorship where applicable
✅ Hybrid working, core hours and the chance to work hands on in vehicle workshops and labs
📚 Learning and development budgets with support for training, conferences and growth
🩺 Comprehensive benefits including health insurance, dental, enhanced maternity and paternity leave, retirement or pension where applicable, access to therapists, wellbeing partnerships, team socials and more

A quick, honest note before you apply.

Wayve is not a mature, fully-structured place with the playbook already written. Much of how we work is still being written, and if you join, you’ll help write it. That suits people who want real ownership more than people who need a settled structure from day one.

If that sounds like the kind of problem you want to spend your time on, we’d really like to hear from you.

At Wayve we're committed to creating a diverse, fair and respectful culture that is inclusive of everyone based on their unique skills and perspectives, and regardless of sex, race, religion or belief, ethnic or national origin, disability, age, citizenship, marital, domestic or civil partnership status, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, pregnancy or related condition (including breastfeeding) or any other basis as protected by applicable law.

For more information visit Careers at Wayve. To learn more about what drives us, visit Values at Wayve

DISCLAIMER: We will not ask about marriage or pregnancy, care responsibilities or disabilities in any of our job adverts or interviews. However, we do look to capture information about care responsibilities, and disabilities among other diversity information as part of an optional DEI Monitoring form to help us identify areas of improvement in our hiring process and ensure that the process is inclusive and non-discriminatory.

We encourage engineers to own as much of the problem space as they can. You will spend time talking to customers, getting feedback from users, and working closely with market operators, while collaborating with Product to deliver scalable engineering solutions.

At Axle, we work in a deliberately flat structure. That means fewer layers, faster decisions, and more ownership for everyone.

 

Solutions Engineering at Axle looks like

  • Forming a deep understanding of our domain, our platform, and our customers' technical challenges, so you have enough context to execute at speed.

  • Building and maintaining integrations with customer systems, distributed energy devices, and third-party platforms.

  • Working closely with customers to troubleshoot technical issues, support implementations, and design scalable solutions.

  • Collaborating closely with our Product team to turn customer feedback into product improvements.

  • Focus on outcomes rather than process, taking ownership of the quality and impact of the final product you deliver.

  • Manage your own time and support others to adapt to changing scope and deadlines, to deliver 80% of the value in 20% of the time

🐍 We build in Python + React for the frontend

title: Platform Security Engineer
description:
At Scality, we build software that stores and protects the world’s most critical data — running on Linux, inside some of the largest infrastructures on the planet, at exabyte scale, for organizations that cannot afford to fail.

We are looking for a Platform Security Engineer to join our platform and delivery team in Paris. This is a new seat, and it exists because security work needs dedicated capacity. Absorbed as background tasks between feature tickets, it never gets the focus it deserves. You would be that dedicated capacity.

This is a Linux-first, hands-on engineering role. You will not write policies for other people to implement — you will write the Python and Bash that hardens our OS, automates our vulnerability management, and proves to auditors and customers that our supply chain is sound.


About Scality

Scality is the leader in software-defined object storage, trusted by 1,000+ enterprises and 700M+ users worldwide across banking, healthcare, and government sectors — exactly the sectors where security posture is a purchasing criterion, not a checkbox.

Industry recognition:

  • Gartner Magic Quadrant Leader for 9 consecutive years — the only 100% software-defined storage company to hold this position since the quadrant’s inception
  • #1 on the GigaOm Radar for Enterprise Object Storage (2024), ahead of 17 competing vendors
  • Gold Stevie Award 2025 — ARTESCA 3.0, Cloud Storage & Backup Solution category
  • Net Promoter Score of 85 across RING and ARTESCA

About the team

You will join a small team of highly skilled Linux engineers responsible for delivering and maintaining ADI (Scality Autonomous Data Infrastructure), our full platform: RING (object storage), S3C (S3-compatible layer), and SCOS (Scality OS — our own Linux distribution).

The team works across the full stack of infrastructure engineering — deep Linux system integration, RPM packaging, CI/CD pipelines, monitoring, and release automation. The command line is where most of our day happens, and we ship a Linux distribution to customers.


How We Build

We build with AI tools, in earnest rather than as an experiment. Every engineer here has Claude Code, and it is part of how we write, review, and ship code day to day.

We are also designing something larger: an AI code and delivery factory — AI woven into the build and release chain itself, not just into the editor. That work is early and still being thought through rather than already solved. We expect it to become part of how we maintain the platform, and CVE remediation is one of the first places we think it fits: an automated path from advisory to assessment to a patched, tested, delivered build.

If that sounds like a problem you would want to work on, this role sits close to it.

One principle is not negotiable: a human owns the outcome. AI writes code here, and when it does, we own what it produces — the review, the decision to ship, the consequences, and the fix. “The tool did it” is not an explanation we accept from ourselves, and it is not one we would offer a customer. In security work that matters doubly: an answer you cannot defend is worse than no answer at all.


How This Role Works

Scality is building a network of security engineers across the engineering department — a security peer embedded in each development team, rather than a central security function working at arm’s length from the code. You would be that peer for the platform and delivery team.

  • Security priorities are owned by our VP of Engineering. The agenda is set at that level, with dedicated resources committed across the teams. You will not have to invent it alone — and you will have a voice in it: the engineers closest to the code help decide what goes on the roadmap. We will be straight with you: today security work competes with delivery commitments and too often loses. Naming an owner and funding dedicated people is how we intend to change that. You would help build that capability, not inherit a finished one.
  • The team is accountable for the deliveries. Security items sit on the team’s plate alongside everything else it commits to, rather than in a separate function filing tickets from the outside.
  • You are the dedicated resource that makes them happen. While your teammates carry releases, OS compatibility, and platform features, your time is reserved for the security work. That focus is the whole reason the seat exists.
  • You share the team’s perimeter and its knowledge. Same repositories, same Jira projects, same code reviews, same sprint rituals. The engineers around you have rare, hard-earned Linux depth — OS integration, RPM packaging, boot and GRUB, CI/CD, monitoring — and you will learn the platform from them.
  • You will have peers. Security engineers embedded in the other development teams work the same problems on different perimeters. That network is where you compare notes, share tooling, and grow into the craft.

    • The point of the model is that security decisions get made inside the team that builds and ships the product, by someone who understands the build system rather than filing tickets against it.


Your First Missions

Two priorities are already on the roadmap, and they will shape your first year.

1. CVE exposure, answered before it is asked

Customers in banking, healthcare, and government ask us, routinely and under their own audit obligations, whether our products are exposed to a given CVE. That will not stop — for them, asking is the compliance requirement. Today each answer is researched from scratch: a customer question becomes a ticket, the ticket becomes a hunt through SBOMs, vendor advisories, and our own configuration, and the round trip can take weeks to produce something the team is not fully confident defending.

Your first mission is to invert that, so the answer already exists when the question arrives.

  • A standing exposure record, per shipped component and per release: what the SBOM says is present, what the upstream vendor has decided (including “will not fix”, which is common on RHEL 8 and often the real answer), and whether the vulnerable code path is actually reachable in our configuration
  • Reachability over presence. A module shipped and loaded by a distribution default is not the same as a module configured on a live URL. That distinction is the difference between “vulnerable” and “no impact”, and it is where the engineering judgement lives
  • Continuous CVE detection across our repositories, vendored third-party modules, container images, and shipped RPMs
  • Wiring detection into our existing SBOM tooling and GitHub Actions pipelines, so exposure is computed when a release is built rather than when a customer asks
  • A defined interface with the security engineers and the customer-facing teams: who produces the technical assessment, who owns the wording that reaches the customer, and how both meet the response commitments in our customer security policy
  • Durable capture. An assessment that lives only in a ticket comment gets re-derived next release. Findings belong somewhere queryable
  • A remediation loop with clear ownership and response targets, integrated with how the team already works in Jira
  • AI-assisted remediation, where it fits: from advisory to proposed patch to a tested build, with a human deciding what ships

    • Done well, a customer’s “are you affected by X?” becomes a lookup and an afternoon, not an escalation and three weeks.

    2. Raising the security baseline of SCOS

    SCOS is our own Linux distribution — we control the kickstarts, the package set, the boot path, and the images. That is unusual leverage, and we intend to use it. You will drive platform-level hardening across the OS we ship:

    • A hardened, defensible default configuration for the distribution
    • Advancing SELinux enforcement across RING and S3C (work already begun on the team, which you will help carry)
    • Supply-chain integrity: artifact provenance, signing, dependency currency, reproducible and verifiable builds
    • Secrets and credential handling across the delivery pipeline
    • Cryptographic posture — including FIPS 140-3 readiness, which matters concretely: FIPS 140-2 certificates move to NIST’s historical list on 22 September 2026, and RHEL 9’s validated OpenSSL, GnuTLS, and kernel crypto modules are the foundation we build on
    • Compliance-driven engineering work, notably the supply-chain security expectations of NIS2 (Article 21(2)(d)) and the EU Cyber Resilience Act — translated into automation and evidence, not spreadsheets

      • You will also contribute to what comes next: threat modelling of the platform, hardening guidance for customers, and security review of significant design changes.


What We Are Looking For

This is a role for someone early in their career who wants to grow into being their team’s security reference. We expect to invest in you, and we expect you to keep growing here for as long as you want to — there is no ceiling built into this seat.

Required

  • Linux is your primary operating system — at work, at home, or both. You are comfortable in the terminal and you reach for a shell before a UI
  • Roughly 2–4 years of relevant experience, or a shorter track record with unusually strong evidence of the skills below
  • Solid working ability in Python and Bash — you will be writing and maintaining real code in a production codebase
  • A genuine, demonstrable interest in security. We care much more about this than about formal credentials. Show it however it is true for you: CTFs, a home lab, reading advisories and CVE writeups for fun, a hardening project, security-adjacent contributions, a blog, anything real
  • Comfortable using Git in a collaborative environment
  • Ability to read and understand existing code before modifying it
  • The judgement to tell a real risk from a scanner’s opinion — and the instinct to check whether vulnerable code is actually reachable before calling it exposed
  • The willingness to say plainly when you are not yet sure, rather than producing an answer you could not defend
  • French — the team works in French day to day
  • Written communication skills in English

    • Nice to Have

    • CVE triage, CVSS scoring, or vulnerability management experience
    • Reading vendor advisories and understanding vendor triage — NVD, RHSA, Red Hat severity and will-not-fix calls
    • Supply-chain security tooling — SBOM formats (SPDX, CycloneDX), scanners (Trivy, Grype, Syft), artifact signing
    • RPM packaging or Linux distribution internals
    • SELinux policy work
    • CI/CD systems, especially GitHub Actions
    • RHEL / Rocky Linux (versions 8 and 9)
    • Containers (Docker, containerd, systemd units)
    • Ansible or Salt
    • Awareness of NIS2, the Cyber Resilience Act, or FIPS 140-3
    • Familiarity with S3 or object storage concepts
    • Serious use of AI coding tools in a real workflow — Claude Code or equivalent, beyond autocomplete

      • To Be Clear About Scope

      This is a software engineering role with a security mandate. It is not a SOC or incident-response analyst position, not a penetration-testing role, and not a GRC or compliance-documentation role. If what you want is to build the tooling and harden the system yourself, in code, you are in the right place.


What We Offer
  • Dedicated focus. Security is your job here, not the thing you get to after the sprint work is done
  • Clear direction, and a say in it. Security priorities are owned by our VP of Engineering, and the team is accountable for delivering them. You would not be inventing the agenda on your own, you would help shape what goes on it, and you would be part of making it stick
  • A network of peers. Security engineers embedded in the other development teams, working the same problems on different perimeters
  • Work that compounds. Customer security questions are a permanent obligation, so every assessment you make reusable and every check you automate keeps paying back, release after release
  • Modern tooling, actually adopted. Claude Code in every engineer’s hands, and a real say in how AI reshapes our build and delivery chain
  • A rare combination: security work with the leverage of owning the whole stack, down to our own Linux distribution
  • Mentorship from senior engineers with deep expertise across Linux, storage, packaging, and distributed systems — you will not be the only person who understands your perimeter
  • A long-term growth path toward becoming your team’s security reference and a senior voice in the network
  • Work that ships to production and runs at exabyte scale, in banking, healthcare, and government
  • Standard French benefits: meal vouchers, Navigo subsidy, mutuelle

title: Account Manager Lille
description:
Our Global Structure


Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we're unlocking new possibilities as one global team.

Pourquoi Deliveroo ?

Nous transformons la façon dont le monde mange et fait ses courses en rendant leur accès plus pratique et agréable. Nous connectons les consommateurs, les restaurants, les magasins et les cyclistes. Nous donnons à chaque personne la possibilité d'acheter ce qu'elles veulent, comme elles le veulent, quand elles le veulent et où elles le veulent.

Nous sommes une entreprise axée sur la technologie, à l'avant-garde d'un secteur qui connaît une des expansions les plus rapides au monde. Nous avançons rapidement, valorisons l'autonomie, et sommes toujours en recherche de nouvelles idées et de personnes talentueuses pour nous rejoindre!

Tes principales missions :  

  • Gérer un portefeuille de restaurants clés sur des zones matures, où l'expertise et l'attention au détail font toute la différence.
  • Développer des partenariats privilégiés et durables en devenant le point de contact expert de votre zone et en mettant à profit vos connaissances Food Tech.
  • Optimiser la performance de vos comptes grâce à un accompagnement personnalisé, construit sur le long terme et nourri par la data.
  • Analyser les résultats de vos restaurants, identifier les leviers d'amélioration et recommander des actions concrètes à votre manager tout en restant agile et ouvert à la nouveauté.
  • Proposer et mettre en place des campagnes marketing et promotionnelles ciblées pour booster l'attractivité de vos restaurants partenaires.
  • Suivre de près le déroulé des opérations afin de garantir la meilleure expérience restaurant et client possible.

Ton expérience et tes qualités :

  • Tu as déjà 2 à 3 ans d'expérience sur un rôle similaire où la gestion d'un portefeuille de partenaires était centrale à ta mission.
  • Tu sais négocier et anticiper les discussions commerciales tout en gardant à l'esprit les valeurs de Deliveroo.
  • Tu sais garder le contrôle de ton portefeuille, identifier les nouvelles tendances du marché et partager du feedback utile à tes partenaires ainsi qu'à ton manager.
  • Le terrain est un lieu où tu te sens à ta place : tu sais construire des relations de confiance avec tes partenaires tout en gardant un œil attentif sur la concurrence.
  • Tu sais te montrer proactif, analyser les résultats de tes actions et proposer des recommandations concrètes à ton manager.
  • Tu travailles de manière autonome tout en gardant le cap fixé, sais t'approprier des objectifs précis et mets tout en œuvre pour les atteindre.
  • Tu sais concevoir des actions spécifiques, adaptées à la fois aux besoins de tes partenaires et à la stratégie définie par ton manager.
  • Tu sais identifier, comprendre et analyser les données de performance (commerciales et opérationnelles) pour garantir un niveau de service irréprochable.
  • Tu sais t'exprimer en anglais (à l'oral comme à l'écrit)
  • Tu arrives à convaincre tout en construisant des relations commerciales solides, durables, où Deliveroo devient le partenaire de choix
  • Et si tu cherches un poste où tu travailles en full remote depuis Lille, tout en gardant un lien fort avec le terrain et les équipes, alors c'est peut‑être le rôle qu'il te faut !

La vie chez Deliveroo

Notre équipe est en forte croissance, notre impact très important, et nous cherchons à répondre aux questions les plus stimulantes du moment. Nous progressons rapidement, nous explorons toujours de nouvelles idées et nous sommes très transparents quant aux décisions que nous prenons et à ce qui motive nos choix.

Il y a tellement de questions que nous souhaitons résoudre, et encore plus que nous n'avons pas encore rencontrées. Comment les données et la technologie peuvent-elles aider les restaurants à développer leur activité à mesure que les habitudes des consommateurs évoluent ? Comment pouvons-nous prédire ce qu'une personne souhaitera pour dîner avant même que l'idée ne lui vienne à l'esprit ? Chez Deliveroo, ces questions ne sont que quelques-uns des défis ambitieux auxquels nous nous efforçons de répondre – et il n'y a aucun projet qui ne peut pas devenir le vôtre. Aucune solution n'appartient à une équipe en particulier, ce qui vous ouvre d'extraordinaires possibilités en termes de développement et d'impact personnel.

Avantages et diversité

À compétences égales, ce poste est ouvert aux travailleurs et travailleuses en situation de handicap ou assimilés au sens de l'article L5212-13 du Code du travail. Deliveroo s'engage en faveur de la diversité, l'égalité professionnelle, l'emploi des personnes en situation de handicap.

Deliveroo France valorise la diversité sans discrimination de genre, race, sexualité, religion ou préférences personnelles. Avec un score de 99/100 à l'Indice de l'Égalité Hommes-Femmes 2023, nous sommes engagés envers l'égalité des chances. Rejoignez-nous avec votre passion pour la nourriture dans une entreprise en pleine croissance.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

At Deliveroo, we know that a great workplace reflects the world around us and that true diversity and inclusion make us stronger, more creative, and better at what we do. We're committed to fostering an environment where everyone can do their best work and feel they belong.

  • Software Engineering Culture: Strong engineering practices including version control, comprehensive testing, CI/CD, and containerization (Docker).

  • Owkin offers of employment are based on merit and only extended once a candidate has interviewed with members of the talent and hiring team. Offers will be extended both verbally and in written format.

ENVIRONNEMENT DU POSTE

Au sein du Département Automatique, Productique et Informatique, le poste sera associé à l’équipe TASC (Théorie, Algorithmes et Systèmes en Contraintes ) dont les thématiques de recherche s’articulent autour de la programmation par contraintes, de la théorie aux applications en passant par l’hybridation. Dans ce cadre, le poste a pour objectif de venir en soutien au développement du solveur de contraintes choco-solver (http://choco-solver.org) maintenu par l’équipe TASC.

 

MISSIONS

Sous la responsabilité fonctionnelle du responsable du projet et développeur principal de la plateforme Choco-solver et en collaboration avec les membres de l’équipe TASC, les missions principales du poste sont :

  1.   Adapter l’algorithme bimodal aux contraintes reposant sur des parcours en profondeur, telles que GlobalCardinality, StableKeysort ou Circuit ;

  2.   Étudier la transposition des bénéfices de l’approche bimodale au cœur d’un solveur de contraintes (p. ex. le moteur de propagation) ;

  3.   Évaluer l’impact des explications paresseuses (lazy) dans les contraintes Sum et AllDifferent, entre autres ;

  4.   Participer à la rédaction d’articles scientifiques liés à ces sujets.

 

 ACTIVITÉS : Activité par mission

2.      Étudier la transposition des bénéfices de l’approche bimodale au cœur d’un solveur de contraintes

·       Étudie le fonctionnement interne de choco-solver (moteur de propagation, ordonnancement des propagateurs, gestion des événements) afin d’identifier les mécanismes pouvant tirer parti d’une stratégie bimodale

·       Propose et prototype une ou plusieurs adaptations, par exemple un basculement dynamique entre modes de propagation

·       Évalue expérimentalement ces prototypes et analyse les compromis entre coût et bénéfice

 

3.      Évaluer l’impact des explications paresseuses (

·       Implémente ou étend la génération paresseuse d’explications pour les contraintes Sum, AllDifferent et d’autres contraintes globales

·       Compare les explications paresseuses aux explications calculées pendant la propagation (taille des clauses apprises, temps de résolution, nombre de nœuds explorés)

Nous recherchons un.e ingénieur.e Platform/DevOps expérimenté.e pour nous aider à améliorer nos pipelines et nos releases afin que nous puissions fournir une plateforme fiable et évolutive à nos clients.

  • Maintenir et faire évoluer notre service cloud en utilisant des outils tels que Terraform et Ansible

  • Concevoir, déployer et administrer des environnements conteneurisés avec Docker, tout en assurant l’orchestration et l’automatisation des déploiements applicatifs via Kubernetes et Helm.

  • Assurer la supervision, le monitoring et l’observabilité avec Datadog, ELK et Logic Monitor

  • Travailler en collaboration avec les équipes de développement pour améliorer les livraisons de code en utilisant Ansible/Gitlab CI

  • Assister en run les équipes de développement sur le projet de transition de plateforme: nous sommes actuellement sous Windows/.NET/.NETCore et nous sommes en train de passer sur Linux/NETCore/NodeJS. Nous souhaitons remplacer notre architecture monolithique par une architecture de microservices

  • Garantir la sécurité, la haute disponibilité et la performance des plateformes

  • Explorer de nouvelles technologies(IA, automatisation… ) tout en prenant en compte les éventuelles problématiques de sécurité


TON PROFIL

  • Tu as une solide expérience dans la création et le développement de pipelines CI/CD et le monitoring d'environnements de production

  • Tu es à l'aise avec les environnements Unix/Linux, Windows, IIS/SQLServer, et de l’expérience avec AWS (ou un autre cloud provider), Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, helm et Ansible.

  • Tu es soucieux.se de la qualité, de la performance et de la sécurité du code

  • Tu as idéalement travaillé sur des projets en lien avec des systèmes comme Apache Kafka, Rabbitmq...

  • Tu as une appétence pour les projets open-source de grand ampleur et tu t'intéresses aux thématiques d'automatisation

  • Tu parles français et anglais opérationnel

  • Tu apprécies le travail au sein d’une équipe multiculturelle et dynamique.

Au cours du premier round, tu auras un entretien avec Sabina, Talent Acquisition Manager, afin d'explorer ton parcours et tes motivations. Ce sera également l'occasion de t'en dire plus sur Lemonway et sur l'équipe.

Pourquoi ce poste : 

L'Academy forme chaque année 2000 professionnels et son offre est solide. Le problème : aujourd'hui, elle ne communique presque pas. Peu de contenu, peu de présence, une notoriété très en dessous de ce que le catalogue mérite.

C'est une page blanche côté growth, et c'est exactement ce qui rend le poste intéressant. At Vio we believe booking accommodation should feel smart, fair, and effortless — never overwhelming or unclear.

As one of the world’s fastest-growing travel tech platforms, we help millions of users make smarter travel decisions by comparing stays across 100+ booking sites — so they can find the perfect place, at the best price, anywhere in the world. We cut through the noise and complexity of hotel and vacation rental booking, surfacing real value with clarity, transparency, and full support. No tricks. No confusion. Just great stays — booked with confidence. With operations in 100+ markets and growing fast, our mission is to reshape how people discover and book accommodation through technology travelers can trust.

Who we're looking for

We are looking for a hands-on Quality Platform Lead to own Vio's quality strategy and automation platform across web, mobile, browser extensions, internal tooling and related surfaces.

This is a technical leadership role (Staff IC) reporting to the Director of Engineering. You define what good looks like for quality, decide where scarce testing effort goes, and give teams the confidence to ship. Your levers are release gates, quality telemetry, and a developer experience that makes the right tests easy to write and keep alive.

Product engineers own the tests for the features they build. Your remit is the platform, the strategy and the enablement that make that work hold up at scale. There is no QA department here and we have no plans to create one.

Where you'll start

  • Web: Playwright, Checkly, BrowserStack

  • Mobile: Patrol (Flutter)

  • Coverage gaps across white-labels, browser extensions, widgets, APIs and internal tooling

  • Web: Playwright, Checkly, BrowserStack

  • Mobile: Patrol (Flutter)

  • Coverage gaps across white-labels, browser extensions, widgets, APIs and internal tooling

The tooling can stay as it is. With a clear case you can migrate or rebuild. E2E coverage today is thin, so a different platform is genuinely on the table if it serves speed, maintainability and DX better. We have no predefined answer.

AI-assisted tooling is an open area too. We have no established practice for agent-generated tests or AI-assisted triage, so your judgment on what earns a place in the platform carries real weight.

What we lack today is clear ownership of strategy, release gates and shared quality telemetry, plus a low-friction path for engineers to spend their testing effort on the highest-risk scenarios.

How the role works

Your time splits between hands-on platform work, enablement, strategy and stakeholder telemetry. One insourced QA Engineer supports you. You own the technical direction, the standards and the quality outcomes.

Once the platform has low friction, product engineers write and maintain the tests for the domains they own. You enable that through patterns, docs, reusable modules, CI checks and risk-based guidance. Gatekeeping releases sits outside the role.

Expect no direct people-management responsibilities in the near future. Any further QE hire gets evaluated against the ~1:50 rule once the value is proven, and we have no committed headcount plan beyond that.

What you'll own

Quality strategy and platform

  • Own the quality strategy and the automation platform across products, covering direction, standards and day-to-day health

  • Decide whether to keep, evolve or replace the current tooling, with clear trade-offs on speed, maintainability and DX

  • Set coding standards and patterns for test code, and keep the suite focused on the tests that earn their place

Release gates and telemetry

  • Build automated release gates into CI/CD and define what protects the core journeys

  • Give Product, Engineering and leadership real-time quality telemetry on release readiness, risk and pipeline health

  • Put failure triage and flaky-test quarantine in place, so every failure is worth acting on

Risk-based coverage and testability

  • Work with Product and Engineering to protect high-impact journeys and APIs

  • Retire flaky and low-value tests, and concentrate effort where the risk is highest

  • Act as the technical stakeholder for testability (hooks, mocks, contract tests, test data) and get those improvements onto team roadmaps

Developer enablement

  • Make it easy for product engineers to write, run and maintain tests locally and in CI

  • Embed quality into how teams plan and ship, and mentor the insourced QA Engineer

  • Drive a measurable increase in developer satisfaction with quality tooling and DX

  1. Platform ownership. You have taken over the automation platform across products and own it outright, with direction, standards and health all unambiguous, whether you kept the tooling or replaced it.

description:
Expansion Intern | Austria or Netherlands

Internship · Full-time · Berlin or Amsterdam

 

Our mission for you

Take trawa beyond borders!

As an Expansion Intern, you'll play a key role in taking trawa into new markets and will experience hands-on what it means to be an operator. You'll work across go-to-market, operations and product, and see up close what it takes to bring a fast-growing energy platform into a new country. We are hiring on a rolling basis, minimum duration is 3 months.

Two markets, one mission:

  • Austria: trawa is already live here, and you'll help scale the market: speeding up growth, sharpening our local positioning and turning our Austrian presence into a success story.

  • The Netherlands: trawa is preparing its Dutch market entry, and you'll help lay the foundations from day one: understanding the market, positioning trawa, supporting our first sales and commercial activities, and preparing everything for launch.

We staff you on the market where your profile and our needs fit best. Either way, you'll build something that truly matters.

 
 

What you'll do, whichever market you work on:

  • Supercharge local go-to-market: You research competitors, help define how trawa wins in your market and support early customer acquisition. Your work directly drives our local growth.

  • Turn regulation into a competitive edge: Energy markets change constantly. You track legal and regulatory updates, work out what they mean for trawa and help us adapt faster than anyone else.

  • Build local operations: You support product rollouts, from contract frameworks to processes, and help adapt what works at our Berlin HQ to the local market.

  • Shape the product for new markets: You bring local customer and market insights into our product team and help make sure trawa fits the needs of businesses in your country.

  • Become the market expert: You run ad-hoc analyses, build market overviews and quickly become the go-to person for everything specific to your country.

  • Collaborate with leadership: You work closely with our expansion leads and senior leadership. You take ownership of your own initiatives and see them through from idea to execution.

  • You are a true team player: You understand that humility and performance go hand in hand, and that what counts is the overall success of the team.

 

Who we are looking for

Standout candidates who want to grow with us:

  • Advanced Bachelor's student, in your gap year, Master's student, or recent graduate with outstanding academic achievements.

  • You have a strong track record. Analytical skills, an entrepreneurial mindset and a high degree of independence set you apart.

  • You’re highly motivated, hands-on, and eager to take real responsibility.

  • You have first practical experience in a dynamic startup, top-tier strategy consultancy or investment banking.

  • You're curious about the energy transition and are not scared of legal texts.

Market-specific requirements:

  • Austrian team: You are fluent in English and German (C1 or higher), and you're based in or willing to move to Berlin.

  • Dutch team: You are fluent in English, German and Dutch are a plus, and you're based in or willing to move to Amsterdam.

 

Why us?

  • Your impact: Your work has a direct influence on how trawa grows across Europe, and you get to help shape a new market from the ground up.

  • Flexible working: We foster a vibrant company culture where we love to work together, and home office is also an option. With flexible working hours and 30 vacation days, we support your work-life balance.

  • Attractive benefits: In addition to a competitive salary, you'll receive lunch vouchers, a learning and development budget and an Urban Sports Club membership.

  • Diversity & inclusion: Everyone is welcome at trawa! We are committed to an inclusive workplace that values diversity. We actively encourage people of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, ethnic backgrounds, and physical or neurodiverse abilities to apply.

  • Application process: You'll receive feedback within a week. The process includes interviews, a practical challenge and conversations with our team.

Don't worry if you don't meet every single requirement. If you're excited about the role and our mission, we want to hear from you!

 

About us

trawa is a fast-growing energy start-up that is revolutionizing the way businesses procure and manage their energy consumption and costs. Our mission is to make sustainable energy accessible and affordable for every business. We are seeking talented individuals who are passionate about making a positive impact and contributing to our shared success.

As our Engineer - Data & Platforms (m/f/d), you build and run the internal data products that our investment team, Quantitative Research and AI Engineering rely on every day: the pipelines, datasets, APIs and tools that turn a large and growing pool of financial and alternative data into something investors can act on.   • Clear communication with non-engineers: you can explain what you built, why, and what it will and will not do, and you can say no constructively.

Stell dir nun vor, du begibst dich auf eine spannende Reise mit Valiantys und Atlassian – eine Reise, auf der Innovation keine Grenzen kennt und dein Beitrag im Mittelpunkt steht.
 

Als Principal Transformation Consultant übernimmst du eine strategische Rolle beim Aufbau wichtiger Kundenbeziehungen, bei der Umsetzung komplexer Transformationsprogramme und beim Ausbau unseres Geschäfts.

Du arbeitest eng mit Senior Executives zusammen, um Transformationsstrategien zu definieren und umzusetzen. Dazu gehören Cloud-Migrationen, technologische Modernisierung und unternehmensweite digitale Initiativen.

Diese Rolle verbindet strategisches Consulting, Business Development und technologische Führung. Ein wesentlicher Teil deiner Aufgabe ist consultative selling. Du identifizierst geschäftliche Herausforderungen, entwickelst überzeugende Value Propositions und wandelst Opportunities in erfolgreiche Kundenprojekte um.

Mit deinem Verständnis für Enterprise Software Delivery, den Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) und moderne Engineering Practices hilfst du unseren Kunden, ihre Transformation zu beschleunigen und gleichzeitig die Präsenz von Valiantys in strategischen Accounts auszubauen.

Du berichtest an den Transformation Consulting Director.

Kundenpartnerschaft & Projektdelivery

Technologie & Transformation

  • Du berätst Kunden dabei, ihre Software Delivery zu verbessern. Dabei nutzt du dein starkes Verständnis des Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC), Developer Experience (DevEx), agiler Delivery, DevOps und moderner Engineering Practices.

Consultative-Led Selling & Business Development

Solution Design & Value Creation

title: Senior Account Executive – DACH

This is a remote-first role based anywhere in Germany, with occasional travel (roughly 10% of your time) for in-person customer or team moments — proximity to our HQ in Tutzing is a plus, not a requirement. We encourage applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of gender identity.

You’ll join a 15-person DACH sales team managing a shared base of 2,000+ existing customers, while also building new business from scratch. We need someone equally comfortable opening a brand-new account and growing one we already have — commercially sharp, technically curious, and credible with both IT stakeholders and business buyers.


You’ll get to take ownership of:

  • New-business hunting: proactively sourcing and closing new-logo accounts across Germany, Austria and Switzerland — sourcing matters as much as closing here.
  • An existing account book: owning and growing a slice of our 2,000+ customer base in DACH, spotting expansion and renewal opportunities alongside your new-business work.
  • Technically credible selling: running discovery and value conversations on data integration, EDI and supply-chain workflows, engaging both IT stakeholders and business buyers like supply chain and logistics leaders.
  • Full sales-cycle ownership: qualification through close, with accountability for your own pipeline health, forecasting accuracy, and ACV.
  • Direct, no-partner-model selling: this territory is direct sales only — you own the relationship end to end, with no channel hand-offs.
  • Staying sharp with AI-assisted tooling: our sales workflow uses AI agents for company research and a lead-scoring system, so you spend your time on conversations that matter.


We’d love to meet someone with:

  • 5+ years of closing experience in B2B software sales, with a track record you can back up — we check references and verified numbers, not just a good story.
  • A genuine blend of hunting and farming: you’ve opened new accounts from scratch, and you’ve grown an existing book — not just one or the other.
  • Technical fluency: comfortable in front of IT managers, EDI owners and integration leads, and able to translate that into a business case for a non-technical buyer.
  • A platform or data-integration background is a strong plus over point-solution SaaS experience — the independent, use-case-driven selling here is a different motion.
  • Domain exposure to logistics, manufacturing or retail is a nice-to-have, not a requirement.
  • German native or C1+ level, with fluent English (our internal working language; HQ in Germany).

If you’re excited about this role but don’t meet every qualification, we encourage you to apply!

Lobster is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive environment where empathy and respect guide our interactions



You can look forward to:

  • A personal, 100% individual quota — no team target to hide behind, and no partner deals to lean on either.
  • A fast, low-politics culture that rewards performance quickly: a quarterly bonus plus a year-end accelerator.
  • Remote-first flexibility across Germany, with purposeful travel rather than a fixed office routine.
  • A genuinely technical product to sell — not another horizontal SaaS tool.
  • A personal learning and development budget
  • 30 vacation days per year
  • Up to 20 days of remote work per year from any EU country
  • Bike leasing through our partnership with JobRad
  • Team evenings every Thursday, with refreshments covered by the company
  • A company pension plan (bAV)
  • Subsidised lunches and a modern office with a view of Lake Starnberg in Tutzing, for the days you're on-site

title: (Senior) Economist für Energiemärkte (w/m/d) bei Dezernat Zukunft – Institut für Makrofinanzen
description:
Wer wir sind und was wir suchen

Ob die Energiewende gelingt, entscheidet sich nicht allein an Technologien, sondern an Kosten, Märkten und politischen Weichenstellungen. Genau dazu arbeitet das Energy Lab des Dezernat Zukunft – und um unsere Arbeit weiter zu vertiefen, suchen wir Dich. 

Das Dezernat Zukunft ist ein überparteilicher Berliner Think Tank an der Schnittstelle von Politik, Verwaltung und Forschung. Rund 30 Personen verfolgen gemeinsam das Ziel, Geld-, Finanz- und Wirtschaftspolitik neu zu denken und verständlich zu vermitteln. Geleitet von den Werten Würde, Wohlstand, Demokratie und Nachhaltigkeit suchen wir zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt – idealerweise ab dem 1. Januar – für unser Energy Lab eine Person als (Senior) Economist für Energiemärkte. 

In dieser Position konzipierst Du Analysen und Studien zu Energiemärkten – insbesondere zum Strommarkt – und führst sie eigenständig durch. Dabei betrachtest Du Energiekosten, Investitionsbedarfe, Gesamtsystemkosten sowie die Wechselwirkungen politischer Instrumente mit diesen Größen. Im Mittelpunkt stehen die Fragen, wie sich Energiepolitik mit Wettbewerbsfähigkeit, Nachhaltigkeit und Bezahlbarkeit zusammendenken lässt, wie Energiekosten strategisch und gezielt gesenkt werden können, und wie das regulatorische Umfeld so ausgestaltet werden kann, dass es den Erfolg der „zweiten Hälfte der Energiewende“ und damit die Erreichung der Klimaneutralität ermöglicht.


Deine Aufgaben

  • Du analysierst Energiemärkte und -preise, einschließlich Systemkosten, und koordinierst dazu Forschungsprojekte. Dabei betrachtest Du auch fiskalpolitische Auswirkungen sowie Wechselwirkungen mit dem Stromnetzausbau. 
  • Du entwickelst konkrete Politikvorschläge, Analysen und Positionen zu den oben genannten Themen, in enger Zusammenarbeit mit Deinen Kolleg:innen im Energy Lab des Dezernat Zukunft sowie den weiteren Teams der Organisation. Außerdem organisierst Du Expert:innen-Gespräche und andere inhaltliche Veranstaltungen. 
  • Du interagierst aktiv mit Vertreter:innen von Parlamenten, Regierungen, Wissenschaft, Wirtschaft und Medien. Unsere Arbeit funktioniert nur dann, wenn wir mit diesen Gruppen im Austausch stehen, zuhören und zusammenarbeiten.


Das bieten wir

  • Eine Vergütung in Anlehnung an den Tarifvertrag des öffentlichen Dienstes (TVöD): Eingruppierung in Entgeltgruppe E 13 – abhängig von Deiner Erfahrung – inkl. Jahressonderzahlung und 30 Urlaubstagen.
  • Aktive Unterstützung bei Deiner Weiterentwicklung – fachlich sowie in Bezug auf Kompetenzen, Netzwerke und Aufgaben. 
  • Einen Arbeitsplatz in Berlin-Mitte mit der Möglichkeit zum mobilen Arbeiten und gemeinsam vereinbarten Kernzeiten.
  • Unbürokratische, verständnisvolle Regelungen bei kurzfristigen Care-Bedarfen; bezahlte Freistellung nach § 29 TVöD bei persönlichen Anlässen (z. B. kranke Kinder). 
  • Einen Zuschuss zum Deutschlandticket oder JobRad. 
  • Und nicht zuletzt: Ein dynamisches,motiviertes Team, gemeinsame Events (z. B. Berg- oder Paddel-Ausflüge) und Arbeit, die zählt. 


Dein Profil

  • Du teilst unsere Werte und Ziele, begeisterst Dich für Energie- und Klimapolitik und brennst dafür, dass die Transformation gelingt. 
  • Du hast einen Master-Abschluss in einem relevanten Fachgebiet sowie mindestens zwei Jahre einschlägige Berufserfahrung. Du kennst Dich in Energiemärkten – insbesondere im Strommarkt – aus, verstehst politische Instrumente und erkennst, welche Zahlen für politische Entscheidungen und ökonomische Weichenstellungen wirklich zählen. 
  • Du konzipierst und erstellst eigene Analysen – quantitativ wie textlich – selbstständig und gründlich. Du hast bereits erfolgreich Forschungsprojekte umgesetzt und Ergebnisse sowie politische Handlungsempfehlungen prägnant kommuniziert. Du bist Dir bewusst, dass unsere Analysen und Vorschläge in der Öffentlichkeit intensiv geprüft werden, und arbeitest entsprechend gewissenhaft und bist bereit, als Eigentümer:in für Deine Projekte einzustehen.
  • Du kommunizierst sehr gut in deutscher und englischer Sprache und verfasst in beiden Sprachen anspruchsvolle, gut verständliche Texte.
  • Du hast fortgeschrittene Kenntnisse in der praktischen Anwendung gängiger KI-Programme. 
  • Du willst den Dingen auf den Grund gehen und jeden Tag dazulernen. Noch wichtiger als mitgebrachtes Wissen ist für uns die Fähigkeit, es zu erweitern und Meinungen zu ändern. 
  • Du arbeitest gern im Team, hörst zu und unterstützt und förderst Deine Kolleg:innen.
Die perfekte Kandidat:in erfüllt nicht immer jede Anforderung. Wenn Du glaubst, dass Du zu uns passt – bewirb Dich gern trotzdem und sag uns, warum.


Beschäftigungsbeginn & Vertragsbedingungen

  • Beginn: Von uns aus so schnell wie möglich. Im Anschluss an das Bewerbungsverfahren rechnen wir mit einem Start im Januar 2027. Das genaue Startdatum ist verhandelbar. 
  • Umfang: 32–39 Stunden/Woche (flexibel je nach Deiner Verfügbarkeit). 
  • Befristung: zunächst 1 Jahr (Entfristung nach zwei Jahren angestrebt).


Bewerbungsverfahren

Bitte bewirb Dich online mit Lebenslauf und einem kurzen Anschreiben, das Deine Eignung entlang der oben genannten Kriterien zeigt. Bitte teile uns auch mit, wie Du auf die Stelle aufmerksam geworden bist und welche Wochenarbeitszeit Du bevorzugen würdest. 

Bewerbungsfrist: 08. November 2026

Das Bewerbungsverfahren besteht aus drei Runden: im ersten Schritt einem Assessment-Test, der aus einer schriftlichen Aufgabe besteht und ca. 1-2 Stunden Arbeitszeit beansprucht; anschließend ein längeres Gespräch bei uns vor Ort im Büro und einem abschließenden Gespräch mit unserem Head of Energy Lab – Janek Steitz.

Wir schätzen Vielfalt und möchten die Diversität unseres Teams fördern. Bewerbungen sind willkommen – unabhängig von Geschlecht, Nationalität, kultureller oder sozialer Herkunft, Religion, Weltanschauung, Alter sowie sexueller Orientierung und Identität.

description:

Genetec - Protect the everyday

Wir sind ein weltweit tätiges kanadisches Unternehmen mit einem breit gefächerten Lösungsportfolio in den Bereichen Sicherheit, Intelligence und Operations. Unsere Kunden kommen aus unterschiedlichsten Branchen, darunter Transport, Bildung und öffentliche Verwaltung. Unser globales Netzwerk von mehr als 2.300 Mitarbeitenden setzt sich aus vielfältigen Persönlichkeiten zusammen, die ihre Arbeit mit Leidenschaft ausüben und offen für neue Ideen sind. Der Erfolg und das Wohlbefinden unserer Mitarbeitenden haben für uns höchste Priorität. Entdecken Sie das Arbeitsumfeld und die lebendige Unternehmenskultur von Genetec in diesem Video: - hier.

Ihre Aufgaben

Als Channel Account Executive (CAE) DACH sind Sie verantwortlich für den Ausbau, die Betreuung und das Wachstum des Genetec-Geschäfts mit bestehenden und neuen Vertriebspartnern in Deutschland, Österreich und der Schweiz. In enger Zusammenarbeit mit Channel Sales Engineers, Account Executives, Marketing sowie weiteren internen Teams stärken Sie die Fähigkeiten unserer Partner, schaffen nachhaltiges Pipeline- und Umsatzwachstum und stellen eine konsistente Partnererfahrung sicher. Die Position berichtet direkt an den Area Sales Director DACH.

  • Ausbau des Channel-Geschäfts in der DACH-Region durch die Entwicklung gemeinsamer Geschäftspläne, Umsatzziele und gezielter Wachstumsinitiativen mit ausgewählten Partnern.
  • Betreuung, Unterstützung und Weiterentwicklung bestehender strategischer Channel- und Lösungspartner sowie Identifikation und Gewinnung neuer Vertriebspartner in der DACH-Region mit besonderem Fokus auf Deutschland.
  • Aufbau und Pflege einer belastbaren, partnergenerierten Vertriebspipeline; Erstellung von Umsatzprognosen sowie regelmäßiges Reporting zu Strategie, Fortschritten, Risiken und Wettbewerbsentwicklungen an das Management.
  • Weiterleitung und Nachverfolgung von Leads gemeinsam mit Partnern, Sicherstellung der Erfassung und Pflege von Opportunities im CRM-System sowie Überwachung von Projekten, die nicht als High-Touch-Deals durch die Account-Executive-Organisation geführt werden.
  • Enge Zusammenarbeit mit Account Executives und Channel Sales Engineers bei der Betreuung von Kundenkonten, der Entwicklung von Vertriebsstrategien, der Auswahl geeigneter Partner und der erfolgreichen Umsetzung von Kundenprojekten.
  • Koordination der Kommunikation zwischen Vertriebspartnern, Genetec-Abteilungen, Beratern und Technologiepartnern, um einen konsistenten und skalierbaren Go-to-Market-Ansatz sicherzustellen.
  • Planung und Durchführung von Partner-Reviews, Vertriebsenablement-Maßnahmen, Veranstaltungen und gezielten Marketinginitiativen; Koordination technischer Schulungen sowie Überwachung von Trainingserfolg und Partnerzufriedenheit.

Ihr Profil

Wir freuen uns über Bewerbungen aller qualifizierten Kandidatinnen und Kandidaten, auch wenn nicht jede einzelne Anforderung vollständig erfüllt wird. Wenn Sie von dieser Rolle begeistert sind und überzeugt sind, einen Mehrwert leisten zu können, möchten wir Sie gerne kennenlernen.

  • Nachgewiesene Erfahrung im Aufbau neuer Channel-Partnerschaften sowie in der Geschäftsentwicklung mit Systemintegratoren und anderen Lösungspartnern.
  • Fundiertes Verständnis des Marktes für physische Sicherheit, einschließlich Videomanagement-Software, Zutrittskontrollsystemen und der dazugehörigen IT-Infrastruktur.
  • Kenntnisse von VSaaS- (Video Surveillance as a Service) und Cloud-Strategien sowie von direkten Hersteller-zu-Partner-Vertriebsmodellen.
  • Erfahrung in der gemeinsamen Geschäftsplanung mit Partnern, im Opportunity-Management, Forecasting sowie im professionellen Umgang mit CRM-Systemen.
  • Fähigkeit, den Mehrwert der Genetec-Lösungen überzeugend zu vermitteln und Produkt-, Markt- sowie Wettbewerbswissen in konkreten Geschäftsnutzen für Partner zu übersetzen.
  • Ausgeprägte Präsentations-, Kommunikations-, Verhandlungs- und zwischenmenschliche Fähigkeiten sowie eine strukturierte, eigenverantwortliche und teamorientierte Arbeitsweise.
  • Deutsch auf muttersprachlichem Niveau sowie verhandlungssichere Englischkenntnisse; zusätzliche Kenntnisse der DACH-Märkte sind von Vorteil.
  • Reisebereitschaft innerhalb der DACH-Region von mindestens 50 % der Arbeitszeit.
  • Proaktive und eigenverantwortliche Arbeitsweise mit unternehmerischem Denken, Ergebnisorientierung und Freude an Herausforderungen.
  • Positive Ausstrahlung und hohe Energie, die zur Förderung von Teamarbeit, Engagement und einer starken Teamkultur beiträgt.
  • Freude an der Arbeit in einem vielfältigen und internationalen Team.

Das bieten wir Ihnen

  • Die Möglichkeit, in einem internationalen und kooperativen Umfeld einen echten Beitrag zu leisten.
  • Eine Unternehmenskultur, die Kreativität, frische Ideen und das Hinterfragen des Status quo fördert.
  • Die Chance, Teil eines weltweit führenden Unternehmens mit einer offenen und unterstützenden Arbeitsatmosphäre zu werden.
  • Zugang zu zahlreichen Vergünstigungen über unser Corporate-Discount-Programm.
  • Kostenlose Französischkurse zur Förderung der internationalen Zusammenarbeit.
  • Teilnahme an internationalen Teamevents und Konferenzen sowie Aufbau wertvoller länderübergreifender Netzwerke.
  • Attraktives Provisionsmodell zur Anerkennung Ihres Beitrags zum Unternehmenserfolg.
  • Kfz-Zuschuss zur Unterstützung Ihrer Reisetätigkeit innerhalb der Region.
  • 30 Urlaubstage für eine gesunde Work-Life-Balance.
  • Zuschuss zu Fitness- und Gesundheitsangeboten zur Förderung Ihres Wohlbefindens.

Genetec ist ein Arbeitgeber, der Chancengleichheit fördert. Wir diskriminieren niemanden aufgrund von ethnischer Herkunft, Geschlecht, Hautfarbe, Religion, Alter, Nationalität, Familienstand, Behinderung, Veteranenstatus, genetischer Informationen, sexueller Orientierung, Geschlechtsidentität oder eines anderen gesetzlich geschützten Merkmals.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

We are a global Canadian company with a broad solutions portfolio that encompasses security, intelligence, and operations. We serve customers within a wide range of industries including transportation, education, and government. At Genetec we embrace open communication, creativity, and continuous learning to allow everyone to flourish in their own unique career paths.

Our network of over 2300 people globally is made up of diverse individuals who are passionate about their work and open to trying new ideas. We prioritize the success and well-being of our employees. Discover Genetec's work environment and lively culture in this video - here.

What your day will look like

As Channel Account Executive (CAE) DACH, you will be responsible for developing, managing and growing Genetec business with existing and new channel partners across Germany, Austria and Switzerland. Working closely with Channel Sales Engineers, Account Executives, Marketing and other internal teams, you will strengthen partner capability, create sustainable pipeline and revenue growth, and ensure a consistent partner experience. The role reports directly to the Area Sales Director DACH.

  • Grow channel sales across the DACH territory by developing joint business plans, revenue objectives and targeted growth initiatives with selected partners.
  • Manage, support and further develop existing strategic Channel and solution partners, while identifying and onboarding new channel relationships across the DACH region. Strong Focus on Germany
  • Build and maintain a reliable partner-generated pipeline; develop channel revenue forecasts and regularly report strategy, progress, risks and competitive developments to management.
  • Distribute and follow up leads with partners, ensure opportunities are captured and updated in CRM, and track projects that are not managed as High-Touch deals by the Account Executive organisation.
  • Work closely with Account Executives and Channel Sales Engineers on account coverage, opportunity strategy, partner selection and the successful delivery of customer projects.
  • Coordinate communication between channel partners, Genetec departments, consultants and technology partners to create a consistent and scalable go-to-market approach.
  • Plan and deliver partner business reviews, sales enablement, events and targeted marketing initiatives; coordinate technical training and monitor training effectiveness and partner satisfaction.

 

About you

We welcome all qualified candidates, including those who may not meet every listed requirement. If you're excited about this role and believe you can make an impact, we’d love to hear from you.

  • At least 7 years of experience in sales and/or business development within physical security, technology or solution sales, including at least 3 years in a relevant channel or business development role.
  • Proven ability to develop new channel relationships and grow business with system integrators and other solution partners.
  • Strong understanding of the physical security market, including video management software, access control systems and related IT infrastructure.
  • Understanding of VSaaS and cloud solution strategies as well as direct manufacturer-to-partner channel models.
  • Experience with partner business planning, opportunity management, revenue forecasting and CRM discipline.
  • Ability to understand and articulate the Genetec value proposition and to translate product, market and competitive knowledge into partner-facing business value.
  • Excellent presentation, communication, interpersonal and negotiation skills, combined with a structured, self-driven and collaborative working style.
  • Native-level German and business-fluent English; additional DACH market knowledge is a strong advantage.
  • Willingness to travel within the DACH region for a minimum of 50% of working time.
  • You proactively manage your responsibilities, embrace challenges, and drive meaningful outcomes through an entrepreneurial and results-oriented approach.
  • A positive attitude and high energy, helping to drive teamwork, engagement, and a strong team culture.
  • Exited to work in a diverse Team

 

What’s in it for you

  • Make a meaningful impact in an international and collaborative environment.
  • Be part of a culture that values creativity, fresh ideas, and challenging the status quo.
  • Join an industry-leading global company with a supportive and open atmosphere.
  • Access a wide range of partner perks through our Corporate Discount Program.
  • Enhance your international collaboration with French language classes.
  • Participate in international team events and conferences, building strong cross-regional connections.
  • Benefit from an Employee Commission Plan that recognizes your contribution to business success.
  • Receive a car allowance to support travel across the region.
  • Enjoy 30 days of vacation to maintain a healthy work-life balance.
  • Take advantage of our Fitness Club contribution to support your well-being.
