title: Applied Research Engineer, Evaluation
description:
About Black Forest Labs

We're the team behind Latent Diffusion, Stable Diffusion, and FLUX — foundational technologies that changed how the world creates images and videos. Our FLUX models are among the most advanced in the world, and we're just getting started.

Headquartered in Freiburg, Germany with a growing presence in San Francisco, we're scaling fast while staying true to what makes us different: research excellence, open science, and building technology that expands human creativity.

Why This Role

Frontier image and video models are now good enough that the hard question is no longer whether they work, but whether a new one is actually better, and how you'd know. Aesthetics, prompt following, editing fidelity, text rendering, character consistency: none of these collapse into a single number, and public benchmarks have fallen well behind the models they're meant to measure.

You'll work on the system BFL uses to answer that question. Every FLUX checkpoint, every finetuning and RL run, and every competitor release goes through our evaluation stack, and you'll help build and sharpen it. Product Research relies on what it shows to decide what to fix next, and to confirm the fix worked.

It gets harder from here. FLUX 3 is our first multimodal model, spanning image, video, audio and action, and each new modality needs its own way of being measured.

What You'll Work On

What you focus on will depend on where you're strongest and what the team needs most when you join.

In scope:

  • Building and maintaining the evaluation stack that every model checkpoint has to pass through and prove itself on, from automated benchmarking and LLM-as-judge pipelines, to human evaluation through panels (Prolific and otherwise).

  • Designing the breadth of evaluation across the taxonomy, from prompt adherence, editing fidelity, aesthetics, text rendering, subject and character consistency, to safety.

  • Evaluating the evaluation stack itself: checking that human and automated evals agree, that results stay stable over time, and improving them when they don't.

  • Benchmarking FLUX against the frontier models continuously, while obtaining a meaningful perspective on where we are better or worse than competitors and what such differences really mean.

  • Finding the ways in which the quality of the model's output falls short that are not captured by aggregate numbers.

  • Closing the loop, ideally, with the RL and finetuning researchers, by defining target metrics for them to aim for, and verifying that a new checkpoint improved the weakness without introducing new ones.

  • Designing how best to exploit the signals we already capture through the API and MCP, and what new signals we should capture, with help from research, data engineering and legal.

  • Maintaining the usefulness of existing metrics as their natural lifecycle brings up concerns of gaming and overfitting, and anticipating this for new metrics.

What We're Looking For

You have made meaningful contributions to the evaluation of generative models already. You understand that a benchmark figure without careful consideration of sample size and judge agreement with humans is at best uninformed optimism and at worst dangerously misleading, and you have been the person that found that inconvenient regression that nobody wanted to talk about.

You likely have:

  • Advanced degree (MS/PhD) in a relevant field or demonstrated equivalent practical experience

  • Practical experience with evaluating generative models, in a hands-on way. You may have worked with diffusion or flow-matching based image or video models already, but the capability to evaluate them in earnest transfers to other modalities too

  • Very strong Python and software engineering skills, with pipelines that run reliably and that other people can read if needed

  • Working knowledge of PyTorch and modern ML infrastructure and practices; you are not a pure Python developer, you know what the modern ML code looks like

  • Strong grasp of statistics and its shortcomings in practice, and how to work with those; sample sizes, inter-annotator agreement, confidence levels, etc., and a healthy skepticism about what those numbers say about the world

  • Practical experience with building and operating LLM-as-judge systems, and understanding their limitations

  • Working knowledge of modern benchmarking practices and of standard datasets and benchmarks in the field already; you have an idea of which to trust and which to disregard

  • The inclination to look at the actual outputs your system is judging, and to care about what is there beyond an aggregate score

We'd be especially excited if you:

  • Have practical experience with human evaluation, including study design and execution via panels, and analysis of disagreements and annotator performance

  • Have worked where evaluation meets training (reward models, preference data, RLHF, DPO or similar) and know that whatever you optimize for is what the model learns

  • Have evaluated agentic or multi-step systems and know how hard it is to attribute success or failure to a single step

  • Have built tools that people actually want to use internally

  • Have made public contributions to the field: papers, open source, or otherwise

How We Work Together

  • Bold. We take the ambitious bet. We ship, we do not wait for conditions to be perfect.

Über uns

Über 5 Millionen Menschen in Deutschland sind pflegebedürftig, und jedes Jahr werden es mehr. Ihnen stehen Leistungen zu, die oft nie ankommen, weil Formulare, Zuständigkeiten und Behördensprache dazwischenstehen.

Jeden Fall einzeln zu prüfen und bis zur Entscheidung zu begleiten, war bisher zu aufwendig. Mit KI geht das zum ersten Mal für viele Familien gleichzeitig. Genau das macht Decari: Wir prüfen, welche Leistungen infrage kommen, etwa ein höherer Pflegegrad, Hilfe zur Pflege oder Eingliederungshilfe, und begleiten die Anträge bis zur Entscheidung. Pflegedienste in mehreren Bundesländern arbeiten bereits mit uns. Unser Ziel: Jede Familie in Deutschland bekommt die Pflegeleistungen, die ihr zusteht.

Wir sind ein kleines, AI-natives Team mit Erfahrung aus der Versicherungs- und Pflegebranche. Wir waren frühe Mitarbeiter in Startups, die von Sequoia, Accel, Index Ventures und Y Combinator finanziert wurden und zusammen über 100 Mio. Euro eingesammelt haben. Neue Ideen testen wir erst einfach und von Hand, was funktioniert, automatisieren wir, und unsere Abläufe ändern wir jede Woche, manchmal täglich. Wir übernehmen Ownership und haben wenig Ego.

Deine Rolle

In deiner Operations & Growth Rolle baust du Decari mit uns auf. Du arbeitest direkt mit Julien (Operations) und den Gründern und bist operativ und taktisch mittendrin: Du sprichst jeden Tag mit Familien und Pflegediensten, siehst, wo es hakt, und gestaltest den Prozess aktiv mit.

Was du machst

  • Du bist der erste Kontakt der Familien zu Decari und verbringst den größten Teil deines Tages am Telefon. Im Gespräch findest du heraus, ob und wie wir helfen können.

  • Du bringst Fälle ins Ziel. Aus einem guten Gespräch machst du einen vollständigen Fall und bleibst dran, bis alles da ist, was wir für den Antrag brauchen.

  • Du betreust unsere Pflegedienste mit. Für sie bist du die erste Ansprechperson zu ihren Familien.

  • Du verbesserst den Funnel. Du kennst die Zahlen von der Anfrage bis zum Antrag, bringst Ideen ein und testest sie direkt.

  • Du baust mit uns Automatisierungen. Was wir oft genug von Hand gemacht haben, übernimmt danach die KI.

Du passt gut zu uns, wenn

  • Du gern telefonierst, auch 50 Mal am Tag, und dich eine Mailbox oder ein Nein nicht aus dem Takt bringt

  • Du gut zuhörst, empathisch bist und schnell und fehlerfrei schreibst

  • Du anpackst und dir für unglamouröse Arbeit nicht zu schade bist

Description

Legartis is on a mission: to unlock legal work at scale.

We set the standard for AI-powered contract work by offering a platform that changes how legal teams work, from drafting through negotiation to completion. We are now looking for the person who turns what customers actually need into what our AI actually does.

Send us your CV, a short note on why Legartis, and links to anything you have built or published.


Your mission

Most companies split this seat across three teams, and that split is exactly the problem. The person who hears the customer describe their workflow should be the person who writes the requirement, and the person who writes the requirement should be able to build the first version themselves. That is you.

1. You translate customer reality into engineering requirements — and into revenue. You sit in customer and expert calls alongside Sales, not as a note-taker but as the person who understands the legal work. In trials and hackathons you coach hands-on: the customer drives, you navigate, and they create the first "wow" moment themselves. When they say "that won't work for us" or "we'll build it ourselves", you answer with a concrete path (a workaround, a workflow, the honest maintenance cost of the alternative) and you leave every conversation with a next step: trial licenses, a hackathon, a scoped rollout. Then you pull out the workflow: what actually happens, in what order, where it breaks, what the customer would pay to never do again. And you write the spec, edge cases, and acceptance criteria that Engineering can build against.

2. You build the skills yourself. You write, test, and ship agent skills and playbooks that solve real customer workflows. You build the evaluation frameworks and test sets that prove they got better rather than just different. When the AI fails on a clause, you diagnose why, at the prompt and context level, and you either fix it or hand Engineering a diagnosis precise enough to act on.

3. You make it repeatable, and therefore sellable. Anything you build once for one customer, you turn into something Sales and Customer Success can run without you. Standard demo environments. A skill library they can reach for. Onboarding that lands in days rather than months. Where Customer Success needs legal depth you step in, fix it, and turn the fix into something the team can handle alone next time. Your success is measured by how rarely you need to be in the room, and by what happens to adoption and expansion when you are not.

4. You are the legal authority in the building. Legal and compliance questions land with you: contract reviews, customer security and data protection questions, the occasional in-house matter which makes roughly ten to fifteen percent of your time. You use our own product to do it, and you tell us honestly when it is not good enough.


Your profile

The person we picture. There is a name emerging for what we are describing, and it is not "lawyer who is good with computers". It is legal quant: a lawyer who builds their own tooling to practise law, rather than waiting for a vendor to ship it. The distinction that matters to us: plenty of lawyers now use AI. A legal quant builds with it. They look at a workflow and ask how to redesign it from first principles to get the best possible outcome, rather than making the existing process incrementally faster.

A note on how we are weighting this role. Three capabilities make someone exceptional here: commercial instinct, legal depth, and technical ability to build. The ideal candidate has all three. We know that person is rare, and we are not going to pretend otherwise by writing a wish list and hoping. So for this role we weight the technical evidence most heavily, because it is the hardest of the three to teach on the job.

If you believe you genuinely combine all three, we want to talk to you regardless of how neatly your CV matches the bullets below. Say so in your note and tell us what you have built and what you have sold.

1. Technical track record. You have built things and they exist and ideally you have published some of it. You are fluent with LLMs the way a practitioner is fluent, not a spectator: you know how context windows fail you or why a prompt stopped working. When something breaks you go into the system rather than around it. Scripting, Git, and APIs are a strong plus.

2. Legal foundation. A law degree with a commercial-contracts focus: German-qualified (Bachelor, Master, or Staatsexamen) or an equivalent qualification from another jurisdiction. No bar admission required, no second Staatsexamen required. What we need: you have worked hands-on with German commercial contracts, drafting, reviewing, and negotiating them, and you can hold a conversation with a General Counsel as a peer.

3. Commercial and entrepreneurial track record. You have carried commercial responsibility for something of your own: a freelance client base, a legal tech product, or a company you started. You know what it takes to win a client from a standing start and why "they did not understand the value" is never the customer's fault. If instead you have supported enterprise sales teams in demos, pilots, and expert calls, tell us what you changed about the outcome.

You prioritise by impact, you are comfortable deciding without permission, and you would rather ship something imperfect this week than something elegant next quarter.

4. Language. Excellent German and English. German is non-negotiable: our customers are DACH legal teams and the nuance lives in their language. You can run a room of legal buyers, ask the sharp question, and write a specification precise enough to build from. Other EU languages are a plus.


Why us?

  • Impact over hype. You define a new discipline at the intersection of law, product, and AI. Your work directly shapes how thousands of legal professionals will operate.
  • No silos. You sit between Product, Engineering, and the customer, with a direct line to all three. The better argument wins, not the higher title.

  • Offices in Berlin, Leipzig, and Zurich with a flexible hybrid setup. Regular apéros, lunches, and hiking trips as we enjoy the journey together.

title: AI Harness Engineer - Agentic & Autonomous Operations (m/f/x)
description:
xHeron is building the Service-as-Software company for short-term rental operators. We take responsibility for guest communication, team coordination and issue resolution, so customers can hand over the work without handing over their business.

Today, we deliver that service through people, software and AI. We’re turning the expertise behind it into autonomous systems that understand situations, take action and follow through. Not another tool to supervise. A service that gets the job done.

We’re looking for an AI Engineer to build the agentic capabilities at the heart of xHeron. You’ll help shape how our agents reason, act and learn, and build a company where AI doesn’t just support the work, but increasingly delivers it.

Tasks

We are looking for an AI Harness Engineer to build the software layer that turns language models into dependable operational systems.

You will work on orchestration, context assembly, tool execution, state, permissions, evaluations, observability, failure recovery, and human handoffs. The goal is not merely to generate a good response.

What You’ll Own

  • Agent harness architecture: Build the control layer around models: task decomposition, state management, model and tool selection, execution loops, checkpoints, retries, stopping conditions, and human handoffs.
  • Decision and execution behavior: Design how agents interpret situations, choose actions, manage uncertainty, and complete bounded operational tasks—not only how they generate text.
  • Context and memory: Determine what an agent needs to know at each step. Build context assembly, retrieval, memory, evidence selection, and knowledge-maintenance strategies while managing relevance, latency, and cost.
  • Tools and real-world effects: Connect agents to APIs and operational systems through explicit tool contracts, permissions, validation, idempotency, and confirmation that the intended effect actually occurred.
  • Evaluation and regression testing: Build representative evaluation suites and automated tests for decision quality, tool use, task completion, safety, escalation behavior, and recurring failure patterns.
  • Observability and failure analysis: Make agent behavior inspectable through structured traces, state, outcomes, and error classification. Diagnose failures across models, prompts, context, tools, and surrounding software.
  • Continuous improvement: Use evaluations, production traces, operator feedback, and controlled experiments to improve prompts, context, tools, model choices, and agent architecture.
  • Production ownership: Ship and operate production Python software alongside our CTO and engineering team. Work closely with systems engineering on integrations, authorization, durable state, recovery, and safe execution.

Requirements

What Makes You a Great Fit

  • You are a strong software engineer who can design, build, test, and operate reliable production systems in Python.
  • You have built a substantial LLM-powered, automation, workflow, or decision system: not only notebooks, chat interfaces, prompt experiments, or a basic retrieval pipeline.
  • You understand the engineering layer around a model: orchestration, state, context, tools, structured outputs, permissions, retries, fallbacks, observability, and evaluations.
  • You can connect intelligence to real work: selecting relevant evidence, making a bounded decision, invoking tools or APIs, and verifying that the intended result occurred.
  • You design for partial failure and uncertainty. You think deliberately about when an agent should act, retry, wait, stop, ask for help, or escalate.
  • You evaluate behavior systematically. You use representative cases, traces, outcome checks, comparisons, and regression tests rather than treating a plausible response as proof of success.
  • You have shipped software that people or operational processes depend on and have worked through debugging, timeouts, inconsistent data, changing APIs, and production incidents.
  • You can investigate ambiguous problems independently, define a useful system boundary, explain trade-offs clearly, and turn decisions into working software.
  • You care about simplicity and control. You know when a deterministic workflow is better than an agent and when additional autonomy is justified by evidence.
  • You bring useful expertise and an independent perspective. Strong adjacent experience in workflow engines, developer tooling, distributed systems, automation platforms, or integration-heavy backend software can be highly relevant when paired with credible LLM-system understanding.

Around 2+ years of professional software-engineering experience is a useful guide, not a hard requirement. What matters is the technical depth of what you built, the decisions and production outcomes you owned, and your ability to learn unfamiliar systems.

You May Not Be a Great Fit If

  • Your LLM experience is mainly prompt engineering, chatbots, basic RAG, or connecting a model API to a user interface.
  • Your background is primarily offline data analysis, model training, or experimentation, and you do not want to own production software and operational behavior.
  • You treat retrieval as the complete agent architecture rather than one possible source of context within a larger execution system.
  • You consider a coherent model response successful without verifying the decision, tool call, state change, or real-world outcome.
  • You rely on an agent framework to provide the system design and are not comfortable reasoning about the control flow, state, permissions, and failure behavior underneath it.
  • You are not interested in owning evaluations, trace analysis, regression testing, and production learning alongside feature development.
  • You prefer fully scoped implementation tasks with stable requirements and limited responsibility for product or operational outcomes.

Benefits

Real ownership: you're not maintaining someone else's codebase, you're building a core, novel part of the product from the ground up.

  • Build at the core. Own a defining part of xHeron’s technology, from the first architectural decisions to production.
  • Shape the direction. Work directly with our CTO, challenge assumptions and help decide what we build, not just how.
  • Grow beyond the job description. We invest in your development, with room to expand your ownership and take on technical leadership as xHeron grows.
  • Share in the upside. Salary plus VSOP participation, so you can benefit from the value you help create.

Our Process

  • Intro call (15-30 min): a conversation with Friedrich (CTO) about your background, what you've built, and why this role.
  • Technical take-home case study: a short, real engineering problem, close to what you'd actually be building.
  • Case study interview (1 hour): you walk us through your thinking, not just the final code.
  • Culture fit (30 min): meet both Founders and make sure it's a fit both ways.

Wir haben letztes Jahr eine Pre-Seed-Finanzierung von über 1 Mio. € von führenden VCs der Baubranche sowie einem der größten Projektentwickler Deutschlands abgeschlossen.

75 % der Infrastruktur, die im Jahr 2050 existieren wird, ist heute noch nicht gebaut.

In dieser Rolle baust du die Maschine, während wir sie skalieren. Du sitzt im Zentrum der Firma, bekommst direkten Zugang zu Produkt, Kunden und Foundern – und trägst ab Tag eins echte Verantwortung.

🧱 Operational Backbone (≈ 1/3)

Du sorgst dafür, dass die Firma rund läuft und sauber mitwächst:

  • Hiring – Du unterstützt den gesamten Recruiting-Prozess: Stellenanzeigen, Sourcing, Pipeline-Pflege, Terminkoordination und Kandidaten-Kommunikation.

  • Operations – Du hältst unsere internen Abläufe, Tools und Dokumentation in Ordnung und schließt die Lücken, die im Alltag auffallen.

  • Produkt-Setups – Du richtest neue Kundenprojekte im Produkt ein, bereitest Projektdaten auf und stellst sicher, dass alles startklar ist.

  • AI-Setup der Company – Du hilfst, unsere internen KI-Workflows aufzubauen und zu pflegen, damit jedes Team mit den besten Tools und Automatisierungen arbeitet.

🚤 Speedboats (≈ 2/3)

Du übernimmst schnelle, eigenständige Projekte, die direkt auf Wachstum einzahlen – zum Beispiel:

  • Interne Prozesse mit Notion, Zapier oder n8n automatisieren

  • Go-to-Market-Experimente aufsetzen und neue Kundensegmente testen

  • Kunden-Discovery vorbereiten und Erkenntnisse verdichten

  • Bei Pricing-Fragen und strategischen Analysen zuarbeiten

Diese Rolle passt zu jemandem, der unternehmerisch denkt, mit Unsicherheit gut umgehen kann und eine Firma an der Schnittstelle von KI und echter Welt mitbauen will.

Requirements

Rahmen

  • Du bist eingeschriebene:r Student:in oder absolvierst ein Pflicht-/freiwilliges Praktikum – idealerweise für mindestens 4–6 Monate, Vollzeit

  • Standort München oder Bereitschaft, für die Dauer des Praktikums von hier aus zu arbeiten

Wie du arbeitest

  • Umsetzung & Ownership: Du bringst Dinge zu Ende, ohne dass jemand nachfassen muss. Was du übernimmst, landet nicht im Nirgendwo.

  • Systems Thinker: Du siehst nicht die einzelne Aufgabe, sondern das System dahinter. Statt zehnmal dasselbe manuell zu machen, baust du beim zweiten Mal den Prozess, der es überflüssig macht — und dokumentierst ihn so, dass ihn auch die nächste Person versteht.

  • Struktur im Chaos: Du schaffst Klarheit in unübersichtlichen Situationen – ob durch eine saubere Notion-Seite, einen organisierten Hiring-Funnel oder ein aufgeräumtes Produkt-Setup.

  • Sorgfalt bei sensiblen Themen: Datenschutz und Dokumentation sind für dich kein lästiges Beiwerk – du arbeitest hier genau und zuverlässig.

Persönlicher Hintergrund

  • DISC-Profil: Du bist extrovertiert und findest eine gute Balance zwischen People- und Task-Fokus

  • Persönliche Eigenschaften: Du bist leidenschaftlich, neugierig, wettbewerbsorientiert und lernbereit / gut coachbar

  • Du hast bereits selbst KI-Automatisierungen oder kleine Tools gebaut (z. B. mit Lovable, n8n, Zapier)

  • Du hast schon in einem schnell wachsenden Startup gearbeitet

Wenn du dich nicht in jedem Punkt wiederfindest, aber überzeugt bist, dass du gut zu alago passt, bewirb dich trotzdem. Entscheidend sind dein Potenzial und deine Lernkurve.

Warum alago?

Die meisten Praktika sind Zuarbeit. Dieses hier ist eine Abkürzung: Du sitzt sechs Monate im Maschinenraum eines Startups, das gerade von elf auf dreißig Leute wächst — und nimmst mit, wofür andere Jahre brauchen.

  1. Du hast ein Hiring von A bis Z begleitet und weißt, wie man gute Leute findet, bewertet und gewinnt.

  2. Du hast interne Systeme selbst gebaut – Automatisierungen, KI-Workflows, Prozesse – und nicht nur bedient.

Am Ende hast du keine Liste von Aufgaben im Lebenslauf, sondern Ergebnisse mit deinem Namen dran: Prozesse, die laufen, Leute, die du mit eingestellt hast, Automatisierungen, die noch nach dir funktionieren. Genau das ist die Währung, mit der du danach verhandelst.

  1. Eigene Gründung – Du hast aus nächster Nähe gesehen, wie man eine Firma baut: Fundraising, erste Kunden, erste Hires, die Fehler inklusive. Du startest nicht bei null, sondern mit einem inneren Playbook — und mit Zugang zu den Foundern, Coaches und VCs, die dir das ehrlich spiegeln.

title: Senior Infrastructure Engineer
description:
Senior Infrastructure Engineer

Remote (UK-based), with occasional on-site work at our data centres | Full-Time

About Us

Reactive Markets is the 2026 OTC Trading Platform of the Year (Risk.net). Our network handles over $75 billion in daily trading volumes across FX, Equities, and Cryptocurrency, connecting 50+ of the world’s leading liquidity providers.

We build trading systems that operate at the edge of what’s technically possible — where nanoseconds matter and a dropped message costs real money. Our engineering team is small, senior, and deeply invested in the craft of building cutting edge, reliable, high-performance systems.

The Role

We’re looking for a Senior Infrastructure Engineer to help run and grow the network and cloud estate behind our trading platform. Networking in our colocation data centres is the core of the role. The estate spans London, New York and Singapore, and from Q1 2027 a new Tokyo data centre.

This is a hands-on role in a small, expert infrastructure team. You’ll work closely with our Head of Infrastructure, following problems from the cross-connect through hosts, containers and AWS. You’ll also help keep infrastructure delivery on track, from timelines and reporting to working closely with our TechOps team.

What You’ll Work On

  • Low-latency networking across our colocation sites: switching and routing, cross-connects, BGP peering with liquidity providers and clients, and the fabric that carries our trading traffic

  • Bringing new sites to application-ready, starting with Tokyo

  • Our hybrid connectivity into multi-region AWS, including Direct Connect, routing and failover

  • Linux hosts and containers on the critical path, with every change made through code (Ansible, Git, Terraform), never by hand

  • Monitoring and alerting that catches problems before clients do, plus runbooks and post-incident reviews that someone else can follow

  • Planning and capacity: forecasting growth, setting timelines and reporting progress to TechOps and engineering

What We Need

  • 4+ years running production infrastructure in a latency-sensitive environment, such as HFT, an exchange, market data or bank trading infrastructure

  • Strong networking: hands-on routing and switching (MLAG, LACP, VLANs), BGP in production, and a solid grasp of low-latency behaviour such as buffers, microbursts and congestion handling

  • Colocation experience: cabinets, cross-connects, remote hands and vendor management

  • Solid Linux (RHEL) and TCP/IP, and the ability to trace a problem from the wire to the application

  • Infrastructure as code and containers as your default way of working

  • Working knowledge of AWS networking, and the confidence to pick up the rest of our stack. Networking depth matters more to us than any particular cloud or platform tooling

  • Methodical, evidence-led troubleshooting and clear documentation

A strong plus:

  • Project management experience: owning timelines, reporting progress, and working with ops teams to hit deadlines

  • Kernel bypass (Onload/ef_vi), PTP and time synchronisation

  • Experience bringing up a new colo site

  • FIX protocol or OTC FX market knowledge

  • Python for tooling

Working pattern: Infrastructure changes are often scheduled outside trading hours, including weekends, and the team shares an on-call rota. We’re a team with flexible hours, so time worked out of hours is taken back during the week. Day-to-day work is remote, with occasional visits to our data centres, most often in London (Slough).

What You Get

  • Real ownership of a live global trading network, hands-on, with few layers of process

  • A build-out year, with a new Tokyo data centre in Q1 and more growth ahead

  • A senior seat in a small, expert team where your changes ship and are measured

  • Competitive package — up to 38 days leave (inc. bank holidays), private health insurance, pension, life insurance, dental/optical cashback, cycle to work, socials and offsites

  • Remote-friendly working with flexibility around out-of-hours work

  • Growth as the estate scales

We believe in transparency, honest feedback and writing things down, and we aim to build systems that don’t depend on the heroics of individuals.

Cyber Security Engineer - Governance Risk & Compliance (GRC) - UK Remote

Immersive is hiring! Could you be our next Cyber Security Engineer?

Due to customer demand and increasing maturity within our platform we have an exciting and challenging opportunity for an experienced cyber professional within the cyber compliance sector - with expertise in conducting governance risk and compliance audits - to join our Product team as Cyber Security Engineer, specialising in Governance, Risk & Compliance (GRC).

If successful you will join our Product team working closely with our Cyber Team Leads as we embark on this exciting new phase of product development within our market leading cyber resilience platform.

This isn’t an ordinary GRC role - we know everyone claims this and will tell you their role is super unique…but this one really is.

You are constantly researching, learning, totally geeking out on all things GRC related, from ISO standards, to the latest AI governance, and then taking that knowledge and creating labs and ranges.

You will be a key player in our Cyber team, shaping and influencing the roll out of our offensive security and AI pen test content roadmap, simulating attack paths and helping train our users to counter the latest threats.

You will be educating the world of GRC professionals on how to make sure they are secure in what they do. Now that is a pretty cool legacy to leave behind.

Your mission (if you choose to accept it) is to evolve and disrupt within the governance space by creating emulated environments within our platform that will simulate incidents within highly regulated sectors in an engaging and intuitive way for our community.

You will design, build and deliver practical and theory content to gamify governance, risk and compliance and make it engaging and fun for the end user. You'll shake up traditional training and teach complex concepts in an innovative way.

If you have a passion for cyber security, are experienced in the area of GRC, and want to disrupt how employees build their resilience against the latest threats we will appreciate your input and give you the space to innovate within our market leading platform, Immersive One.

  • Deep understanding of common compliance frameworks and security standards (e.g., NIST SP 800-53, NIST CSF, ISO 27001/27002, SOC 2).

  • Have a strong technical understanding of networking, computing and cyber security concepts

  • Have the ability to use examples and analogies to simplify complex subjects - your content will train real world users to identify and combat the latest threats so you need to be able to inhabit the mindset of your target audience to create realistic simulations

  • Certifications such as CISSP, CISA, CRISC, CISM would be useful to have but not essential

We encourage people of all different backgrounds and identities to apply. We are committed to maintaining an inclusive, supportive place for you to be you and do your very best work. Excited by the above? We’re ready to receive your application!

title: Installation Support Coordinator
description:
Bij DeWarmte maken we slimme en betaalbare warmtepompen waarmee we woningen van het gas af helpen. We groeien hard en voeren steeds meer installaties uit. En hoe meer installaties we doen, hoe belangrijker het wordt dat onze installateurs snel geholpen worden als ze ergens tegenaan lopen.

Daarom zoeken we een Installation Support Coordinator.

Jij bent tijdens installaties het eerste aanspreekpunt voor onze installateurs. Je hoeft niet ieder technisch probleem zelf op te kunnen lossen. Jouw kracht zit vooral in snel begrijpen wat er speelt, bepalen wat er nodig is en zorgen dat de juiste persoon in actie komt.

Zie jezelf een beetje als de luchtverkeersleider van onze installaties: er gebeurt veel tegelijk, verschillende vragen hebben verschillende prioriteiten en jij houdt het overzicht.

Wat ga je doen?

Installateurs kunnen tijdens hun werk tegen allerlei vragen aanlopen. Soms kun je die zelf direct beantwoorden. Soms heb je werkvoorbereiding, engineering, service of een andere collega nodig. Jij zorgt dat de installateur zo snel mogelijk verder kan.

Concreet betekent dat dat je:

  • het eerste aanspreekpunt bent voor installateurs met vragen tijdens een installatie;

  • snel uitzoekt wat er precies aan de hand is en hoe urgent het is;

  • eenvoudige vragen zelf oplost;

  • bepaalt wie er nodig is als je de vraag niet zelf kunt beantwoorden;

  • zorgt voor een duidelijke overdracht naar de juiste collega;

  • urgente vragen actief blijft volgen totdat er een oplossing is;

  • installateurs op de hoogte houdt van de voortgang;

  • supportvragen en oplossingen goed registreert;

  • terugkerende problemen signaleert en bespreekt met de betrokken teams;

  • helpt om werkinstructies en veelvoorkomende oplossingen beter vast te leggen.

Je werkt daarbij veel samen met onder andere werkvoorbereiding, engineering, service en onze commerciële teams.

Wat maakt jou goed in deze rol?

Voor deze functie zoeken we niet per se iemand met jarenlange technische ervaring. Veel belangrijker is dat je snel kunt schakelen en goed overzicht houdt.

Je krijgt gedurende de dag verschillende vragen op je af. Jij kunt bepalen wat nú moet worden opgelost, wat kan wachten en wie je waarvoor nodig hebt. En als je iets bij een collega neerlegt, blijf je betrokken totdat duidelijk is hoe de installateur verder kan.

We denken dat je goed bij deze rol past als je:

  • energie krijgt van regelen, coördineren en problemen oplossen;

  • rustig blijft als er meerdere dingen tegelijk spelen;

  • snel hoofd- van bijzaken kunt onderscheiden;

  • makkelijk contact legt met verschillende soorten collega's;

  • duidelijk en praktisch communiceert;

  • verantwoordelijkheid neemt en dingen niet zomaar over de schutting gooit;

  • gestructureerd werkt en openstaande acties goed bijhoudt;

  • nieuwsgierig bent en graag wilt begrijpen hoe dingen werken;

  • goed Nederlands spreekt.

Ongeveer 1 tot 2 jaar werkervaring is mooi meegenomen, bijvoorbeeld in een operationele of coördinerende functie. Technische kennis van warmtepompen is geen vereiste. We kunnen je leren hoe onze producten en installaties werken. Belangrijker is dat jij snel leert en ervoor zorgt dat een vraag bij de juiste persoon terechtkomt.

Hoe ziet succes eruit?

Het belangrijkste is dat onze installateurs snel en goed geholpen worden en zo min mogelijk stil komen te staan doordat ze op een antwoord wachten.

Daarbij kijken we bijvoorbeeld naar hoe snel supportvragen worden opgepakt, of je de juiste prioriteiten stelt, of vragen bij de juiste collega's terechtkomen en hoe goed je openstaande vragen opvolgt.

Maar we willen ook steeds beter worden. Als jij merkt dat dezelfde vraag iedere week terugkomt, verwachten we niet dat je hem alleen iedere week opnieuw beantwoordt. Je zoekt samen met het team uit hoe we het probleem structureel kunnen oplossen.

Daar ligt voor jou veel ruimte om de rol verder uit te bouwen. Je helpt niet alleen individuele installateurs, maar kijkt ook naar de hele inbound support flow: hoe komen vragen binnen, hoe bepalen we de prioriteit, wie pakt wat op, hoe houden we overzicht en hoe zorgen we dat kennis niet verloren gaat?

Wat bieden we?

  • Een salaris tussen €3.000 en €4.000 bruto per maand op basis van 40 uur.

  • Een werkdag van 08:00 tot 16:30 uur.

  • Een werkplek op ons kantoor in Den Haag.

  • Veel verantwoordelijkheid en vrijheid om je werk goed in te richten.

  • De kans om veel te leren over warmtepompen en installatietechniek.

  • Lunch op kantoor.

  • Laptop en telefoon.

  • Regelmatige teamactiviteiten, van borrels tot onze jaarlijkse winter trip.

  • De mogelijkheid om mee te groeien met een bedrijf dat nog volop in ontwikkeling is.

Je komt terecht in een omgeving waar we snel schakelen, elkaar helpen en niet wachten tot iemand anders een probleem oplost. Zie je iets dat beter kan? Dan horen we dat graag. En nog liever zien we dat je helpt om het ook daadwerkelijk beter te maken.

title: Customer Experience Manager
description:
Over DeWarmte

Wij zijn DeWarmte. Wij maken het makkelijk om afscheid te nemen van gas voor verwarming en warm water. Dat doen we met slimme, design warmte-oplossingen én met een customer journey die het voor onze klanten van begin tot eind makkelijk maakt.

We groeien snel. Steeds meer klantgroepen kiezen voor DeWarmte en dat betekent dat ook onze customer journey steeds groter en complexer wordt. Van het eerste contact met Sales tot planning, installatie, onboarding, service en onderhoud: op ieder moment willen we het voor onze klanten zo makkelijk mogelijk maken om van het gas af te gaan. Dat betekent goed advies, duidelijke communicatie, ondersteuning en aandacht bij elke stap.

Jouw bijdrage aan onze missie

Als Customer Experience Manager ben je verantwoordelijk voor de kwaliteit en consistentie van de totale customer experience. Van digitale tot persoonlijke interacties: jij bewaakt de kwaliteit van alle processen die onze customer journey direct raken. Daarom zoeken we iemand die over de hele organisatie heen kijkt, ontdekt waar het beter kan en ervoor zorgt dat verbeteringen ook daadwerkelijk worden gerealiseerd.

Jij bent binnen DeWarmte de functionele eigenaar van Customer Experience. Je bepaalt samen met de organisatie wat onze CX-standaard is, brengt systematisch in kaart waar we daar niet aan voldoen en zorgt dat de belangrijkste verbeteringen daadwerkelijk worden gerealiseerd. Je werkt hiervoor dwars door Marketing, Sales, Operations, Installation, Support & Service en Software heen.

Je hoeft daarbij niet ieder project zelf uit te voeren. Een verbetering kan bij jou liggen, bij een ‘Head of’ of bij iemand anders in de organisatie. Wat wél bij jou blijft liggen, is de accountability voor het realiseren van de verbetering: je zorgt voor een duidelijke eigenaar, doelstelling, deadlines en een kwaliteitsstandaard. Daarnaast bewaak je de voortgang en het resultaat. Je rapporteert rechtstreeks aan de CEO. Vanuit die positie werk je organisatiebreed en krijg je het mandaat om CX-verbeteringen over teams heen aan te jagen. Cross-functionele verbeterprojecten die over meerdere teams heen lopen, leid je in principe zelf.

Dat vraagt senioriteit. Je moet een Head kunnen challengen wanneer de customer experience niet goed genoeg is, maar net zo makkelijk zelf een review beantwoorden, een geautomatiseerde e-mail herschrijven of een (kleiner) verbeterproject van A tot Z uitvoeren.

 

Wat ga je doen?

  • Je beheert en verbetert onze bestaande customer journey en bijbehorende process maps en gebruikt deze om continu te identificeren waar de customer experience beter kan.

  • Je ontwikkelt samen met de verschillende teams onze CX-standaarden voor de belangrijkste customer touchpoints, bewaakt deze en spreekt teams erop aan wanneer de ervaring daar niet aan voldoet.

  • Je gebruikt reviews, klachten, customer feedback en operationele data om structurele problemen en verbeterkansen te identificeren en te prioriteren.

  • Je vertaalt deze inzichten naar een duidelijke, geprioriteerde CX-improvement roadmap.

  • Je initieert verbeterprojecten binnen Marketing, Sales, Operations, Installation, Support & Service, Software en andere teams en zorgt voor een duidelijke eigenaar, doelstelling, deadlines en kwaliteitsstandaard.

  • Je bewaakt de voortgang en het resultaat van deze verbeterprojecten en zorgt dat afgesproken verbeteringen daadwerkelijk worden gerealiseerd.

  • Cross-functionele CX-projecten die over meerdere teams heen lopen, leid je in principe zelf van analyse tot implementatie.

  • Je meet na implementatie of verbeteringen daadwerkelijk het gewenste effect op de customer experience hebben gehad.

  • Je bent verantwoordelijk voor onze aanpak rondom Google Reviews en Trustpilot: je zorgt dat reviews snel en goed worden beantwoord, dat problemen bij de juiste eigenaar terechtkomen en dat noodzakelijke opvolging snel plaatsvindt.

Hoe ziet succes eruit?

Makkelijk van het gas af. Dat moet de ervaring van onze klanten zijn gedurende de hele customer journey. Na de belangrijkste onderdelen van deze journey vragen we onze klanten actief om feedback. De scores op deze customer feedback vormen belangrijke KPI’s voor deze rol en laten zien waar de ervaring goed is en waar deze beter moet.

Onze Google- en Trustpilot-scores zijn belangrijke overkoepelende KPI’s voor de totale customer experience. Het doel is daarbij niet alleen om scores te verbeteren, maar vooral om de onderliggende customer experience structureel beter te maken.

Daarom kijken we ook naar hoe snel en goed customer feedback en reviews worden opgevolgd, hoeveel structurele customer pain points we oplossen en hoe snel en met welke kwaliteit de belangrijkste CX-improvement projecten worden gerealiseerd.

 

Wie zoeken we?

We zoeken iemand die continu ziet hoe het beter kan en vervolgens zorgt dat het ook beter wordt. Je combineert een hoge kwaliteitsstandaard en sterk analytisch vermogen met executiekracht. Je kunt diep de details induiken, maar ook bepalen waar de grootste impact ligt en op senior niveau door de hele organisatie verbeteringen realiseren.

Je hebt:

  • Meerdere jaren relevante ervaring binnen customer experience, customer operations, customer journey management, process improvement, projectmanagement of een vergelijkbare rol. Wat je aantoonbaar hebt gerealiseerd vinden we daarbij belangrijker dan je functietitel.

  • Ervaring met het verbeteren van customer journeys en processen, bij voorkeur in een snelgroeiende B2C-omgeving met een complexe operationele customer journey.

  • Aantoonbare ervaring met het omzetten van customer feedback en data naar concrete verbeteringen.

  • Een sterk analytisch vermogen: je kunt individuele klachten onderscheiden van structurele problemen, komt tot de root cause en weet waar je de meeste impact kunt maken.

  • Een uitzonderlijk oog voor detail en een hoge kwaliteitsstandaard. Je ziet inconsistenties, spelfouten, onduidelijke communicatie en afwijkingen van onze branding die anderen missen. Ook wanneer klanten tevreden zijn en duidelijke feedback opdroogt, blijf je zoeken naar hoe de customer experience nog beter kan.

  • Sterke projectmanagementvaardigheden. Je brengt structuur aan, maakt ownership en deadlines expliciet en krijgt meerdere verbeterinitiatieven daadwerkelijk over de finish.

  • De senioriteit en overtuigingskracht om stakeholders op verschillende niveaus te challengen en accountable te houden, ook wanneer zij niet aan jou rapporteren.

  • Een hands-on mentaliteit. Je vindt het prima om zelf een review te beantwoorden, een process map uit te pluizen of een (kleiner) project van A tot Z uit te voeren als dat nodig is.

  • Sterke communicatieve vaardigheden in het Nederlands en Engels. Duits is een plus.

Ervaring in een scale-up, consumer tech, energy, mobility, home services of een andere omgeving met een complexe operationele customer journey is een sterke plus.

Wat wij bieden

  • Een sleutelrol waarin je direct invloed hebt op hoe duizenden klanten DeWarmte ervaren.

  • Veel verantwoordelijkheid en ownership vanaf dag één, met een organisatiebreed mandaat en een directe rapportagelijn naar de CEO.

Interesse?

title: Lead Controls & Data Engineer
description:
At DeWarmte, we develop technology that helps homes move away from gas. Our heat pumps combine hardware, embedded control software, cloud services and data—and the quality of the software connecting those elements directly determines how well our products perform in customers’ homes.


We are looking for a Lead Controls & Data Engineer to take ownership of two foundations of our products: the control software that operates our heat pumps and the data platform that helps us monitor, understand and improve them.


This is a hands-on leadership role. Initially, most of your time will be spent writing code, diagnosing real-world behaviour, improving reliability and delivering new functionality. At the same time, you are in the lead for collaborating with external partners, ensuring data reliability and scalability. Additionally, you will build the technical foundations, documentation and team that move us away from dependence on any one engineer.

Your mission

Build reliable, scalable controls and data capability that is owned by a team—not an individual.

You will inherit working systems and products already operating in the field. Your job is to understand them deeply, keep them running, improve their performance and evolve their architecture. You will then recruit and develop the engineers needed to create durable, shared ownership.

What you'll do

Own and improve our control software

  • Work directly in the production code that controls our heat pumps.

  • Design, build, test and deploy new control functionality.

  • Improve product performance, stability, safety and energy efficiency.

  • Diagnose and understand complex behaviour across software, electronics, sensors, hydraulics and the physical installation.

  • Manage controlled software rollouts across both new products and the installed fleet.

  • Establish appropriate automated testing, simulation, observability and release practices.

  • Current stack includes Bash/Shell, Python, Kafka, Telegraf and Influx. You will own the evolution of the stack together with our Hardware R&D team.


Build our product data platform

  • Take technical ownership of the systems that collect, process and expose data from our connected smart heat pumps.

  • Make product behaviour and fleet trends observable for engineering, service and product teams.

  • Improve the quality, reliability and accessibility of operational data.

  • Ensure pipeline and server capabilities are able to handle rapid scaling.

  • Create the foundations for performance analysis, remote diagnostics and continuous product improvement.

  • Define clear interfaces between device software, cloud systems, the customer app and internal tools.


Build a team and eliminate key-person dependency

  • Turn implicit knowledge into clear documentation, tooling and repeatable engineering practices.

  • Design systems that other engineers can intuitively understand, easily test and safely change.

  • Define the roles and capabilities the team will need as DeWarmte scales.

  • Recruit, onboard and mentor controls, embedded-software and data engineers.

  • Introduce effective code reviews, technical decision-making and shared operational ownership.

  • Gradually move from being the primary implementer to leading a capable team—without losing touch with the code.


Work across the product

You will collaborate closely with colleagues in hardware, software, data, product development, assembly, installation and service. You will help resolve immediate customer and operational issues while protecting the long-term quality of the platform.

 

What success looks like

In your first months

  • You understand the existing controls, data flows and operational risks.

  • You can independently maintain, debug and release the current systems.

  • The most important technical risks and knowledge gaps are visible and prioritised.

  • Monitoring, documentation and development practices begin to improve.


As the role develops

  • New control functionality can be delivered predictably and safely.

  • You work closely together with Hardware colleagues, developing the next generation of products

  • Product data supports faster diagnosis and better engineering decisions.

  • Critical systems are understood and maintained by more than one person.

  • A small, strong controls and data team is in place, with clear ownership and effective ways of working.

  • DeWarmte is no longer dependent on a single engineer to operate or evolve this part of the product.

What we are looking for

  • Strong hands-on software engineering experience, including ownership of production systems.

  • Experience developing control or embedded software for physical products, machines or connected devices.

  • A track record of taking functionality through design, implementation, testing, deployment and real-world operation.

  • The ability to reason across software, hardware and physical-system behaviour.

  • Experience working with telemetry, time-series data, data pipelines or connected-device platforms.

  • Strong engineering fundamentals, including version control, automated testing, CI/CD, observability and structured incident resolution.

  • The ability to create clarity in an environment where systems and processes are still developing.

  • Experience mentoring engineers and improving how a team works.

  • The ambition and ability to recruit and lead a team while remaining highly hands-on.


Experience with heat pumps, HVAC systems, safety-critical design, fleet-management systems or optimisation is valuable, but we care more about your ability to learn a complex physical product and take genuine end-to-end ownership.

How you work

  • You solve urgent problems without allowing permanent workarounds to become the architecture.

  • You explain complex technical matters clearly to people with different backgrounds.

  • You balance reliability today with the investments needed to scale tomorrow.

  • You share knowledge by default and measure success by what the team can own without you.

  • You are comfortable switching between debugging a specific installation, reviewing architecture and interviewing a future teammate.

  • You are able to maintain alignment between your own team’s development roadmap and the roadmap of other product teams.

What you will get

  • Direct influence on technology that contributes to the energy transition.

  • Ownership of software and data that sit at the heart of a real physical product.

  • The opportunity to shape both the technical platform and the team around it.

  • A role that starts deeply hands-on and grows into broader engineering leadership.

What we offer

Interested?

Heel Nederland helpen om van het gas af te gaan. Dat is waar we iedere dag aan werken.

Daar kom jij in beeld.

 

Wij maken warmte zonder gas

Je agenda zit 's ochtends al vol met mensen die zelf hebben gebeld. Ze willen weten of een warmtepomp past bij hun huis en of het uit kan.

 

Geen koude acquisitie dus. Nooit.

Dat lukt niet zonder jou als sales adviseur.

title: Staff Software Engineer, Infrastructure
description:
Staff Software Engineer, Platform & Infrastructure

The role

We are hiring a Staff Software Engineer for our Infrastructure team.

Stream runs behind apps that more than a billion people use: billions of API requests a month, a 99.999% uptime promise, and a small team keeping it all running. Infrastructure here decides how fast our products feel, how well they scale, and how quickly we can launch new ones.

This year we're wrapping up a big move. We're simplifying where and how we host, and rebuilding our data layer on self-hosted, open-source systems that are faster and cheaper to run. That's the groundwork, not the job. Next comes building the infrastructure every Stream product runs on, including the ones we haven't built yet. That means real SLOs, clear costs, calmer on-call, and a platform that helps teams ship faster.

What you build will shape how much Stream spends and how fast it grows, and we'll trust you with big decisions from your first few weeks.

This is a Software Engineering role first. Attitude, ambition and a willingness to experiment across the stack matter more to us than years of Kubernetes or database operations. We expect AI to cover a good share of the DevOps-heavy work, and we expect you to use it that way. What a tool can't give us is system design judgement, strong fundamentals and good code, so that is what we look for.

Platform & Infrastructure is a small, senior team without the support structures of a large organisation. It moves fast and it gets hectic. We would rather say that now than have you find out in month two.

 

What team is focusing on:

  • Runs Stream's global platform. Keeps the edge and backend that serve customers worldwide fast and up, at single-digit millisecond latency on a 99.999% uptime SLA.

  • Shapes Stream's margins. Our hosting and infrastructure decisions directly drive the company's profitability. You will decide where and how we run, and what we stop paying for.

  • Builds tools people actually want to use. Internal tools that change how engineers deploy and debug, and external ones that give customers a clear view of their own traffic and health.

  • Makes on-call boring. Builds a rotation people can sustain, and cuts alert noise until a page means something real is broken.

  • Makes cost visible. Gives every team a clear view of what it spends on infrastructure and why, so cost becomes part of every engineering decision.

What you will do:

  • Define what "good" looks like for the platform. Set latency and uptime SLOs for every product team, and decide what we measure, from error rates and delivery times to how healthy our customers' apps really are.

  • Make the big infrastructure calls. Lead the design reviews and decisions on where and how we run, working with backend, video and moderation engineers on tradeoffs that cross service boundaries.

  • Build the platform tooling. Write the internal tools and services that help engineers ship, deploy and debug faster, plus the docs and AI skills that make launching a new product repeatable.

  • Turn incidents into fixes that stick. Take part in on-call, and make sure every root cause ends in a durable fix, not a workaround.

  • Make cost part of every design. Weigh cost alongside reliability in every decision, and give teams the numbers to do the same.

What we are looking for:

  • A software engineer who has built systems, not only configured them. You write production code in Go, Python or a similar language. Scripting-only backgrounds are not a fit.

  • Strong system design. You can reason about failure modes, capacity and cost in distributed systems, and explain why you chose what you chose.

  • Solid fundamentals in networking, storage and concurrency, and the habit of asking why a system behaves the way it does instead of accepting the default.

  • You have owned high-scale production systems and set technical direction beyond your own work, through design reviews, RFCs and decisions other engineers build on.

  • You experiment. When you hit Kubernetes, a database or a cloud service you have not run before, you dig in, use AI to close the gap, and ship.

  • You already use AI tools every day in your engineering work.

  • You treat cost and reliability as engineering problems, and you can put a number on an outcome you drove.

  • You write clearly. Much of this role is docs and standards that other teams will follow.

  • You are comfortable in a small team, setting direction and reviewing a PR in the same week.

Nice to have experience:

  • Kubernetes in production: cluster architecture, workload design or a migration you led.

  • PostgreSQL at scale, ideally self-hosted or with CloudNativePG: sharding, replication, partitioning tradeoffs.

  • Valkey or Redis at scale, ideally on Kubernetes.

  • Hands-on AWS and GCP, including multi-cloud setups or migrations between providers.

  • Cloud commitment and reservation strategy (committed use discounts, savings plans), or formal FinOps practice.

  • SLO design, alert hygiene and a Prometheus and Grafana based observability stack.

  • Real-time systems: WebSockets, WebRTC, streaming or other persistent-connection workloads.

  • Open source contributions, or writing and talks on cloud, platform or distributed systems.

Our stack

  • Go, gRPC, RocksDB, Python

  • PostgreSQL, RabbitMQ

  • GCP

  • Grafana, Prometheus, ELK (Elasticsearch and Kibana)

  • Jaeger and Tempo for distributed tracing, Datadog

  • Redis, Memcached

  • Claude Code, Cursor

You will thrive here if

  • You want platform and infrastructure problems at a scale most engineers never touch, and the autonomy to set the direction yourself.

  • You would rather try something, measure it and change course than wait for a perfect plan.

  • You ship fast and learn fast, including when it is hectic.

  • You are self-directed and comfortable working with a globally distributed team across time zones.

You probably will not if

  • You want to stay a specialist in one layer of the stack.

  • You want tightly scoped tickets and step-by-step direction.

  • You need a calm, highly predictable environment.

Compensation and benefits

For employees based in the Netherlands:

  • 28 days paid time off plus Dutch public holidays

  • Pension plan

  • Commute covered: an NS Business Card or a company Swapfiets

  • Fitness contribution of up to €60 a month toward a gym or sports club membership

  • Learning and development budget

  • Work from anywhere: up to four weeks a year

  • Full Dutch statutory leave, with Stream topping up paternity leave to 100% pay

  • Catered team lunches in the office, and snacks

  • MacBook Pro and peripherals

  • Relocation support, visa sponsorship and 30% ruling support

  • An office in the centre of Amsterdam

  • Conferences and meetups, as an attendee or a speaker

  • The chance to work on our open source SDKs

Why join Stream?

We're a Series B company with global presence and a team of around 145 people from more than 35 countries.

We're backed by Felicis Ventures, GGV Capital, 01 Advisors, Techstars, and Arthur Ventures, with angels including Dick Costolo (ex-CEO of Twitter), Olivier Pomel (CEO of Datadog), Tom Preston-Werner (co-founder of GitHub), and Nicolas Dessaigne (co-founder of Algolia).

We'll be straight with you: a startup is more demanding than a large company. There's no fixed playbook, you'll own things end to end, and you'll sometimes pick up work outside your title. That's also what makes it a fast place to grow. If you want real ownership and high scale more than structure and a set career ladder, you'll feel at home here.

title: Backend Engineer
description:
About myTomorrows 

myTomorrows is a global health tech company dedicated to breaking down barriers for patients seeking treatment options.   

We strive to enable earlier and better treatment access by bridging the gap between those searching for possible options, and the companies who develop them. We work closely with patients, healthcare professionals, trial sites, patient advocacy groups, and BioPharma – connecting key stakeholders in the drug development ecosystem.   

We’ve developed a cutting-edge AI-powered technology platform that simplifies and streamlines access to drugs in development. To support our users and clients, we have a range of industry-expert specialized teams ready to help. Our services include clinical trial patient recruitment, Expanded Access Program management and Real-World Data collection.   

With a global footprint spanning 134 countries, to date we’ve supported over 17,000 patients, 3,000 physicians and 350 sites, earning the trust of 60+ BioPharma companies. In October 2025, we closed a €25M investment with Avego Healthcare Capital to fuel our global ambitions and scale the business.  

Join us in shaping the future of treatment access - making tomorrow’s therapies accessible for people who need them today. 

The opportunity: Backend Engineer

As a Backend Engineer, you will be responsible for developing and maintaining the platform infrastructure that powers our products. You will work closely with our Frontend Engineers, DevOps Engineers, and other stakeholders to design and build scalable, reliable, and high-performance products.

Given that most of our team is located in the Netherlands, we only consider candidates for this position who live within commuting distance to our office in Amsterdam.

What you'll do in this role:

  • Design and implement scalable and reliable backend systems and infrastructure to support our products

  • Develop and maintain our micro-services to expose platform functionality to internal and external clients

  • Collaborate with development and quality assurance teams to ensure high availability, scalability, and security of our systems

  • Collaborate with DevOps Engineers to ensure the continuous delivery and deployment of software products

  • Work with software developers to identify and implement improvements to our platform architecture and functionality

  • Develop and maintain documentation of our systems and processes

  • Mentor and train junior members of the backend team

  • Keep up-to-date with the latest trends and technologies

What you bring to the table:

  • Proficiency in Python programming language

  • 3+ years of experience in the related field

  • Experience with relational databases such as MySQL, PostgreSQL, or Oracle

  • Experience with the cloud platforms (AWS, Azure or GCP)

  • Experience with containerization technologies such as Docker and Kubernetes

  • Excellent problem-solving skills and ability to work independently and as part of a team

  • Strong communication skills and the ability to work with stakeholders across the organization

  • Excellent English communication skills 

What success in the first 6 months looks like:

  • You’ve built trust with Product, Frontend, and DevOps peers and taken clear ownership of 2-3 domain APIs/services, including stewardship of their contracts and SLAs.

  • You’ve established an API-first workflow: starting from use cases, you propose and socialize OpenAPI specs, align on naming and conventions, then implement in FastAPI with Pydantic models.

  • You’ve delivered impactful API features end-to-end (design → implementation → tests → docs) that are consumed by internal and external clients without hand-holding.

  • You’ve raised API robustness: strong request/response validation, consistent error models, pagination and idempotency where appropriate, and backward-compatible versioning enforced via automated contract tests in CI (ruff, Poetry, pre-commit).

  • You’ve improved the reliability and performance of our service by adding meaningful observability (metrics, logs, tracing) and defining SLIs/SLOs for key endpoints—reducing 5xx rates and improving p95 latency.

  • You’ve made safe database changes in MySQL with SQLAlchemy migrations, optimized critical queries, and contributed to data access patterns involving DynamoDB or Neo4j while keeping API contracts stable.

  • You’ve strengthened the security of APIs (authN/authZ boundaries, scoped tokens, least-privilege access, secrets management, rate limiting) and documented the approach.

  • You’ve written clear API documentation and examples (e.g., snippets/collections), shared knowledge with the team, and mentored junior engineers so others can build on your work.

Current tech stack:

We are fully cloud-native, leveraging AWS and adopting a Lean, API-first product development approach driven by modern cloud technologies and thoughtful design practices.

Our backend applications are built using Python, FastAPI, Pydantic, and SQLAlchemy (MySQL). On the front end, we predominantly develop with Angular and also utilize Headless Wagtail and WordPress for select products. To ensure code quality and a consistent release pipeline, we employ GitHub Actions for CI/CD along with tools like Renovate, ruff, Poetry, and pre-commit.

We containerize our applications using Docker and Docker Compose. Currently, we are transitioning from AWS Lambda-based deployments to Kubernetes-managed services and moving from AWS CloudFormation to Terraform for infrastructure as code. We continue to expand our capabilities in knowledge graphs (Neo4j) and database technologies (MySQL, DynamoDB).

What we offer:

  • Impactful work that helps patients gain access to potentially lifesaving treatments. 

  • International work environment, scale-up energy and a flat organizational structure that encourages creativity and accountability. 

  • Competitive salary, annual performance bonus and an Employee Stock Option Plan. 

  • Great career development opportunities in a fast-growing company.  

  • Learning and development budget alongside internal knowledge sharing sessions. 

  • Attractive pension plan, full premium covered by myTomorrows. 

  • Hybrid working model. 

  • Policies to support working parents. 

  • Healthy lunch at the thriving Amsterdam office.  

  • Unlimited access to professional guidance by certified psychologists via OpenUp  

  • Enjoy monthly events hosted by our vibrant Culture Club as well as an annual ‘myTomorrowland’ company-wide celebration! 

Equal opportunities

myTomorrows is an Equal Opportunity Employer and, beyond upholding discrimination-free practices, we are committed to cultivating a workplace where difference and diversity are protected and celebrated. The best work comes from our best selves, and we go to great lengths in supporting our team members to be just that.

The Mission

Every day, patients, physicians, and pharma companies navigate a fragmented, slow, and complex healthcare ecosystem to find pre-approval treatments. At myTomorrows, we are building the global infrastructure to solve this. Our mission is clear: to enable earlier and better access to all possible treatment options for patients who cannot afford to wait.

Operating across 134+ countries, with hubs in Amsterdam, New York, and India, we've supported over 17,000 patients and 3,000+ physicians. Avego's €25 million growth investment is our launchpad to scale the business internationally, deepen BioPharma partnerships, and build the financial architecture that a company of this complexity now requires.

As our Chief Financial Officer (CFO), based at our Amsterdam headquarters, you will be a central member of the Leadership Team and a close strategic partner to the CEO. You will not simply run a finance function. You will build the financial infrastructure, governance, and discipline that this next chapter of growth demands, across a business spanning technology, regulated healthcare services, and multiple jurisdictions.

The Challenges

As CFO, you will step into the trenches to tackle four defining challenges:

  • Leading buy-side M&A execution: You will be the primary financial architect behind our inorganic growth. As myTomorrows evaluates acquisitions and strategic partnerships to complement organic growth, you will lead deal structuring, due diligence, valuation, and integration from a buyer's seat, bringing real process discipline to a company entering its first phase of consolidation.

  • Architecting for multi-jurisdiction complexity: You will own the financial structure connecting our operations across the Netherlands, the US, and India. This means building robust transfer pricing policies, intercompany arrangements, and multi-party revenue recognition frameworks that hold up to investor and regulatory scrutiny as the business scales across borders.

  • Being a credible investor partner: You will serve as the finance function's primary interface to our Supervisory Board. You will bring investor-grade reporting rhythms, board governance discipline, and the judgment to translate operational reality into the language our sponsor and Board expect.

  • Preparing for future fundraising and exit: You will help set the company up for its next capital event, whether that is a follow-on raise, a strategic sale, or another form of exit. This means building the financial track record, audit readiness, and data room discipline that institutional buyers and investors expect, well ahead of any process actually starting.

What You Bring to the Table

Experience & Technical Depth

  • Proven CFO or strong CFO-1 experience in a high-growth, investor-backed business, ideally in healthtech, healthcare services, life sciences, or another complex international platform environment.

  • Buy-side M&A execution is a firm requirement. You have led acquisitions from the buyer's side, not only sell-side or advisory M&A, and can speak credibly to deal structuring, diligence, and post-deal integration.

  • Multi-jurisdiction financial complexity: hands-on experience with transfer pricing, intercompany structures, and multi-party revenue recognition across at least two of the following: Europe, the US, and Asia.

  • Institutional governance familiarity: direct experience with board reporting rhythms, supervisory board obligations, and the accountability that comes with a private equity or growth equity sponsor.

  • Regulated sector navigation: exposure to compliance-intensive environments, ideally in healthcare, life sciences, or another highly regulated domain.

  • Leading a lean senior team: you have led finance at this scale and know how to raise the ceiling of a small team rather than solving it with headcount.

  • Fundraising and exit experience: you have run or closely supported a capital raise, whether equity, debt, or both, and ideally have direct exposure to a sale process, IPO, or other exit event. You know what "diligence-ready" actually means in practice.

  • A Builder at Heart: You are energized by creating and scaling finance infrastructure, and you are comfortable reviewing a deal model, writing a Board memo, or rolling up your sleeves with the team when needed.

  • Commercially Astute: You connect mission to economics, balancing patient-first principles with the discipline an investor-backed business requires, and you can challenge constructively.

  • Low Ego, High Accountability: You establish clear standards, hold yourself and others to them, and proactively remove roadblocks rather than waiting for structure to be handed to you.

  • A Strategic Connector: You translate financial complexity into a clear narrative for the CEO, Supervisory Board, and cross-functional leaders, building alignment and confidence in the numbers.

The Financial Foundation Today

You will inherit a finance function with a solid FP&A core and real scope to build:

  • Led or materially advanced one or more buy-side M&A processes, demonstrating deal discipline from sourcing through integration.

  • Established a robust multi-jurisdiction financial architecture, including transfer pricing policy and intercompany structures that hold up under scrutiny.

  • Built investor-grade financial governance and greater confidence in data quality across the business.

  • Become a trusted partner to the CEO and Supervisory Board, with a reporting rhythm that meets institutional ownership expectations.

  • Helped shape a clear financial roadmap for international scale and long-term value creation.

title: Deployment Operations Manager
description:
Monumental is automating on-site construction with robotics and software. Our mission is to make construction software-defined and autonomous - a future where beautiful, bespoke buildings go up in a single day, with minimal labour.

 

We're a growing team of engineers, operators and technicians from companies like Palantir, Qualcomm, Dyson, Shopify, Tesla, Meta and Google DeepMind. It's still the early days of building the company, and this is a chance to make an outsized impact on a problem that matters. From day one, you’ll be working with an experienced founding team, backed by a $32M Series B led by Khosla Ventures and Plural.

 

Monumental is based in the city centre of Amsterdam, in a beautiful facility with an fully equipped workshop and robot testing floor. We build the whole stack in-house - hardware and software, we're explicitly not a hybrid or remote-first company - you can't build robots or walls from home, so we're onsite five days a week.

Read more on why we believe you should spend your time working on construction, and learn about our vision and company. You might enjoy our YouTube Channel, Based in Europe’s film on how we’re fixing Europe’s housing shortage, or this video by Andreas Klinger of what our office looks like.

About the role

Monumental is unique in that we’re completely vertically-integrated. We design and build our own hardware and software, we manufacture the robots in-house, and we deploy them on construction sites ourselves, with our own team, operating as a subcontractor.

We build cutting-edge technology, but we sell the old-fashioned way: by showing up, walking the site, and earning trust in person. If you’re looking for a remote-first role, this isn’t it. Onsite construction usually starts before sunrise on a site in a town you'd otherwise never visit.

Construction is one of the most chaotic industries there is, and we're deploying hardware and software into it in a way that hasn't happened before. Robots fail, contractors change the plan, and it's on you to keep the build moving forward no matter what.

We call these projects deployments. So far our operators, deployment managers and fleet of 150+ robots have laid bricks for 100+ homes, a school, a community centre, a hotel, and 150+ metres of canal wall - and we're taking on more every month as we scale from the Netherlands into the UK and US.

In practice the job is five jobs in one: site foreman, operations manager, account executive, analyst, and project manager. You make the build plan, deploy yourself with your team on site as a subcontractor, manage the contractor relationship, and take responsibility for delivering quality walls, finished on time.

The other half of the job happens back at our facility. Managing your deployment's P&L, planning the build plan for the next one, and reconsidering the operational systems to improve your margin. You own the delivery, and you own translating the friction you see on site back to our R&D team.

This is a very entrepreneurial role - you'll get an extraordinary amount of autonomy, if you've spent the last couple of years building something operationally messy - startup, scale-up, running your own company, or in a heavy industry where the plan changes routinely. What you'll do

  • Plan the logistics of a deployment: decide how many and which robots and humans to send, coordinate with other subcontractors, and build both a day-to-day operational plan and a view of how your decisions move our unit economics.

  • Spend real time on the construction site, overseeing, managing and motivating the team; liaising with the general contractors and other stakeholders; and generally representing the company and selling our story. You're comfortable speaking with the guys building scaffolds, the CEOs of the biggest general contractors, and our engineers, all on the same day.

  • Build the operational systems that make each deployment run better than the last - spotting inefficiencies, fixing processes, improving margin.

  • Own the P&L of your deployment and keep proposing ways to improve our unit economics.

  • Work with our existing customer base and drive growth of new construction projects and, in the future, adjacent product lines beyond bricklaying.

  • Support hiring and interviewing additional robot and deployment operators.

What we’re looking for

  • 2-5 years of industry experience in operations, commercial, project delivery, or running your own company. We care far more about what you've personally owned than the title above it.

  • You've worked somewhere chaotic. Startups and scale-ups, construction, logistics and last-mile delivery, e-mobility, offshore, field services - environments where plans break daily and someone has to absorb it.

  • Given the local nature of the construction industry, this role requires you to be a native Dutch speaker.

  • You're an excellent communicator and comfortable speaking with a broad range of personas.

  • You don't mind getting your hands (literally) dirty to get the job done.

  • A strong bias-to-action and getting-shit-done mentality with the required tenacity and speed. The emphasis of this role is execution, not analysis.

  • You're comfortable in a high-stress environment. Things constantly go wrong at construction sites, the stakes are high, and we're introducing new technology with novel failure modes.

  • You've led people, even informally - a crew, a shift, a small team, your own subcontractors.

  • Strong operational and analytical skills. You can build a spreadsheet with a clear operational plan, or present a P&L and model various scenarios and drivers. You're a strong project manager.

  • Raw intellectual horsepower and eagerness to learn. We expect this role to have a steep learning curve whatever your background, and it might in practice feel like a completely new job every 3-6 months. You'll learn a lot about construction, robotics, and being part of a high-growth, hard-tech company.

Why Monumental?

Joining Monumental means being at the forefront of a movement aimed at making significant strides in the construction industry. You are the first dedicated hire in FP&A, start as an Individual Contributor and work directly with the CFO and management. Our existing models and tools have grown organically and are partly manual. You understand them, keep what works, rebuild the rest and automate consistently. With AI agents, you build the leverage that elsewhere would take an entire team.

  • Build and operate agentic AI workflows for forecasting, anomaly detection, variance commentary and reporting, incl. guardrails and governance
