  • You enjoy taking ownership of a feature while collaborating closely on the broader vision and direction

  • You’re comfortable with ambiguity and zero-to-one product work

  • You naturally think beyond the happy path and account for edge cases and complete product states

  • You care about creating accessible experiences and solving the right problem, not just creating polished UI

  • You enjoy working closely with Product and Engineering throughout the design process

  • You’re comfortable using research, data, and customer feedback to guide decisions

  • You move quickly, seek feedback, and iterate based on what you learn

  • You’re curious about designing for AI

You Have Experience With

  • 2–5 years working in product design

  • Independently owning features from discovery through implementation, with support on vision and direction

  • Running user research from discovery through usability testing

  • Translating broad or ambiguous problems into clear product solutions

  • Working closely with Design, Product, and Engineering teams

  • Designing complex, accessible workflows and accounting for loading, empty, error, and permission states

  • Using qualitative and quantitative data to inform design decisions

  • Building within established design patterns while knowing when something needs to evolve

  • Using AI tools as part of your workflow and applying judgment to AI-generated output

  • A portfolio that demonstrates strong product thinking and execution, and where you can articulate the impact of your work, with data where you had access to it

Align With What We Value

At Endear, we live by five core principles. Here’s how they translate into what we’re looking for in this role:

  • Customer First: You start by understanding the people using the product, run thoughtful research, and use what you learn to shape better experiences.

  • Take Ownership: You take responsibility for your features, follow through on the details, and care about the quality of what ships.

  • Enable Autonomy: You communicate clearly, collaborate early, and give Product and Engineering the context they need to make strong decisions together.

  • Under Promise, Over Deliver: You set realistic expectations, think through the details, and deliver complete, production-ready work.

title: Senior AI Product Engineer
description:
About the company

Turning marketing into a market-domination weapon, we created a new category — the marketplace for future customers. Businesses shop for leads as they shop for products in e-commerce: you see everything about a lead before you buy — full transparency, control, and predictable outcomes. We're the #1 lead marketplace in the USA, and we're accelerating.

Role overview

We're looking for a Senior AI Product Engineer to build the AI operating layer behind our marketplace. You take a valuable but unclear business problem — improve lead quality, cut refunds, automate a manual workflow, extract intelligence from calls — and turn it into a dependable production system end-to-end: investigate, define success, design, build, deploy, and improve on real usage data. You are a one-person AI product team for high-leverage problems, not a spec-taker.

We are expanding beyond real estate into new service-business niches, and growth is powered by reusable software and automation — not proportional growth in manual work. Every system you ship either compounds into that leverage or exposes where it leaks — no in-between.

Why this role exists

Our growth is not limited by ideas or data — we already run 40K+ members, 750+ verified daily leads, and 50B data points powering AI. It's limited by how fast we can turn ambiguous, high-value problems into shipped AI systems that actually move business metrics. We need a builder who owns the complete production outcome — not a prompt tinkerer, not a researcher, not a PM who delegates the build.

Requirements:

  • Strong record of building and shipping production software end-to-end, ideally in a SaaS, marketplace, or workflow product — with real users and real revenue on the line.

  • Strong Python and/or TypeScript, plus solid backend fundamentals: APIs, databases, auth, data models, testing, and deployment.

  • Hands-on experience shipping LLM-powered functionality using model APIs, structured outputs, tool/function calling, retrieval, context engineering, and agentic workflows.

  • Production automation experience: webhooks, events, queues, schedules, retries, idempotency, monitoring, and failure recovery — not just happy-path demos.

  • Practical evaluation skills: test sets, traces, quality metrics, regression checks, feedback loops, and root-causing real production failures.

  • Daily fluency with AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or equivalent) — you review, test, refactor, and secure generated work, not ship it raw.

  • English C1+; our stakeholders, users, and business owners are US-based, and communication must be sharp and clear.

  • AI-first by default — if you are not already using AI to 3x your own output, you will be behind the rest of engineering.

  • Product ownership and strong judgment in ambiguous, fast-moving environments — you clarify goals, make tradeoffs, and connect every technical decision to a business KPI.

What You'll Be Doing:

  • Discover high-value product and operational problems by working directly with users, business owners, and internal teams, then frame clear success criteria before writing code.

  • Design and ship customer-facing AI features and internal automations across lead quality, matching, prediction, call intelligence, CRM, support, and operations.

  • Build agents and workflows that safely use tools, APIs, databases, calls, SMS, email, and other company systems — with human approval where risk requires it.

  • Create the context layer around models: instructions, retrieval, memory, structured outputs, tool definitions, permissions, and feedback loops.

  • Build reliable event-driven and scheduled automation using webhooks, queues, schedulers, retries, idempotency, audit logs, and graceful fallbacks.

  • Create evaluation datasets and automated checks that measure usefulness, accuracy, failure modes, regressions, latency, and cost — before and after release.

  • Investigate real production failures and improve the complete system, not just the prompt or the model response.

  • Turn successful solutions into reusable components and patterns that support additional iSpeedToLead niches without rebuilding from zero.

  • Own architecture, quality, security, and business outcomes — not just the pull request.

This is not for you if

  • You want a prompt-only role or a research position focused on training foundation models.

  • You do no-code-only automation and can't own real production code.

  • You call yourself a product manager who delegates the build.

  • You ship unreviewed "vibe coding" and call it done.

  • You need a complete spec before you can start.

  • You optimize for demo quality instead of measurable business impact.

What we expect from you (first 3 months)

We don't do long onboarding: access on day one, context in days, first shipped improvement in the first 30.

  • Days 1–30 — Understand and ship: you have learned the product, data, and workflows, identified the best first problem with evidence, and released one useful, low-risk improvement in production.

  • Days 31–60 — Own the workflow: you have launched one meaningful AI product or automation with evaluation, monitoring, clear ownership, and a human fallback — running against real marketplace volume.

  • Days 61–90 (the bar) — Prove and repeat: the system shows measurable business impact (fewer manual hours, faster verification, lower refunds, better matching, higher conversion, or shorter time from idea to production), reliability is proven, and the solution is turned into a reusable pattern for future workflows or niches.

Nice to Have:

  • Voice AI, call transcription, telephony, SMS, email, CRM, or customer-support automation experience.

  • Lead generation, marketplaces, real estate, sales technology, or marketing automation background.

  • Ranking, scoring, prediction, experimentation, or data pipeline experience.

  • Cloud deployment, Docker, CI/CD, observability, security, and handling sensitive customer data.

  • MCP, vector search, LangGraph or equivalent orchestration, Temporal, n8n, or custom workflow engines.

  • Track record taking a product or automation from zero to one in a fast-moving startup.

What We Offer:

  • Impact: Own visible, high-value problems with direct access to decision-makers, users, and production feedback at the core of a product-led, AI-powered marketplace.

  • Autonomy: High ownership, low bureaucracy, and real authority to choose tools based on results and define the reusable AI architecture for multiple future niches.

  • Flexibility: Remote-first culture with flexible hours and async-friendly communication. 4+ hour overlap with Asia/Dubai required for weekly reviews.

  • Compensation: Competitive fixed base salary above the market average.

  • Team: Join a smart, passionate team that moves fast, supports each other, and builds cool stuff.

  • Time Off: 15 paid vacation days plus 5 paid sick days annually.

  • Growth: Unlimited learning policy — paid courses, books, and growth resources.

  • AI-Heavy Environment: AI is deeply embedded across prospecting, research, engineering, and workflows.

  • Ownership: Real decision-making power and direct ownership of your outcomes.

Location: Remote, 4+ hour overlap with Asia/Dubai

title: Senior Financial Operations Specialist
description:
Ecochain is a fast-growing, purpose-driven B2B SaaS scale-up on a mission to make sustainability data accessible for 100M products by 2035. We build LCA (Life Cycle Assessment) automation platforms—Mobius and Helix—that help Industrial Manufacturers quantify, share, and reduce their environmental footprint with speed and scale.

Founded in 2011 in the Netherlands, we're now a team of 50+ professionals serving Construction Products and Industrial Equipment manufacturers across Benelux, DACH, and beyond. Our customers trust us to turn complex impact data into actionable insights, enabling them to meet compliance requirements (CPR, EPBD, ESPR) and build more sustainable products.

Our Values:

  • We Care – We support our teammates, customers, and the planet

  • We Share – We grow stronger by sharing knowledge, feedback, and success

  • We Empower – We create space for people to lead, learn, and make a difference

The Role

As our Senior Financial Operations Specialist, you'll own the operational backbone of our financial administration—accounts receivable, the vendor invoice pipeline, and a clean, on-time month-end close. Reporting directly to our Financial Controller, you won't be assisting someone else's process. You'll own a domain outright, and your Controller will review your work rather than rebuild it.

This is a deliberately designed 24-hour role. Not a full-time job squeezed into part-time pay, and not a stopgap—a permanent, well-organised position for someone who wants to do one thing properly rather than five things partially.

What You'll Do

  • Own accounts receivable end-to-end—customer billing, contract invoicing, credit management, and the AR aging overview.

  • Run collections independently, following up past-due balances with a friendly, professional approach and resolving billing queries yourself.

  • Manage the accounts payable pipeline—intake, approval routing, and submission of vendor invoices to our external accountant.

  • Prepare weekly payment batches for approval, maintaining continuous oversight of what's unpaid.

  • Code invoices accurately to the correct general ledger accounts and cost centres.

  • Prepare routine monthly journal entries (accruals and revenue allocations) and perform balance-sheet reconciliations.

  • Review P&L cost and revenue lines to verify correct period allocation.

  • Keep the administration audit-ready as a matter of course, and support the Financial Controller on ad-hoc projects and process improvements.

  • Reports to: Financial Controller

  • Team: Finance (working closely with our external accountant, Customer Success, and Sales)

  • Hours: 24 per week—three full days, or spread across four or five. You choose the pattern.

What We Offer

Compensation & Benefits

  • Competitive Salary: Gross full-time salary of €3,500 – €4,500 per month depending on experience (based on 40 hours, pro-rated to 24 hours), plus 8% holiday allowance (vakantiegeld)

  • Secondary benefits: Pension contribution, phone allowance, sports allowance

  • Free lunch options in our Amsterdam-area office

  • 100% public transport reimbursement or €0.25/km for own vehicle

Purpose & Impact

  • Mission-driven work: Enable 100M products to share sustainability data by 2035

  • Real-world impact: Clean, well-run administration is what frees up capacity for the mission-driven work everyone else here is doing. Cash collected on time is cash that funds the next release

  • B Corp employer: We're measured on our impact, not just our margins

Growth & Development

  • Scale-up phase: We're growing—be part of the journey

  • High ownership: Influence how our financial processes are designed, not just how they're executed

  • Career path: Grow through scope—ownership of the close calendar, the AP approval design, supplier terms. If the role outgrows 24 hours, we'll have that conversation honestly

  • Learning culture: Product training, cross-functional exposure, and sustainability context you won't get in a traditional finance department

Work-Life Integration

  • Genuinely flexible hours: 24 per week, structured around your life. We plan around your pattern, not the other way around

  • Hybrid working: Office presence during close week, otherwise your call

  • Protected time: When you're off, you're off. You are not expected to monitor emails, Slack, or check in on days you aren't working

  • Trust-based culture: High autonomy with clear accountability and support

  • Inclusive team: International team of 50+ colleagues who live our values (We Care, We Share, We Empower)

How to Apply

Submit your application including your Resume/CV and a Cover Letter. We read the cover letter first, and we'd love for you to answer three quick questions directly:

  1. The full cycle you've owned: Walk us from a customer signing to the accountant filing. Be specific about where your responsibility started and stopped.

  2. A balance you recovered: Tell us about a past-due balance you recovered from an unhappy customer. What did you say, and what happened to the relationship afterwards?

  3. Managing a 24-hour week: How do you organize your work across 24 hours so that routine deadlines (like month-end or payment runs) are met smoothly without urgent tasks getting stuck on days you're off?

Three short paragraphs are plenty. Specific beats polished—we'd rather read one real story than three pages of adjectives.

Interview Process

We move quickly for the right candidate:

  1. Screening Interview – Financial Controller (30 min): Culture fit, ownership experience, motivation, and how a 24-hour week fits your life.

  2. Working Interview – Financial Controller (90 min): A live case using real, anonymised material from our own administration, plus a short take-home assignment (capped at 3 hours, and paid).

  3. Final Interview – CEO (30 min): Vision alignment, long-term commitment.


What We're Looking For

Must-Haves:

  • Full-cycle ownership: Proven track record in bookkeeping, financial administration, or financial operations where you've owned a complete financial administration alongside an external accountant.

  • Accounting know-how: Solid understanding of general ledger mechanics, double-entry bookkeeping, accruals, and reconciliations.

  • Collections capability: You chase money by picking up the phone, and you keep the relationship intact while you do it.

  • Tech-savvy: Comfortable with cloud accounting platforms (e.g. Exact, AFAS, NetSuite) and Excel.

  • Languages: Fluent in English and Dutch, written and spoken—including phoning a customer about money in either.

  • Self-starter mentality: You manage your own schedule and follow up on details independently.

Strong Preferences:

  • Scale-up or SaaS experience—particularly recurring billing (proration, mid-term upgrades, monthly-to-annual conversions)

  • Experience working alongside an external accountant rather than inside a large finance department

  • Company size of roughly 30–150 people—big enough for real volume, small enough that you owned it

  • B2B invoicing to international customers across multiple countries and currencies

  • Dutch professional qualifications (PDB, MBA Moderne Bedrijfsadministratie, MBO/HBO bedrijfsadministratie)

  • Having been through an audit or due-diligence process from the administration side

Who Will Thrive in This Role?

YOU'RE A GREAT FIT IF:

  • You've owned a complete financial administration and can describe exactly where your responsibility started and stopped

  • You take genuine pride in clean accounts—being audit-ready is just how you work, not a project you run in January

  • You treat collections as a relationship job with a number attached, not as sending reminders

  • You're clear and outcome-focused: you appreciate having simple, transparent goals so you always know what success looks like

  • You want a permanent, well-organised 24-hour role that fits your life, and you're not looking to grow out of it next year

  • You'd rather fix the cause of a recurring problem than get faster at handling it

  • You're willing to tell a colleague—including a senior one—that a number or a contract term is wrong

YOU'RE NOT A FIT IF:

  • You've only ever been one specialist inside a large finance department—this role has nobody to hand work to

  • You need fully remote work (we need you in the Amsterdam office during close week)

  • You want to move into controlling or FP&A within a year—this is a permanent operations role and that ambition will frustrate you

  • You're looking for a bonus—there isn't one here, deliberately

  • You expect a full-time workload to be squeezed into 24 hours, or you expect 24 hours to mean 32
